units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the Tent of Meeting, on the first day of the second month, in the second year after they had come out of the land of Egypt, saying,
units.rightText: On the first day of the second month of the second year after the Israelites had come out of the land of Egypt, the LORD spoke to Moses in the Tent of Meeting in the Wilderness of Sinai. He said:
leftNotes: 1:1 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).

units.leftText: “Take a census of all the congregation of the children of Israel, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, every male, one by one,
units.rightText: “Take a census of the whole congregation of Israel by their clans and families, listing every man by name, one by one.

units.leftText: from twenty years old and upward, all who are able to go out to war in Israel. You and Aaron shall count them by their divisions.
units.rightText: You and Aaron are to number those who are twenty years of age or older by their divisions— everyone who can serve in Israel’s army.

units.leftText: With you there shall be a man of every tribe, each one head of his fathers’ house.
units.rightText: And one man from each tribe, the head of each family, must be there with you. The Leaders of the Tribes

units.leftText: These are the names of the men who shall stand with you: Of Reuben: Elizur the son of Shedeur.
units.rightText: These are the names of the men who are to assist you: From the tribe of Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur;

units.leftText: Of Simeon: Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai.
units.rightText: from Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;

units.leftText: Of Judah: Nahshon the son of Amminadab.
units.rightText: from Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab;

units.leftText: Of Issachar: Nethanel the son of Zuar.
units.rightText: from Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar;

units.leftText: Of Zebulun: Eliab the son of Helon.
units.rightText: from Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon;

units.leftText: Of the children of Joseph: of Ephraim: Elishama the son of Ammihud; of Manasseh: Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur.
units.rightText: from the sons of Joseph: from Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud, and from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur;

units.leftText: Of Benjamin: Abidan the son of Gideoni.
units.rightText: from Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni;

units.leftText: Of Dan: Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai.
units.rightText: from Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai;

units.leftText: Of Asher: Pagiel the son of Ochran.
units.rightText: from Asher, Pagiel son of Ocran;

units.leftText: Of Gad: Eliasaph the son of Deuel.
units.rightText: from Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel;

units.leftText: Of Naphtali: Ahira the son of Enan.”
units.rightText: and from Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.”

units.leftText: These are those who were called of the congregation, the princes of the tribes of their fathers; they were the heads of the thousands of Israel.
units.rightText: These men were appointed from the congregation; they were the leaders of the tribes of their fathers, the heads of the clans of Israel. The Number of Every Tribe
leftNotes: 1:16 or, chiefs, or, leaders

units.leftText: Moses and Aaron took these men who are mentioned by name.
units.rightText: So Moses and Aaron took these men who had been designated by name,

units.leftText: They assembled all the congregation together on the first day of the second month; and they declared their ancestry by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, one by one.
units.rightText: and on the first day of the second month they assembled the whole congregation and recorded their ancestry by clans and families, counting one by one the names of those twenty years of age or older,

units.leftText: As the LORD commanded Moses, so he counted them in the wilderness of Sinai.
units.rightText: just as the LORD had commanded Moses. So Moses numbered them in the Wilderness of Sinai:

units.leftText: The children of Reuben, Israel’s firstborn, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, one by one, every male from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war:
units.rightText: From the sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel, according to the records of their clans and families, counting one by one the names of every male twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,

units.leftText: those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Reuben, were forty-six thousand five hundred.
units.rightText: those registered to the tribe of Reuben numbered 46,500.

units.leftText: Of the children of Simeon, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, those who were counted of it, according to the number of the names, one by one, every male from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war:
units.rightText: From the sons of Simeon, according to the records of their clans and families, counting one by one the names of every male twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,

units.leftText: those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Simeon, were fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
units.rightText: those registered to the tribe of Simeon numbered 59,300.

units.leftText: Of the children of Gad, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war:
units.rightText: From the sons of Gad, according to the records of their clans and families, counting the names of all those twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,

units.leftText: those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Gad, were forty-five thousand six hundred fifty.
units.rightText: those registered to the tribe of Gad numbered 45,650.

units.leftText: Of the children of Judah, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war:
units.rightText: From the sons of Judah, according to the records of their clans and families, counting the names of all those twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,

units.leftText: those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Judah, were seventy-four thousand six hundred.
units.rightText: those registered to the tribe of Judah numbered 74,600.

units.leftText: Of the children of Issachar, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war:
units.rightText: From the sons of Issachar, according to the records of their clans and families, counting the names of all those twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,

units.leftText: those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Issachar, were fifty-four thousand four hundred.
units.rightText: those registered to the tribe of Issachar numbered 54,400.

units.leftText: Of the children of Zebulun, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war:
units.rightText: From the sons of Zebulun, according to the records of their clans and families, counting the names of all those twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,

units.leftText: those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Zebulun, were fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
units.rightText: those registered to the tribe of Zebulun numbered 57,400.

units.leftText: Of the children of Joseph: of the children of Ephraim, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war:
units.rightText: From the sons of Joseph:

units.leftText: those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Ephraim, were forty thousand five hundred.
units.rightText: those registered to the tribe of Ephraim numbered 40,500.

units.leftText: Of the children of Manasseh, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war:
units.rightText: And from the sons of Manasseh, according to the records of their clans and families, counting the names of all those twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,

units.leftText: those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Manasseh, were thirty-two thousand two hundred.
units.rightText: those registered to the tribe of Manasseh numbered 32,200.

units.leftText: Of the children of Benjamin, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war:
units.rightText: From the sons of Benjamin, according to the records of their clans and families, counting the names of all those twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,

units.leftText: those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Benjamin, were thirty-five thousand four hundred.
units.rightText: those registered to the tribe of Benjamin numbered 35,400.

units.leftText: Of the children of Dan, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war:
units.rightText: From the sons of Dan, according to the records of their clans and families, counting the names of all those twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,

units.leftText: those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Dan, were sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
units.rightText: those registered to the tribe of Dan numbered 62,700.

units.leftText: Of the children of Asher, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war:
units.rightText: From the sons of Asher, according to the records of their clans and families, counting the names of all those twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,

units.leftText: those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Asher, were forty-one thousand five hundred.
units.rightText: those registered to the tribe of Asher numbered 41,500.

units.leftText: Of the children of Naphtali, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war:
units.rightText: From the sons of Naphtali, according to the records of their clans and families, counting the names of all those twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,

units.leftText: those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Naphtali, were fifty-three thousand four hundred.
units.rightText: those registered to the tribe of Naphtali numbered 53,400.

units.leftText: These are those who were counted, whom Moses and Aaron counted, and the twelve men who were princes of Israel, each one for his fathers’ house.
units.rightText: These were the men numbered by Moses and Aaron, with the assistance of the twelve leaders of Israel, each one representing his family.

units.leftText: So all those who were counted of the children of Israel by their fathers’ houses, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war in Israel—
units.rightText: So all the Israelites twenty years of age or older who could serve in Israel’s army were counted according to their families.

units.leftText: all those who were counted were six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty.
units.rightText: And all those counted totaled 603,550. The Exemption of the Levites

units.leftText: But the Levites after the tribe of their fathers were not counted among them.
units.rightText: The Levites, however, were not numbered along with them by the tribe of their fathers.

units.leftText: For the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: For the LORD had said to Moses:

units.leftText: “Only the tribe of Levi you shall not count, neither shall you take a census of them among the children of Israel;
units.rightText: “Do not number the tribe of Levi in the census with the other Israelites.

units.leftText: but appoint the Levites over the Tabernacle of the Testimony, and over all its furnishings, and over all that belongs to it. They shall carry the tabernacle and all its furnishings; and they shall take care of it, and shall encamp around it.
units.rightText: Instead, you are to appoint the Levites over the tabernacle of the Testimony, all its furnishings, and everything in it. They shall carry the tabernacle and all its articles, care for it, and camp around it.

units.leftText: When the tabernacle is to move, the Levites shall take it down; and when the tabernacle is to be set up, the Levites shall set it up. The stranger who comes near shall be put to death.
units.rightText: Whenever the tabernacle is to move, the Levites are to take it down, and whenever it is to be pitched, the Levites are to set it up. Any outsider who goes near it must be put to death.

units.leftText: The children of Israel shall pitch their tents, every man by his own camp, and every man by his own standard, according to their divisions.
units.rightText: The Israelites are to camp by their divisions, each man in his own camp and under his own standard.

units.leftText: But the Levites shall encamp around the Tabernacle of the Testimony, that there may be no wrath on the congregation of the children of Israel. The Levites shall be responsible for the Tabernacle of the Testimony.”
units.rightText: But the Levites are to camp around the tabernacle of the Testimony and watch over it, so that no wrath will fall on the congregation of Israel. So the Levites are responsible for the tabernacle of the Testimony.”

units.leftText: Thus the children of Israel did. According to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so they did.
units.rightText: Thus the Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron:

units.leftText: “The children of Israel shall encamp every man by his own standard, with the banners of their fathers’ houses. They shall encamp around the Tent of Meeting at a distance from it.
units.rightText: “The Israelites are to camp around the Tent of Meeting at a distance from it, each man under his standard, with the banners of his family.

units.leftText: “Those who encamp on the east side toward the sunrise shall be of the standard of the camp of Judah, according to their divisions. The prince of the children of Judah shall be Nahshon the son of Amminadab.
units.rightText: On the east side, toward the sunrise, the divisions of Judah are to camp under their standard:

units.leftText: His division, and those who were counted of them, were seventy-four thousand six hundred.
units.rightText: and his division numbers 74,600.

units.leftText: “Those who encamp next to him shall be the tribe of Issachar. The prince of the children of Issachar shall be Nethanel the son of Zuar.
units.rightText: The tribe of Issachar will camp next to it. The leader of the Issacharites is Nethanel son of Zuar,

units.leftText: His division, and those who were counted of it, were fifty-four thousand four hundred.
units.rightText: and his division numbers 54,400.

units.leftText: “The tribe of Zebulun: the prince of the children of Zebulun shall be Eliab the son of Helon.
units.rightText: Next will be the tribe of Zebulun. The leader of the Zebulunites is Eliab son of Helon,

units.leftText: His division, and those who were counted of it, were fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
units.rightText: and his division numbers 57,400.

units.leftText: “All who were counted of the camp of Judah were one hundred eighty-six thousand four hundred, according to their divisions. They shall set out first.
units.rightText: The total number of men in the divisions of the camp of Judah is 186,400; they shall set out first.

units.leftText: “On the south side shall be the standard of the camp of Reuben according to their divisions. The prince of the children of Reuben shall be Elizur the son of Shedeur.
units.rightText: On the south side, the divisions of Reuben are to camp under their standard:

units.leftText: His division, and those who were counted of it, were forty-six thousand five hundred.
units.rightText: and his division numbers 46,500.

units.leftText: “Those who encamp next to him shall be the tribe of Simeon. The prince of the children of Simeon shall be Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai.
units.rightText: The tribe of Simeon will camp next to it. The leader of the Simeonites is Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai,

units.leftText: His division, and those who were counted of them, were fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
units.rightText: and his division numbers 59,300.

units.leftText: “The tribe of Gad: the prince of the children of Gad shall be Eliasaph the son of Reuel.
units.rightText: Next will be the tribe of Gad. The leader of the Gadites is Eliasaph son of Deuel,
rightNotes: 2:14 Many MT manuscripts, SP, and Vulgate (see also Numbers 1:14|NUM 1:14*); most MT manuscripts Reuel

units.leftText: His division, and those who were counted of them, were forty-five thousand six hundred fifty.
units.rightText: and his division numbers 45,650.

units.leftText: “All who were counted of the camp of Reuben were one hundred fifty-one thousand four hundred fifty, according to their armies. They shall set out second.
units.rightText: The total number of men in the divisions of the camp of Reuben is 151,450; they shall set out second.

units.leftText: “Then the Tent of Meeting shall set out, with the camp of the Levites in the middle of the camps. As they encamp, so shall they set out, every man in his place, by their standards.
units.rightText: In the middle of the camps, the Tent of Meeting is to travel with the camp of the Levites. They are to set out in the order they encamped, each in his own place under his standard.

units.leftText: “On the west side shall be the standard of the camp of Ephraim according to their divisions. The prince of the children of Ephraim shall be Elishama the son of Ammihud.
units.rightText: On the west side, the divisions of Ephraim are to camp under their standard:

units.leftText: His division, and those who were counted of them, were forty thousand five hundred.
units.rightText: and his division numbers 40,500.

units.leftText: “Next to him shall be the tribe of Manasseh. The prince of the children of Manasseh shall be Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur.
units.rightText: The tribe of Manasseh will be next to it. The leader of the Manassites is Gamaliel son of Pedahzur,

units.leftText: His division, and those who were counted of them, were thirty-two thousand two hundred.
units.rightText: and his division numbers 32,200.

units.leftText: “The tribe of Benjamin: the prince of the children of Benjamin shall be Abidan the son of Gideoni.
units.rightText: Next will be the tribe of Benjamin. The leader of the Benjamites is Abidan son of Gideoni,

units.leftText: His army, and those who were counted of them, were thirty-five thousand four hundred.
units.rightText: and his division numbers 35,400.

units.leftText: “All who were counted of the camp of Ephraim were one hundred eight thousand one hundred, according to their divisions. They shall set out third.
units.rightText: The total number of men in the divisions of the camp of Ephraim is 108,100; they shall set out third.

units.leftText: “On the north side shall be the standard of the camp of Dan according to their divisions. The prince of the children of Dan shall be Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai.
units.rightText: On the north side, the divisions of Dan are to camp under their standard:

units.leftText: His division, and those who were counted of them, were sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
units.rightText: and his division numbers 62,700.

units.leftText: “Those who encamp next to him shall be the tribe of Asher. The prince of the children of Asher shall be Pagiel the son of Ochran.
units.rightText: The tribe of Asher will camp next to it. The leader of the Asherites is Pagiel son of Ocran,

units.leftText: His division, and those who were counted of them, were forty-one thousand five hundred.
units.rightText: and his division numbers 41,500.

units.leftText: “The tribe of Naphtali: the prince of the children of Naphtali shall be Ahira the son of Enan.
units.rightText: Next will be the tribe of Naphtali. The leader of the Naphtalites is Ahira son of Enan,

units.leftText: His division, and those who were counted of them, were fifty-three thousand four hundred.
units.rightText: and his division numbers 53,400.

units.leftText: “All who were counted of the camp of Dan were one hundred fifty-seven thousand six hundred. They shall set out last by their standards.”
units.rightText: The total number of men in the camp of Dan is 157,600; they shall set out last, under their standards.”

units.leftText: These are those who were counted of the children of Israel by their fathers’ houses. All who were counted of the camps according to their armies were six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty.
units.rightText: These are the Israelites, numbered according to their families. The total of those counted in the camps, by their divisions, was 603,550.

units.leftText: But the Levites were not counted among the children of Israel, as the LORD commanded Moses.
units.rightText: But the Levites were not counted among the other Israelites, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

units.leftText: Thus the children of Israel did. According to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so they encamped by their standards, and so they set out, everyone by their families, according to their fathers’ houses.
units.rightText: So the Israelites did everything the LORD commanded Moses; they camped under their standards in this way and set out in the same way, each man with his clan and his family.

units.leftText: Now this is the history of the generations of Aaron and Moses in the day that the LORD spoke with Moses in Mount Sinai.
units.rightText: This is the account of Aaron and Moses at the time the LORD spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.

units.leftText: These are the names of the sons of Aaron: Nadab the firstborn, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
units.rightText: These are the names of the sons of Aaron: Nadab the firstborn, then Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

units.leftText: These are the names of the sons of Aaron, the priests who were anointed, whom he consecrated to minister in the priest’s office.
units.rightText: These were Aaron’s sons, the anointed priests, who were ordained to serve as priests.

units.leftText: Nadab and Abihu died before the LORD when they offered strange fire before the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no children. Eleazar and Ithamar ministered in the priest’s office in the presence of Aaron their father.
units.rightText: Nadab and Abihu, however, died in the presence of the LORD when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD in the Wilderness of Sinai. And since they had no sons, only Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests during the lifetime of their father Aaron. The Duties of the Levites
rightNotes: 3:4 Or strange

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Bring the tribe of Levi near, and set them before Aaron the priest, that they may minister to him.
units.rightText: “Bring the tribe of Levi and present them to Aaron the priest to assist him.

units.leftText: They shall keep his requirements, and the requirements of the whole congregation before the Tent of Meeting, to do the service of the tabernacle.
units.rightText: They are to perform duties for him and for the whole congregation before the Tent of Meeting, attending to the service of the tabernacle.

units.leftText: They shall keep all the furnishings of the Tent of Meeting, and the obligations of the children of Israel, to do the service of the tabernacle.
units.rightText: They shall take care of all the furnishings of the Tent of Meeting and fulfill obligations for the Israelites by attending to the service of the tabernacle.

units.leftText: You shall give the Levites to Aaron and to his sons. They are wholly given to him on the behalf of the children of Israel.
units.rightText: Assign the Levites to Aaron and his sons; they have been given exclusively to him from among the Israelites.
rightNotes: 3:9 Most MT manuscripts; some MT manuscripts, SP, and LXX (see also Numbers 8:16|NUM 8:16*) to Me

units.leftText: You shall appoint Aaron and his sons, and they shall keep their priesthood, but the stranger who comes near shall be put to death.”
units.rightText: So you shall appoint Aaron and his sons to carry out the duties of the priesthood; but any outsider who approaches the tabernacle must be put to death.”

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: Again the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Behold, I have taken the Levites from among the children of Israel instead of all the firstborn who open the womb among the children of Israel; and the Levites shall be mine,
units.rightText: “Behold, I have taken the Levites from among the children of Israel in place of every firstborn Israelite from the womb. The Levites belong to Me,
leftNotes: 3:12 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: for all the firstborn are mine. On the day that I struck down all the firstborn in the land of Egypt I made holy to me all the firstborn in Israel, both man and animal. They shall be mine. I am the LORD.”
units.rightText: for all the firstborn are Mine. On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated to Myself all the firstborn in Israel, both man and beast. They are Mine; I am the LORD.” The Numbering of the Levites

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, saying,
units.rightText: Then the LORD spoke to Moses in the Wilderness of Sinai, saying,

units.leftText: “Count the children of Levi by their fathers’ houses, by their families. You shall count every male from a month old and upward.”
units.rightText: “Number the Levites by their families and clans. You are to count every male a month old or more.”

units.leftText: Moses counted them according to the LORD’s word, as he was commanded.
units.rightText: So Moses numbered them according to the word of the LORD, as he had been commanded.

units.leftText: These were the sons of Levi by their names: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
units.rightText: These were the sons of Levi by name: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

units.leftText: These are the names of the sons of Gershon by their families: Libni and Shimei.
units.rightText: These were the names of the sons of Gershon by their clans: Libni and Shimei.

units.leftText: The sons of Kohath by their families: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
units.rightText: The sons of Kohath by their clans were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.

units.leftText: The sons of Merari by their families: Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites according to their fathers’ houses.
units.rightText: And the sons of Merari by their clans were Mahli and Mushi. These were the clans of the Levites, according to their families. The Gershonites (Numbers 4:21–28|NUM 4:21-28*; 1 Chronicles 23:7–11|1CH 23:7-11*)

units.leftText: Of Gershon was the family of the Libnites, and the family of the Shimeites. These are the families of the Gershonites.
units.rightText: From Gershon came the Libnite clan and the Shimeite clan; these were the Gershonite clans.

units.leftText: Those who were counted of them, according to the number of all the males from a month old and upward, even those who were counted of them were seven thousand five hundred.
units.rightText: The number of all the males a month old or more was 7,500.

units.leftText: The families of the Gershonites shall encamp behind the tabernacle westward.
units.rightText: The Gershonite clans were to camp on the west, behind the tabernacle,

units.leftText: Eliasaph the son of Lael shall be the prince of the fathers’ house of the Gershonites.
units.rightText: and the leader of the families of the Gershonites was Eliasaph son of Lael.

units.leftText: The duty of the sons of Gershon in the Tent of Meeting shall be the tabernacle, the tent, its covering, the screen for the door of the Tent of Meeting,
units.rightText: The duties of the Gershonites at the Tent of Meeting were the tabernacle and tent, its covering, the curtain for the entrance to the Tent of Meeting,

units.leftText: the hangings of the court, the screen for the door of the court which is by the tabernacle and around the altar, and its cords for all of its service.
units.rightText: the curtains of the courtyard, the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard that surrounds the tabernacle and altar, and the cords— all the service for these items. The Kohathites (Numbers 4:1–20|NUM 4:1-20*; 1 Chronicles 23:12–20|1CH 23:12-20*)

units.leftText: Of Kohath was the family of the Amramites, the family of the Izharites, the family of the Hebronites, and the family of the Uzzielites. These are the families of the Kohathites.
units.rightText: From Kohath came the clans of the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites; these were the clans of the Kohathites.

units.leftText: According to the number of all the males from a month old and upward, there were eight thousand six hundred keeping the requirements of the sanctuary.
units.rightText: The number of all the males a month old or more was 8,600. They were responsible for the duties of the sanctuary.
rightNotes: 3:28 Hebrew; some LXX manuscripts 8,300; see the total in verse 39.

units.leftText: The families of the sons of Kohath shall encamp on the south side of the tabernacle.
units.rightText: The clans of the Kohathites were to camp on the south side of the tabernacle,

units.leftText: The prince of the fathers’ house of the families of the Kohathites shall be Elizaphan the son of Uzziel.
units.rightText: and the leader of the families of the Kohathites was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
rightNotes: 3:30 Elizaphan is a variant of Elzaphan; see Exodus 6:22|EXO 6:22* and Leviticus 10:4.

units.leftText: Their duty shall be the ark, the table, the lamp stand, the altars, the vessels of the sanctuary with which they minister, the screen, and all its service.
units.rightText: Their duties were the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the articles of the sanctuary used with them, and the curtain— all the service for these items.

units.leftText: Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest shall be prince of the princes of the Levites, with the oversight of those who keep the requirements of the sanctuary.
units.rightText: The chief of the leaders of the Levites was Eleazar son of Aaron the priest; he oversaw those responsible for the duties of the sanctuary. The Merarites (Numbers 4:29–33|NUM 4:29-33*; 1 Chronicles 23:21–23|1CH 23:21-23*)

units.leftText: Of Merari was the family of the Mahlites and the family of the Mushites. These are the families of Merari.
units.rightText: From Merari came the clans of the Mahlites and Mushites; these were the Merarite clans.

units.leftText: Those who were counted of them, according to the number of all the males from a month old and upward, were six thousand two hundred.
units.rightText: The number of all the males a month old or more was 6,200.
leftNotes: 3:34 + 22,000 is the sum rounded to 2 significant digits. The sum of the Gershonites, Kohathites, and Merarites given above is 22,300, but the traditional Hebrew text has the number rounded to 2 significant digits, not 3 significant digits.

units.leftText: The prince of the fathers’ house of the families of Merari was Zuriel the son of Abihail. They shall encamp on the north side of the tabernacle.
units.rightText: The leader of the families of the Merarites was Zuriel son of Abihail; they were to camp on the north side of the tabernacle.

units.leftText: The appointed duty of the sons of Merari shall be the tabernacle’s boards, its bars, its pillars, its sockets, all its instruments, all its service,
units.rightText: The duties assigned to the sons of Merari were the tabernacle’s frames, crossbars, posts, bases, and all its equipment— all the service for these items,

units.leftText: the pillars of the court around it, their sockets, their pins, and their cords.
units.rightText: as well as the posts of the surrounding courtyard with their bases, tent pegs, and ropes. Moses and Aaron

units.leftText: Those who encamp before the tabernacle eastward, in front of the Tent of Meeting toward the sunrise, shall be Moses, with Aaron and his sons, keeping the requirements of the sanctuary for the duty of the children of Israel. The outsider who comes near shall be put to death.
units.rightText: Moses, Aaron, and Aaron’s sons were to camp to the east of the tabernacle, toward the sunrise, before the Tent of Meeting. They were to perform the duties of the sanctuary as a service on behalf of the Israelites; but any outsider who approached the sanctuary was to be put to death.

units.leftText: All who were counted of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the commandment of the LORD, by their families, all the males from a month old and upward, were twenty-two thousand.
units.rightText: The total number of Levites that Moses and Aaron counted by their clans at the LORD’s command, including all the males a month old or more, was 22,000. The Redemption of the Firstborn

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “Count all the firstborn males of the children of Israel from a month old and upward, and take the number of their names.
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Number every firstborn male of the Israelites a month old or more, and list their names.

units.leftText: You shall take the Levites for me—I am the LORD—instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel; and the livestock of the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the livestock of the children of Israel.”
units.rightText: You are to take the Levites for Me— I am the LORD— in place of all the firstborn of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the livestock of the Israelites.”

units.leftText: Moses counted, as the LORD commanded him, all the firstborn among the children of Israel.
units.rightText: So Moses numbered all the firstborn of the Israelites, as the LORD had commanded him.

units.leftText: All the firstborn males according to the number of names from a month old and upward, of those who were counted of them, were twenty-two thousand two hundred seventy-three.
units.rightText: The total number of the firstborn males a month old or more, listed by name, was 22,273.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: Again the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Take the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites instead of their livestock; and the Levites shall be mine. I am the LORD.
units.rightText: “Take the Levites in place of all the firstborn of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock. The Levites belong to Me; I am the LORD.

units.leftText: For the redemption of the two hundred seventy-three of the firstborn of the children of Israel who exceed the number of the Levites,
units.rightText: To redeem the 273 firstborn Israelites who outnumber the Levites,

units.leftText: you shall take five shekels apiece for each one; according to the shekel of the sanctuary you shall take them (the shekel is twenty gerahs );
units.rightText: you are to collect five shekels for each one, according to the sanctuary shekel of twenty gerahs.
leftNotes: 3:47 A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces.
3:47 A gerah is about 0.5 grams or about 7.7 grains.
rightNotes: 3:47 5 shekels is approximately 2 ounces or 57 grams.
3:47 20 gerahs is equivalent to one shekel (approximately 0.4 ounces or 11.4 grams).

units.leftText: and you shall give the money, with which their remainder is redeemed, to Aaron and to his sons.”
units.rightText: Give the money to Aaron and his sons as the redemption price for the excess among the Israelites.”

units.leftText: Moses took the redemption money from those who exceeded the number of those who were redeemed by the Levites;
units.rightText: So Moses collected the redemption money from those in excess of the number redeemed by the Levites.

units.leftText: from the firstborn of the children of Israel he took the money, one thousand three hundred sixty-five shekels, according to the shekel of the sanctuary;
units.rightText: He collected the money from the firstborn of the Israelites: 1,365 shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.
leftNotes: 3:50 A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces, so 1365 shekels is about 13.65 kilograms or about 30 pounds.
rightNotes: 3:50 1,365 shekels is approximately 34.3 pounds or 15.6 kilograms.

units.leftText: and Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and to his sons, according to the LORD’s word, as the LORD commanded Moses.
units.rightText: And Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons in obedience to the word of the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded him.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,

units.leftText: “Take a census of the sons of Kohath from among the sons of Levi, by their families, by their fathers’ houses,
units.rightText: “Take a census of the Kohathites among the Levites by their clans and families,

units.leftText: from thirty years old and upward even until fifty years old, all who enter into the service to do the work in the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: men from thirty to fifty years old— everyone who is qualified to serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.

units.leftText: “This is the service of the sons of Kohath in the Tent of Meeting, regarding the most holy things.
units.rightText: This service of the Kohathites at the Tent of Meeting regards the most holy things.

units.leftText: When the camp moves forward, Aaron shall go in with his sons; and they shall take down the veil of the screen, cover the ark of the Testimony with it,
units.rightText: Whenever the camp sets out, Aaron and his sons are to go in, take down the veil of the curtain, and cover the ark of the Testimony with it.
rightNotes: 4:5 That is, the ark of the covenant

units.leftText: put a covering of sealskin on it, spread a blue cloth over it, and put in its poles.
units.rightText: They are to place over this a covering of fine leather, spread a solid blue cloth over it, and insert its poles.
rightNotes: 4:6 Possibly the hides of large aquatic mammals; also in verses 8, 10, 11, 12, 14, and 25; see Exodus 25:5|EXO 25:5*.

units.leftText: “On the table of show bread they shall spread a blue cloth, and put on it the dishes, the spoons, the bowls, and the cups with which to pour out; and the continual bread shall be on it.
units.rightText: Over the table of the Presence they are to spread a blue cloth and place the plates and cups on it, along with the bowls and pitchers for the drink offering. The regular bread offering is to remain on it.

units.leftText: They shall spread on them a scarlet cloth, and cover it with a covering of sealskin, and shall put in its poles.
units.rightText: And they shall spread a scarlet cloth over them, cover them with fine leather, and insert the poles.

units.leftText: “They shall take a blue cloth and cover the lamp stand of the light, its lamps, its snuffers, its snuff dishes, and all its oil vessels, with which they minister to it.
units.rightText: They are to take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand used for light, together with its lamps, wick trimmers, and trays, as well as the jars of oil with which to supply it.

units.leftText: They shall put it and all its vessels within a covering of sealskin, and shall put it on the frame.
units.rightText: Then they shall wrap it and all its utensils inside a covering of fine leather and put it on the carrying frame.

units.leftText: “On the golden altar they shall spread a blue cloth, and cover it with a covering of sealskin, and shall put in its poles.
units.rightText: Over the gold altar they are to spread a blue cloth, cover it with fine leather, and insert the poles.

units.leftText: “They shall take all the vessels of ministry with which they minister in the sanctuary, and put them in a blue cloth, cover them with a covering of sealskin, and shall put them on the frame.
units.rightText: They are to take all the utensils for serving in the sanctuary, place them in a blue cloth, cover them with fine leather, and put them on the carrying frame.

units.leftText: “They shall take away the ashes from the altar, and spread a purple cloth on it.
units.rightText: Then they shall remove the ashes from the bronze altar, spread a purple cloth over it,

units.leftText: They shall put on it all its vessels with which they minister about it, the fire pans, the meat hooks, the shovels, and the basins—all the vessels of the altar; and they shall spread on it a covering of sealskin, and put in its poles.
units.rightText: and place on it all the vessels used to serve there: the firepans, meat forks, shovels, and sprinkling bowls— all the equipment of the altar. They are to spread over it a covering of fine leather and insert the poles.

units.leftText: “When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the sanctuary and all the furniture of the sanctuary, as the camp moves forward; after that, the sons of Kohath shall come to carry it; but they shall not touch the sanctuary, lest they die. The sons of Kohath shall carry these things belonging to the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the holy objects and all their equipment, as soon as the camp is ready to move, the Kohathites shall come and do the carrying. But they must not touch the holy objects, or they will die. These are the transportation duties of the Kohathites regarding the Tent of Meeting.

units.leftText: “The duty of Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest shall be the oil for the light, the sweet incense, the continual meal offering, and the anointing oil, the requirements of all the tabernacle, and of all that is in it, the sanctuary, and its furnishings.”
units.rightText: Eleazar son of Aaron the priest shall oversee the oil for the light, the fragrant incense, the daily grain offering, and the anointing oil. He has oversight of the entire tabernacle and everything in it, including the holy objects and their utensils.”

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,

units.leftText: “Don’t cut off the tribe of the families of the Kohathites from among the Levites;
units.rightText: “Do not allow the Kohathite tribal clans to be cut off from among the Levites.

units.leftText: but do this to them, that they may live, and not die, when they approach the most holy things: Aaron and his sons shall go in and appoint everyone to his service and to his burden;
units.rightText: In order that they may live and not die when they come near the most holy things, do this for them: Aaron and his sons are to go in and assign each man his task and what he is to carry.

units.leftText: but they shall not go in to see the sanctuary even for a moment, lest they die.”
units.rightText: But the Kohathites are not to go in and look at the holy objects, even for a moment, or they will die.” The Duties of the Gershonites (Numbers 3:21–26|NUM 3:21-26*; 1 Chronicles 23:7–11|1CH 23:7-11*)

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: And the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Take a census of the sons of Gershon also, by their fathers’ houses, by their families;
units.rightText: “Take a census of the Gershonites as well, by their families and clans,

units.leftText: you shall count them from thirty years old and upward until fifty years old: all who enter in to wait on the service, to do the work in the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: from thirty to fifty years old, counting everyone who comes to serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.

units.leftText: “This is the service of the families of the Gershonites, in serving and in bearing burdens:
units.rightText: This is the service of the Gershonite clans regarding work and transport:

units.leftText: they shall carry the curtains of the tabernacle and the Tent of Meeting, its covering, the covering of sealskin that is on it, the screen for the door of the Tent of Meeting,
units.rightText: They are to carry the curtains of the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting with the covering of fine leather over it, the curtains for the entrance to the Tent of Meeting,

units.leftText: the hangings of the court, the screen for the door of the gate of the court which is by the tabernacle and around the altar, their cords, and all the instruments of their service, and whatever shall be done with them. They shall serve in there.
units.rightText: the curtains of the courtyard, and the curtains for the entrance at the gate of the courtyard that surrounds the tabernacle and altar, along with their ropes and all the equipment for their service. The Gershonites will do all that needs to be done with these items.

units.leftText: At the commandment of Aaron and his sons shall be all the service of the sons of the Gershonites, in all their burden and in all their service; and you shall appoint their duty to them in all their responsibilities.
units.rightText: All the service of the Gershonites — all their transport duties and other work — is to be done at the direction of Aaron and his sons; you are to assign to them all that they are responsible to carry.

units.leftText: This is the service of the families of the sons of the Gershonites in the Tent of Meeting. Their duty shall be under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest.
units.rightText: This is the service of the Gershonite clans at the Tent of Meeting, and their duties shall be under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest. The Duties of the Merarites (Numbers 3:33–37|NUM 3:33-37*; 1 Chronicles 23:21–23|1CH 23:21-23*)

units.leftText: “As for the sons of Merari, you shall count them by their families, by their fathers’ houses;
units.rightText: As for the sons of Merari, you are to number them by their clans and families,

units.leftText: you shall count them from thirty years old and upward even to fifty years old—everyone who enters on the service, to do the work of the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: from thirty to fifty years old, counting everyone who comes to serve in the work of the Tent of Meeting.

units.leftText: This is the duty of their burden, according to all their service in the Tent of Meeting: the tabernacle’s boards, its bars, its pillars, its sockets,
units.rightText: This is the duty for all their service at the Tent of Meeting: to carry the frames of the tabernacle with its crossbars, posts, and bases,

units.leftText: the pillars of the court around it, their sockets, their pins, their cords, with all their instruments, and with all their service. You shall appoint the instruments of the duty of their burden to them by name.
units.rightText: and the posts of the surrounding courtyard with their bases, tent pegs, and ropes, including all their equipment and everything related to their use. You shall assign by name the items that they are responsible to carry.

units.leftText: This is the service of the families of the sons of Merari, according to all their service in the Tent of Meeting, under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest.”
units.rightText: This is the service of the Merarite clans according to all their work at the Tent of Meeting, under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.” The Numbering of the Levite Clans

units.leftText: Moses and Aaron and the princes of the congregation counted the sons of the Kohathites by their families, and by their fathers’ houses,
units.rightText: So Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of the congregation numbered the Kohathites by their clans and families,

units.leftText: from thirty years old and upward even to fifty years old, everyone who entered into the service for work in the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: everyone from thirty to fifty years old who came to serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.

units.leftText: Those who were counted of them by their families were two thousand seven hundred fifty.
units.rightText: And those numbered by their clans totaled 2,750.

units.leftText: These are those who were counted of the families of the Kohathites, all who served in the Tent of Meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the commandment of the LORD by Moses.
units.rightText: These were counted from the Kohathite clans, everyone who could serve at the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron numbered them according to the command of the LORD through Moses.

units.leftText: Those who were counted of the sons of Gershon, by their families, and by their fathers’ houses,
units.rightText: Then the Gershonites were numbered by their clans and families,

units.leftText: from thirty years old and upward even to fifty years old—everyone who entered into the service for work in the Tent of Meeting,
units.rightText: everyone from thirty to fifty years old who came to serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.

units.leftText: even those who were counted of them, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, were two thousand six hundred thirty.
units.rightText: And those numbered by their clans and families totaled 2,630.

units.leftText: These are those who were counted of the families of the sons of Gershon, all who served in the Tent of Meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the commandment of the LORD.
units.rightText: These were counted from the Gershonite clans who served at the Tent of Meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the LORD’s command.

units.leftText: Those who were counted of the families of the sons of Merari, by their families, by their fathers’ houses,
units.rightText: And the Merarites were numbered by their clans and families,

units.leftText: from thirty years old and upward even to fifty years old—everyone who entered into the service for work in the Tent of Meeting,
units.rightText: everyone from thirty to fifty years old who came to serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.

units.leftText: even those who were counted of them by their families, were three thousand two hundred.
units.rightText: The men registered by their clans numbered 3,200.

units.leftText: These are those who were counted of the families of the sons of Merari, whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the commandment of the LORD by Moses.
units.rightText: These were counted from the Merarite clans, whom Moses and Aaron numbered at the LORD’s command through Moses.

units.leftText: All those who were counted of the Levites whom Moses and Aaron and the princes of Israel counted, by their families and by their fathers’ houses,
units.rightText: So Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel numbered by their clans and families all the Levites

units.leftText: from thirty years old and upward even to fifty years old, everyone who entered in to do the work of service and the work of bearing burdens in the Tent of Meeting,
units.rightText: from thirty to fifty years old who came to do the work of serving and carrying the Tent of Meeting.

units.leftText: even those who were counted of them, were eight thousand five hundred eighty.
units.rightText: And the number of men was 8,580.

units.leftText: According to the commandment of the LORD they were counted by Moses, everyone according to his service and according to his burden. Thus they were counted by him, as the LORD commanded Moses.
units.rightText: At the LORD’s command through Moses they were numbered, and each one was assigned his work and burden, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Command the children of Israel that they put out of the camp every leper, everyone who has a discharge, and whoever is unclean by a corpse.
units.rightText: “Command the Israelites to send away from the camp anyone with a skin disease, anyone who has a bodily discharge, and anyone who is defiled by a dead body.
rightNotes: 5:2 Forms of the Hebrew tzaraath, traditionally translated as leprosy, were used for various skin diseases; see Leviticus 13.

units.leftText: You shall put both male and female outside of the camp so that they don’t defile their camp, in the midst of which I dwell.”
units.rightText: You must send away male and female alike; send them outside the camp so they will not defile their camp, where I dwell among them.”

units.leftText: The children of Israel did so, and put them outside of the camp; as the LORD spoke to Moses, so the children of Israel did.
units.rightText: So the Israelites did this, sending such people outside the camp. They did just as the LORD had instructed Moses. Confession and Restitution (Luke 19:1–10|LUK 19:1-10*)

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: And the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Speak to the children of Israel: ‘When a man or woman commits any sin that men commit, so as to trespass against the LORD, and that soul is guilty,
units.rightText: “Tell the Israelites that when a man or woman acts unfaithfully against the LORD by committing any sin against another, that person is guilty

units.leftText: then he shall confess his sin which he has done; and he shall make restitution for his guilt in full, add to it the fifth part of it, and give it to him in respect of whom he has been guilty.
units.rightText: and must confess the sin he has committed. He must make full restitution, add a fifth to its value, and give all this to the one he has wronged.

units.leftText: But if the man has no kinsman to whom restitution may be made for the guilt, the restitution for guilt which is made to the LORD shall be the priest’s, in addition to the ram of the atonement, by which atonement shall be made for him.
units.rightText: But if the man has no relative to whom restitution can be made for the wrong, the restitution belongs to the LORD and must be given to the priest along with the ram of atonement, by which the atonement is made for him.

units.leftText: Every heave offering of all the holy things of the children of Israel, which they present to the priest, shall be his.
units.rightText: Every sacred contribution the Israelites bring to the priest shall belong to him.

units.leftText: Every man’s holy things shall be his; whatever any man gives the priest, it shall be his.’”
units.rightText: Each man’s sacred gifts are his own, but whatever he gives to the priest will belong to the priest.” The Adultery Test

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them: ‘If any man’s wife goes astray and is unfaithful to him,
units.rightText: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them that if any man’s wife goes astray and is unfaithful to him

units.leftText: and a man lies with her carnally, and it is hidden from the eyes of her husband and this is kept concealed, and she is defiled, there is no witness against her, and she isn’t taken in the act;
units.rightText: by sleeping with another man, and it is concealed from her husband and her impurity is undetected (since there is no witness against her and she was not caught in the act),

units.leftText: and the spirit of jealousy comes on him, and he is jealous of his wife and she is defiled; or if the spirit of jealousy comes on him, and he is jealous of his wife and she isn’t defiled;
units.rightText: and if a feeling of jealousy comes over her husband and he suspects his wife who has defiled herself— or if a feeling of jealousy comes over him and he suspects her even though she has not defiled herself—

units.leftText: then the man shall bring his wife to the priest, and shall bring her offering for her: one tenth of an ephah of barley meal. He shall pour no oil on it, nor put frankincense on it, for it is a meal offering of jealousy, a meal offering of memorial, bringing iniquity to memory.
units.rightText: then he is to bring his wife to the priest. He must also bring for her an offering of a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He is not to pour oil over it or put frankincense on it, because it is a grain offering for jealousy, an offering of memorial as a reminder of iniquity.
leftNotes: 5:15 1 ephah is about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel
rightNotes: 5:15 A tenth of an ephah is approximately 2 dry quarts or 2.2 liters (probably about 3.5 pounds or 1.6 kilograms of barley flour).

units.leftText: The priest shall bring her near, and set her before the LORD.
units.rightText: The priest is to bring the wife forward and have her stand before the LORD.

units.leftText: The priest shall take holy water in an earthen vessel; and the priest shall take some of the dust that is on the floor of the tabernacle and put it into the water.
units.rightText: Then he is to take some holy water in a clay jar and put some of the dust from the tabernacle floor into the water.

units.leftText: The priest shall set the woman before the LORD, and let the hair of the woman’s head go loose, and put the meal offering of memorial in her hands, which is the meal offering of jealousy. The priest shall have in his hand the water of bitterness that brings a curse.
units.rightText: After the priest has the woman stand before the LORD, he is to let down her hair and place in her hands the grain offering of memorial, which is the grain offering for jealousy. The priest is to hold the bitter water that brings a curse.

units.leftText: The priest shall cause her to take an oath and shall tell the woman, “If no man has lain with you, and if you haven’t gone aside to uncleanness, being under your husband’s authority, be free from this water of bitterness that brings a curse.
units.rightText: And he is to put the woman under oath and say to her, ‘If no other man has slept with you and you have not gone astray and become defiled while under your husband’s authority, may you be immune to this bitter water that brings a curse.

units.leftText: But if you have gone astray, being under your husband’s authority, and if you are defiled, and some man has lain with you besides your husband—”
units.rightText: But if you have gone astray while under your husband’s authority and have defiled yourself and lain carnally with a man other than your husband’—

units.leftText: then the priest shall cause the woman to swear with the oath of cursing, and the priest shall tell the woman, “May the LORD make you a curse and an oath among your people, when the LORD allows your thigh to fall away, and your body to swell;
units.rightText: and the priest shall have the woman swear under the oath of the curse— ‘then may the LORD make you an attested curse among your people by making your thigh shrivel and your belly swell.

units.leftText: and this water that brings a curse will go into your bowels, and make your body swell, and your thigh fall away.” The woman shall say, “Amen, Amen.”
units.rightText: May this water that brings a curse enter your stomach and cause your belly to swell and your thigh to shrivel.’ Then the woman is to say, ‘Amen, Amen.’

units.leftText: “‘The priest shall write these curses in a book, and he shall wipe them into the water of bitterness.
units.rightText: And the priest shall write these curses on a scroll and wash them off into the bitter water.

units.leftText: He shall make the woman drink the water of bitterness that causes the curse; and the water that causes the curse shall enter into her and become bitter.
units.rightText: He is to have the woman drink the bitter water that brings a curse, and it will enter her and may cause her bitter suffering.

units.leftText: The priest shall take the meal offering of jealousy out of the woman’s hand, and shall wave the meal offering before the LORD, and bring it to the altar.
units.rightText: The priest shall take from her hand the grain offering for jealousy, wave it before the LORD, and bring it to the altar.

units.leftText: The priest shall take a handful of the meal offering, as its memorial portion, and burn it on the altar, and afterward shall make the woman drink the water.
units.rightText: Then the priest is to take a handful of the grain offering as a memorial portion and burn it on the altar; after that he is to have the woman drink the water.

units.leftText: When he has made her drink the water, then it shall happen, if she is defiled and has committed a trespass against her husband, that the water that causes the curse will enter into her and become bitter, and her body will swell, and her thigh will fall away; and the woman will be a curse among her people.
units.rightText: When he has made her drink the water, if she has defiled herself and been unfaithful to her husband, then the water that brings a curse will enter her and cause bitter suffering; her belly will swell, her thigh will shrivel, and she will become accursed among her people.

units.leftText: If the woman isn’t defiled, but is clean; then she shall be free, and shall conceive offspring.
units.rightText: But if the woman has not defiled herself and is clean, she will be unaffected and able to conceive children.
leftNotes: 5:28 or, seed

units.leftText: “‘This is the law of jealousy, when a wife, being under her husband, goes astray, and is defiled,
units.rightText: This is the law of jealousy when a wife goes astray and defiles herself while under her husband’s authority,

units.rightText: or when a feeling of jealousy comes over a husband and he suspects his wife. He is to have the woman stand before the LORD, and the priest is to apply to her this entire law.

units.leftText: The man shall be free from iniquity, and that woman shall bear her iniquity.’”
units.rightText: The husband will be free from guilt, but the woman shall bear her iniquity.”

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: And the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them: ‘When either man or woman shall make a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite, to separate himself to the LORD,
units.rightText: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them that if a man or woman makes a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite, to separate himself to the LORD,
rightNotes: 6:2 Nazirite means one separated or one consecrated.

units.leftText: he shall separate himself from wine and strong drink. He shall drink no vinegar of wine, or vinegar of fermented drink, neither shall he drink any juice of grapes, nor eat fresh grapes or dried.
units.rightText: he is to abstain from wine and strong drink. He must not drink vinegar made from wine or strong drink, and he must not drink any grape juice or eat fresh grapes or raisins.

units.leftText: All the days of his separation he shall eat nothing that is made of the grapevine, from the seeds even to the skins.
units.rightText: All the days of his separation, he is not to eat anything that comes from the grapevine, not even the seeds or skins.

units.leftText: “‘All the days of his vow of separation no razor shall come on his head, until the days are fulfilled in which he separates himself to the LORD. He shall be holy. He shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow long.
units.rightText: For the entire period of his vow of separation, no razor shall touch his head. He must be holy until the time of his separation to the LORD is complete; he must let the hair of his head grow long.

units.leftText: “‘All the days that he separates himself to the LORD he shall not go near a dead body.
units.rightText: Throughout the days of his separation to the LORD, he must not go near a dead body.

units.leftText: He shall not make himself unclean for his father, or for his mother, for his brother, or for his sister, when they die, because his separation to God is on his head.
units.rightText: Even if his father or mother or brother or sister should die, he is not to defile himself, because the symbol of consecration to his God is upon his head.
leftNotes: 6:7 The Hebrew word rendered “God” is “אֱלֹהִ֑ים*” (Elohim).

units.leftText: All the days of his separation he is holy to the LORD.
units.rightText: Throughout the time of his separation, he is holy to the LORD.

units.leftText: “‘If any man dies very suddenly beside him, and he defiles the head of his separation, then he shall shave his head in the day of his cleansing. On the seventh day he shall shave it.
units.rightText: If someone suddenly dies in his presence and defiles his consecrated head of hair, he must shave his head on the day of his cleansing — the seventh day.

units.leftText: On the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest, to the door of the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: On the eighth day he must bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

units.leftText: The priest shall offer one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering, and make atonement for him, because he sinned by reason of the dead, and shall make his head holy that same day.
units.rightText: And the priest is to offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to make atonement for him, because he has sinned by being in the presence of the dead body. On that day he must consecrate his head again.
rightNotes: 6:11 Or purification offering; here and throughout Numbers

units.leftText: He shall separate to the LORD the days of his separation, and shall bring a male lamb a year old for a trespass offering; but the former days shall be void, because his separation was defiled.
units.rightText: He must rededicate his time of separation to the LORD and bring a year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. But the preceding days shall not be counted, because his separation was defiled.

units.leftText: “‘This is the law of the Nazirite: when the days of his separation are fulfilled, he shall be brought to the door of the Tent of Meeting,

units.rightText: Then at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, the Nazirite is to shave his consecrated head, take the hair, and put it on the fire under the peace offering.

units.leftText: “‘This is the law of the Nazirite who vows and of his offering to the LORD for his separation, in addition to that which he is able to afford. According to his vow which he vows, so he must do after the law of his separation.’”

units.rightText: Each silver platter weighed a hundred and thirty shekels, and each silver bowl seventy shekels. The total weight of the silver articles was two thousand four hundred shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.
rightNotes: 7:85 2,400 shekels is approximately 60.3 pounds or 27.4 kilograms.

units.leftText: the twelve golden ladles, full of incense, weighing ten shekels apiece, according to the shekel of the sanctuary; all the gold of the ladles weighed one hundred twenty shekels;
units.rightText: The twelve gold dishes filled with incense weighed ten shekels each, according to the sanctuary shekel. The total weight of the gold dishes was a hundred and twenty shekels.
rightNotes: 7:86 120 shekels is approximately 3 pounds or 1.4 kilograms.

units.leftText: all the cattle for the burnt offering twelve bulls, the rams twelve, the male lambs a year old twelve, and their meal offering; and twelve male goats for a sin offering;
units.rightText: All the livestock for the burnt offering totaled twelve bulls, twelve rams, and twelve male lambs a year old — together with their grain offerings — and twelve male goats for the sin offering.

units.leftText: and all the cattle for the sacrifice of peace offerings: twenty-four bulls, sixty rams, sixty male goats, and sixty male lambs a year old. This was the dedication offering of the altar, after it was anointed.
units.rightText: All the livestock sacrificed for the peace offering totaled twenty-four bulls, sixty rams, sixty male goats, and sixty male lambs a year old. This was the dedication offering for the altar after it was anointed.

units.leftText: When Moses went into the Tent of Meeting to speak with the LORD, he heard his voice speaking to him from above the mercy seat that was on the ark of the Testimony, from between the two cherubim; and he spoke to him.
units.rightText: When Moses entered the Tent of Meeting to speak with the LORD, he heard the voice speaking to him from between the two cherubim above the mercy seat on the ark of the Testimony. Thus the LORD spoke to him.
rightNotes: 7:89 Or atonement cover
7:89 That is, the ark of the covenant

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Speak to Aaron, and tell him, ‘When you light the lamps, the seven lamps shall give light in front of the lamp stand.’”
units.rightText: “Speak to Aaron and tell him: ‘When you set up the seven lamps, they are to light the area in front of the lampstand.’”

units.leftText: Aaron did so. He lit its lamps to light the area in front of the lamp stand, as the LORD commanded Moses.
units.rightText: And Aaron did so; he set up the lamps facing toward the front of the lampstand, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

units.leftText: This was the workmanship of the lamp stand, beaten work of gold. From its base to its flowers, it was beaten work. He made the lamp stand according to the pattern which the LORD had shown Moses.
units.rightText: This is how the lampstand was constructed: it was made of hammered gold from its base to its blossoms, fashioned according to the pattern the LORD had shown Moses. Cleansing the Levites

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: Again the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Take the Levites from among the children of Israel, and cleanse them.
units.rightText: “Take the Levites from among the Israelites and make them ceremonially clean.

units.leftText: You shall do this to them to cleanse them: sprinkle the water of cleansing on them, let them shave their whole bodies with a razor, let them wash their clothes, and cleanse themselves.
units.rightText: This is what you must do to cleanse them: Sprinkle them with the water of purification. Have them shave their whole bodies and wash their clothes, and so purify themselves.

units.leftText: Then let them take a young bull and its meal offering, fine flour mixed with oil; and another young bull you shall take for a sin offering.
units.rightText: Then have them take a young bull with its grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil, and you are to take a second young bull for a sin offering.

units.leftText: You shall present the Levites before the Tent of Meeting. You shall assemble the whole congregation of the children of Israel.
units.rightText: Bring the Levites before the Tent of Meeting and assemble the whole congregation of Israel.

units.leftText: You shall present the Levites before the LORD. The children of Israel shall lay their hands on the Levites,
units.rightText: You are to present the Levites before the LORD and have the Israelites lay their hands upon them.

units.leftText: and Aaron shall offer the Levites before the LORD for a wave offering on the behalf of the children of Israel, that it may be theirs to do the service of the LORD.
units.rightText: Aaron is to present the Levites before the LORD as a wave offering from the sons of Israel, so that they may perform the service of the LORD.

units.leftText: “The Levites shall lay their hands on the heads of the bulls, and you shall offer the one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering to the LORD, to make atonement for the Levites.
units.rightText: And the Levites are to lay their hands on the heads of the bulls, and offer to the LORD one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, to make atonement for the Levites.

units.leftText: You shall set the Levites before Aaron and before his sons, and offer them as a wave offering to the LORD.
units.rightText: You are to have the Levites stand before Aaron and his sons and then present them before the LORD as a wave offering.

units.leftText: Thus you shall separate the Levites from among the children of Israel, and the Levites shall be mine.
units.rightText: In this way you shall separate the Levites from the rest of the Israelites, and the Levites will belong to Me.

units.leftText: “After that, the Levites shall go in to do the service of the Tent of Meeting. You shall cleanse them, and offer them as a wave offering.
units.rightText: After you have cleansed them and presented them as a wave offering, they may come to serve at the Tent of Meeting.

units.leftText: For they are wholly given to me from among the children of Israel; instead of all who open the womb, even the firstborn of all the children of Israel, I have taken them to me.
units.rightText: For the Levites have been wholly given to Me from among the sons of Israel. I have taken them for Myself in place of all who come first from the womb, the firstborn of all the sons of Israel.

units.leftText: For all the firstborn among the children of Israel are mine, both man and animal. On the day that I struck all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, I sanctified them for myself.
units.rightText: For every firstborn male in Israel is Mine, both man and beast. I set them apart for Myself on the day I struck down all the firstborn in the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: I have taken the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel.
units.rightText: But I have taken the Levites in place of all the firstborn among the sons of Israel.

units.leftText: I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and to his sons from among the children of Israel, to do the service of the children of Israel in the Tent of Meeting, and to make atonement for the children of Israel, so that there will be no plague among the children of Israel when the children of Israel come near to the sanctuary.”
units.rightText: And I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons from among the Israelites, to perform the service for the Israelites at the Tent of Meeting and to make atonement on their behalf, so that no plague will come against the Israelites when they approach the sanctuary.”

units.leftText: Moses, and Aaron, and all the congregation of the children of Israel did so to the Levites. According to all that the LORD commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so the children of Israel did to them.
units.rightText: So Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation of Israel did with the Levites everything that the LORD had commanded Moses they should do.

units.leftText: The Levites purified themselves from sin, and they washed their clothes; and Aaron offered them for a wave offering before the LORD and Aaron made atonement for them to cleanse them.
units.rightText: The Levites purified themselves and washed their clothes, and Aaron presented them as a wave offering before the LORD. Aaron also made atonement for them to cleanse them.

units.leftText: After that, the Levites went in to do their service in the Tent of Meeting before Aaron and before his sons: as the LORD had commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so they did to them.
units.rightText: After that, the Levites came to perform their service at the Tent of Meeting in the presence of Aaron and his sons. Thus they did with the Levites just as the LORD had commanded Moses. Retirement for Levites

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: And the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “This is what is assigned to the Levites: from twenty-five years old and upward they shall go in to wait on the service in the work of the Tent of Meeting;
units.rightText: “This applies to the Levites: Men twenty-five years of age or older shall enter to perform the service in the work at the Tent of Meeting.

units.leftText: and from the age of fifty years they shall retire from doing the work, and shall serve no more,
units.rightText: But at the age of fifty, they must retire from performing the work and no longer serve.

units.leftText: but shall assist their brothers in the Tent of Meeting, to perform the duty, and shall perform no service. This is how you shall have the Levites do their duties.”
units.rightText: After that, they may assist their brothers in fulfilling their duties at the Tent of Meeting, but they themselves are not to do the work. This is how you are to assign responsibilities to the Levites.”

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after they had come out of the land of Egypt, saying,
units.rightText: In the first month of the second year after Israel had come out of the land of Egypt, the LORD spoke to Moses in the Wilderness of Sinai:

units.leftText: “Let the children of Israel keep the Passover in its appointed season.
units.rightText: “The Israelites are to observe the Passover at its appointed time.

units.leftText: On the fourteenth day of this month, at evening, you shall keep it in its appointed season. You shall keep it according to all its statutes and according to all its ordinances.”
units.rightText: You are to observe it at the appointed time, at twilight on the fourteenth day of this month, in accordance with its statutes and ordinances.”
rightNotes: 9:3 Hebrew between the two evenings of the fourteenth; also in verses 5 and 11

units.leftText: Moses told the children of Israel that they should keep the Passover.
units.rightText: So Moses told the Israelites to observe the Passover,

units.leftText: They kept the Passover in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at evening, in the wilderness of Sinai. According to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so the children of Israel did.
units.rightText: and they did so in the Wilderness of Sinai, at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month. The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

units.leftText: There were certain men who were unclean because of the dead body of a man, so that they could not keep the Passover on that day, and they came before Moses and Aaron on that day.
units.rightText: But there were some men who were unclean due to a dead body, so they could not observe the Passover on that day. And they came before Moses and Aaron that same day

units.leftText: Those men said to him, “We are unclean because of the dead body of a man. Why are we kept back, that we may not offer the offering of the LORD in its appointed season among the children of Israel?”
units.rightText: and said to Moses, “We are unclean because of a dead body, but why should we be excluded from presenting the LORD’s offering with the other Israelites at the appointed time?”
