units.leftText: Moses answered them, “Wait, that I may hear what the LORD will command concerning you.”
units.rightText: “Wait here until I find out what the LORD commands concerning you,” Moses replied.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Say to the children of Israel, ‘If any man of you or of your generations is unclean by reason of a dead body, or is on a journey far away, he shall still keep the Passover to the LORD.
units.rightText: “Tell the Israelites: ‘When any one of you or your descendants is unclean because of a dead body, or is away on a journey, he may still observe the Passover to the LORD.

units.leftText: In the second month, on the fourteenth day at evening they shall keep it; they shall eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
units.rightText: Such people are to observe it at twilight on the fourteenth day of the second month. They are to eat the lamb, together with unleavened bread and bitter herbs;

units.leftText: They shall leave none of it until the morning, nor break a bone of it. According to all the statute of the Passover they shall keep it.
units.rightText: they may not leave any of it until morning or break any of its bones. They must observe the Passover according to all its statutes.

units.leftText: But the man who is clean, and is not on a journey, and fails to keep the Passover, that soul shall be cut off from his people. Because he didn’t offer the offering of the LORD in its appointed season, that man shall bear his sin.
units.rightText: But if a man who is ceremonially clean and is not on a journey still fails to observe the Passover, he must be cut off from his people, because he did not present the LORD’s offering at its appointed time. That man will bear the consequences of his sin.

units.leftText: “‘If a foreigner lives among you and desires to keep the Passover to the LORD, then he shall do so according to the statute of the Passover, and according to its ordinance. You shall have one statute, both for the foreigner and for him who is born in the land.’”
units.rightText: If a foreigner dwelling among you wants to observe the Passover to the LORD, he is to do so according to the Passover statute and its ordinances. You are to apply the same statute to both the foreigner and the native of the land.’” The Cloud above the Tabernacle (Exodus 40:34–38|EXO 40:34-38*)

units.leftText: On the day that the tabernacle was raised up, the cloud covered the tabernacle, even the Tent of the Testimony. At evening it was over the tabernacle, as it were the appearance of fire, until morning.
units.rightText: On the day that the tabernacle, the Tent of the Testimony, was set up, the cloud covered it and appeared like fire above the tabernacle from evening until morning.

units.leftText: So it was continually. The cloud covered it, and the appearance of fire by night.
units.rightText: It remained that way continually; the cloud would cover the tabernacle by day, and at night it would appear like fire.
rightNotes: 9:16 LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate; Hebrew does not include by day

units.leftText: Whenever the cloud was taken up from over the Tent, then after that the children of Israel traveled; and in the place where the cloud remained, there the children of Israel encamped.
units.rightText: Whenever the cloud was lifted from above the Tent, the Israelites would set out, and wherever the cloud settled, there the Israelites would camp.

units.leftText: At the commandment of the LORD, the children of Israel traveled, and at the commandment of the LORD they encamped. As long as the cloud remained on the tabernacle they remained encamped.
units.rightText: At the LORD’s command the Israelites set out, and at the LORD’s command they camped. As long as the cloud remained over the tabernacle, they remained encamped.

units.leftText: When the cloud stayed on the tabernacle many days, then the children of Israel kept the LORD’s command, and didn’t travel.
units.rightText: Even when the cloud lingered over the tabernacle for many days, the Israelites kept the LORD’s charge and did not set out.

units.leftText: Sometimes the cloud was a few days on the tabernacle; then according to the commandment of the LORD they remained encamped, and according to the commandment of the LORD they traveled.
units.rightText: Sometimes the cloud remained over the tabernacle for only a few days, and they would camp at the LORD’s command and set out at the LORD’s command.

units.leftText: Sometimes the cloud was from evening until morning; and when the cloud was taken up in the morning, they traveled; or by day and by night, when the cloud was taken up, they traveled.
units.rightText: Sometimes the cloud remained only from evening until morning, and when it lifted in the morning, they would set out. Whether it was by day or by night, when the cloud was taken up, they would set out.

units.leftText: Whether it was two days, or a month, or a year that the cloud stayed on the tabernacle, remaining on it, the children of Israel remained encamped, and didn’t travel; but when it was taken up, they traveled.
units.rightText: Whether the cloud lingered for two days, a month, or longer, the Israelites camped and did not set out as long as the cloud remained over the tabernacle; but when it was lifted, they would set out.

units.leftText: At the commandment of the LORD they encamped, and at the commandment of the LORD they traveled. They kept the LORD’s command, at the commandment of the LORD by Moses.
units.rightText: They camped at the LORD’s command, and they set out at the LORD’s command; they carried out the LORD’s charge according to His command through Moses.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Make two trumpets of silver. You shall make them of beaten work. You shall use them for the calling of the congregation and for the journeying of the camps.
units.rightText: “Make two trumpets of hammered silver to be used for calling the congregation and for having the camps set out.

units.leftText: When they blow them, all the congregation shall gather themselves to you at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: When both are sounded, the whole congregation is to assemble before you at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

units.leftText: If they blow just one, then the princes, the heads of the thousands of Israel, shall gather themselves to you.
units.rightText: But if only one is sounded, then the leaders, the heads of the clans of Israel, are to gather before you.

units.leftText: When you blow an alarm, the camps that lie on the east side shall go forward.
units.rightText: When you sound short blasts, the camps that lie on the east side are to set out.

units.leftText: When you blow an alarm the second time, the camps that lie on the south side shall go forward. They shall blow an alarm for their journeys.
units.rightText: When you sound the short blasts a second time, the camps that lie on the south side are to set out. The blasts are to signal them to set out.

units.leftText: But when the assembly is to be gathered together, you shall blow, but you shall not sound an alarm.
units.rightText: To convene the assembly, you are to sound long blasts, not short ones.

units.leftText: “The sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow the trumpets. This shall be to you for a statute forever throughout your generations.
units.rightText: The sons of Aaron, the priests, are to sound the trumpets. This shall be a permanent statute for you and the generations to come.

units.leftText: When you go to war in your land against the adversary who oppresses you, then you shall sound an alarm with the trumpets. Then you will be remembered before the LORD your God, and you will be saved from your enemies.
units.rightText: When you enter into battle in your land against an adversary who attacks you, sound short blasts on the trumpets, and you will be remembered before the LORD your God and saved from your enemies.

units.leftText: “Also in the day of your gladness, and in your set feasts, and in the beginnings of your months, you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings, and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings; and they shall be to you for a memorial before your God. I am the LORD your God.”
units.rightText: And on your joyous occasions, your appointed feasts, and the beginning of each month, you are to blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and peace offerings to serve as a reminder for you before your God. I am the LORD your God.” From Sinai to Paran

units.leftText: In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle of the covenant.
units.rightText: On the twentieth day of the second month of the second year, the cloud was lifted from above the tabernacle of the Testimony,

units.leftText: The children of Israel went forward on their journeys out of the wilderness of Sinai; and the cloud stayed in the wilderness of Paran.
units.rightText: and the Israelites set out from the Wilderness of Sinai, traveling from place to place until the cloud settled in the Wilderness of Paran.

units.leftText: They first went forward according to the commandment of the LORD by Moses.
units.rightText: They set out this first time according to the LORD’s command through Moses.

units.leftText: First, the standard of the camp of the children of Judah went forward according to their armies. Nahshon the son of Amminadab was over his army.
units.rightText: First, the divisions of the camp of Judah set out under their standard, with Nahshon son of Amminadab in command.

units.leftText: Nethanel the son of Zuar was over the army of the tribe of the children of Issachar.
units.rightText: Nethanel son of Zuar was over the division of the tribe of Issachar,

units.leftText: Eliab the son of Helon was over the army of the tribe of the children of Zebulun.
units.rightText: and Eliab son of Helon was over the division of the tribe of Zebulun.

units.leftText: The tabernacle was taken down; and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari, who bore the tabernacle, went forward.
units.rightText: Then the tabernacle was taken down, and the Gershonites and the Merarites set out, transporting it.

units.leftText: The standard of the camp of Reuben went forward according to their armies. Elizur the son of Shedeur was over his army.
units.rightText: Then the divisions of the camp of Reuben set out under their standard, with Elizur son of Shedeur in command.

units.leftText: Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai was over the army of the tribe of the children of Simeon.
units.rightText: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was over the division of the tribe of Simeon,

units.leftText: Eliasaph the son of Deuel was over the army of the tribe of the children of Gad.
units.rightText: and Eliasaph son of Deuel was over the division of the tribe of Gad.

units.leftText: The Kohathites set forward, bearing the sanctuary. The others set up the tabernacle before they arrived.
units.rightText: Then the Kohathites set out, transporting the holy objects; the tabernacle was to be set up before their arrival.

units.leftText: The standard of the camp of the children of Ephraim set forward according to their armies. Elishama the son of Ammihud was over his army.
units.rightText: Next, the divisions of the camp of Ephraim set out under their standard, with Elishama son of Ammihud in command.

units.leftText: Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur was over the army of the tribe of the children of Manasseh.
units.rightText: Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was over the division of the tribe of Manasseh,

units.leftText: Abidan the son of Gideoni was over the army of the tribe of the children of Benjamin.
units.rightText: and Abidan son of Gideoni was over the division of the tribe of Benjamin.

units.leftText: The standard of the camp of the children of Dan, which was the rear guard of all the camps, set forward according to their armies. Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai was over his army.
units.rightText: Finally, the divisions of the camp of Dan set out under their standard, serving as the rear guard for all units, with Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai in command.

units.leftText: Pagiel the son of Ochran was over the army of the tribe of the children of Asher.
units.rightText: Pagiel son of Ocran was over the division of the tribe of Asher,

units.leftText: Ahira the son of Enan was over the army of the tribe of the children of Naphtali.
units.rightText: and Ahira son of Enan was over the division of the tribe of Naphtali.

units.leftText: Thus were the travels of the children of Israel according to their armies; and they went forward.
units.rightText: This was the order of march for the Israelite divisions as they set out.

units.leftText: Moses said to Hobab, the son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law, “We are journeying to the place of which the LORD said, ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us, and we will treat you well; for the LORD has spoken good concerning Israel.”
units.rightText: Then Moses said to Hobab, the son of Moses’ father-in-law Reuel the Midianite, “We are setting out for the place of which the LORD said: ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us, and we will treat you well, for the LORD has promised good things to Israel.”
rightNotes: 10:29 Reuel was also called Jethro; see Exodus 3:1|EXO 3:1*.

units.leftText: He said to him, “I will not go; but I will depart to my own land, and to my relatives.”
units.rightText: “I will not go,” Hobab replied. “Instead, I am going back to my own land and my own people.”

units.leftText: Moses said, “Don’t leave us, please; because you know how we are to encamp in the wilderness, and you can be our eyes.
units.rightText: “Please do not leave us,” Moses said, “since you know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you can serve as our eyes.

units.leftText: It shall be, if you go with us—yes, it shall be—that whatever good the LORD does to us, we will do the same to you.”
units.rightText: If you come with us, we will share with you whatever good things the LORD gives us.”

units.leftText: They set forward from the Mount of the LORD three days’ journey. The ark of the LORD’s covenant went before them three days’ journey, to seek out a resting place for them.
units.rightText: So they set out on a three-day journey from the mountain of the LORD, with the ark of the covenant of the LORD traveling ahead of them for those three days to seek a resting place for them.

units.leftText: The cloud of the LORD was over them by day, when they set forward from the camp.
units.rightText: And the cloud of the LORD was over them by day when they set out from the camp.

units.leftText: When the ark went forward, Moses said, “Rise up, LORD, and let your enemies be scattered! Let those who hate you flee before you!”
units.rightText: Whenever the ark set out, Moses would say, “Rise up, O LORD! May Your enemies be scattered; may those who hate You flee before You.”

units.leftText: When it rested, he said, “Return, LORD, to the ten thousands of the thousands of Israel.”
units.rightText: And when it came to rest, he would say: “Return, O LORD, to the countless thousands of Israel.”

units.leftText: The people were complaining in the ears of the LORD. When the LORD heard it, his anger burned; and the LORD’s fire burned among them, and consumed some of the outskirts of the camp.
units.rightText: Soon the people began to complain about their hardship in the hearing of the LORD, and when He heard them, His anger was kindled, and fire from the LORD blazed among them and consumed the outskirts of the camp.

units.leftText: The people cried to Moses; and Moses prayed to the LORD, and the fire abated.
units.rightText: And the people cried out to Moses, and he prayed to the LORD, and the fire died down.

units.leftText: The name of that place was called Taberah, because the LORD’s fire burned among them.
units.rightText: So that place was called Taberah, because the fire of the LORD had burned among them.
leftNotes: 11:3 Taberah means “burning”
rightNotes: 11:3 Taberah means burning.

units.leftText: The mixed multitude that was among them lusted exceedingly; and the children of Israel also wept again, and said, “Who will give us meat to eat?
units.rightText: Meanwhile, the rabble among them had a strong craving for other food, and again the Israelites wept and said, “Who will feed us meat?

units.leftText: We remember the fish, which we ate in Egypt for nothing; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlic;
units.rightText: We remember the fish we ate freely in Egypt, along with the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic.

units.leftText: but now we have lost our appetite. There is nothing at all except this manna to look at.”
units.rightText: But now our appetite is gone; there is nothing to see but this manna!”

units.leftText: The manna was like coriander seed, and it looked like bdellium.
units.rightText: Now the manna resembled coriander seed, and its appearance was like that of gum resin.
leftNotes: 11:7 Bdellium is a resin extracted from certain African trees.

units.leftText: The people went around, gathered it, and ground it in mills, or beat it in mortars, and boiled it in pots, and made cakes of it. Its taste was like the taste of fresh oil.
units.rightText: The people walked around and gathered it, ground it on a handmill or crushed it in a mortar, then boiled it in a cooking pot or shaped it into cakes. It tasted like pastry baked with fine oil.

units.leftText: When the dew fell on the camp in the night, the manna fell on it.
units.rightText: When the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna would fall with it. The Complaint of Moses

units.leftText: Moses heard the people weeping throughout their families, every man at the door of his tent; and the LORD’s anger burned greatly; and Moses was displeased.
units.rightText: Then Moses heard the people of family after family weeping at the entrances to their tents, and the anger of the LORD was kindled greatly, and Moses was also displeased.

units.leftText: Moses said to the LORD, “Why have you treated your servant so badly? Why haven’t I found favor in your sight, that you lay the burden of all this people on me?
units.rightText: So Moses asked the LORD, “Why have You brought this trouble on Your servant? Why have I not found favor in Your sight, that You have laid upon me the burden of all these people?

units.leftText: Have I conceived all this people? Have I brought them out, that you should tell me, ‘Carry them in your bosom, as a nurse carries a nursing infant, to the land which you swore to their fathers’?
units.rightText: Did I conceive all these people? Did I give them birth, so that You should tell me, ‘Carry them in your bosom, as a nurse carries an infant,’ to the land that You swore to give their fathers?

units.leftText: Where could I get meat to give all these people? For they weep before me, saying, ‘Give us meat, that we may eat.’
units.rightText: Where can I get meat for all these people? For they keep crying out to me, ‘Give us meat to eat!’

units.leftText: I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me.
units.rightText: I cannot carry all these people by myself; it is too burdensome for me.

units.leftText: If you treat me this way, please kill me right now, if I have found favor in your sight; and don’t let me see my wretchedness.”
units.rightText: If this is how You are going to treat me, please kill me right now — if I have found favor in Your eyes — and let me not see my own wretchedness.” Seventy Elders Anointed

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “Gather to me seventy men of the elders of Israel, whom you know to be the elders of the people and officers over them; and bring them to the Tent of Meeting, that they may stand there with you.
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Bring Me seventy of the elders of Israel known to you as leaders and officers of the people. Bring them to the Tent of Meeting and have them stand there with you.

units.leftText: I will come down and talk with you there. I will take of the Spirit which is on you, and will put it on them; and they shall bear the burden of the people with you, that you don’t bear it yourself alone.
units.rightText: And I will come down and speak with you there, and I will take some of the Spirit that is on you and put that Spirit on them. They will help you bear the burden of the people, so that you do not have to bear it by yourself.

units.leftText: “Say to the people, ‘Sanctify yourselves in preparation for tomorrow, and you will eat meat; for you have wept in the ears of the LORD, saying, “Who will give us meat to eat? For it was well with us in Egypt.” Therefore the LORD will give you meat, and you will eat.
units.rightText: And say to the people: Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, and you will eat meat, because you have cried out in the hearing of the LORD, saying: ‘Who will feed us meat? For we were better off in Egypt!’ Therefore the LORD will give you meat, and you will eat.

units.leftText: You will not eat just one day, or two days, or five days, or ten days, or twenty days,
units.rightText: You will eat it not for one or two days, nor for five or ten or twenty days,

units.leftText: but a whole month, until it comes out at your nostrils, and it is loathsome to you; because you have rejected the LORD who is among you, and have wept before him, saying, “Why did we come out of Egypt?”’”
units.rightText: but for a whole month— until it comes out of your nostrils and makes you nauseous— because you have rejected the LORD, who is among you, and have cried out before Him, saying, ‘Why did we ever leave Egypt?’”

units.leftText: Moses said, “The people, among whom I am, are six hundred thousand men on foot; and you have said, ‘I will give them meat, that they may eat a whole month.’
units.rightText: But Moses replied, “Here I am among 600,000 men on foot, yet You say, ‘I will give them meat, and they will eat for a month.’

units.leftText: Shall flocks and herds be slaughtered for them, to be sufficient for them? Shall all the fish of the sea be gathered together for them, to be sufficient for them?”
units.rightText: If all our flocks and herds were slaughtered for them, would they have enough? Or if all the fish in the sea were caught for them, would they have enough?”

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “Has the LORD’s hand grown short? Now you will see whether my word will happen to you or not.”
units.rightText: The LORD answered Moses, “Is the LORD’s arm too short? Now you will see whether or not My word will come to pass.”

units.leftText: Moses went out, and told the people the LORD’s words; and he gathered seventy men of the elders of the people, and set them around the Tent.
units.rightText: So Moses went out and relayed to the people the words of the LORD, and he gathered seventy of the elders of the people and had them stand around the tent.

units.leftText: The LORD came down in the cloud, and spoke to him, and took of the Spirit that was on him, and put it on the seventy elders. When the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied, but they did so no more.
units.rightText: Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to him, and He took some of the Spirit that was on Moses and placed that Spirit on the seventy elders. As the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied — but they never did so again.

units.leftText: But two men remained in the camp. The name of one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad; and the Spirit rested on them. They were of those who were written, but had not gone out to the Tent; and they prophesied in the camp.
units.rightText: Two men, however, had remained in the camp — one named Eldad and the other Medad — and the Spirit rested on them. They were among those listed, but they had not gone out to the tent, and they prophesied in the camp.

units.leftText: A young man ran, and told Moses, and said, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp!”
units.rightText: A young man ran and reported to Moses, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.”

units.leftText: Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of Moses, one of his chosen men, answered, “My lord Moses, forbid them!”
units.rightText: Joshua son of Nun, the attendant to Moses since youth, spoke up and said, “Moses, my lord, stop them!”

units.leftText: Moses said to him, “Are you jealous for my sake? I wish that all the LORD’s people were prophets, that the LORD would put his Spirit on them!”
units.rightText: But Moses replied, “Are you jealous on my account? I wish that all the LORD’s people were prophets and that the LORD would place His Spirit on them!”

units.leftText: Moses went into the camp, he and the elders of Israel.
units.rightText: Then Moses returned to the camp, along with the elders of Israel. The Quail and the Plague

units.leftText: A wind from the LORD went out and brought quails from the sea, and let them fall by the camp, about a day’s journey on this side, and a day’s journey on the other side, around the camp, and about two cubits above the surface of the earth.
units.rightText: Now a wind sent by the LORD came up, drove in quail from the sea, and brought them near the camp, about two cubits above the surface of the ground, for a day’s journey in every direction around the camp.
leftNotes: 11:31 A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters.
rightNotes: 11:31 Or up to two cubits deep; that is, approximately 3 feet or 91.4 centimeters

units.leftText: The people rose up all that day, and all of that night, and all the next day, and gathered the quails. He who gathered least gathered ten homers; and they spread them all out for themselves around the camp.
units.rightText: All that day and night, and all the next day, the people stayed up gathering the quail. No one gathered less than ten homers, and they spread them out all around the camp.
leftNotes: 11:32 1 homer is about 220 liters or 6 bushels
rightNotes: 11:32 10 homers is approximately 62.4 bushels or 2,200 liters.

units.leftText: While the meat was still between their teeth, before it was chewed, the LORD’s anger burned against the people, and the LORD struck the people with a very great plague.
units.rightText: But while the meat was still between their teeth, before it was chewed, the anger of the LORD burned against the people, and the LORD struck them with a severe plague.

units.leftText: The name of that place was called Kibroth Hattaavah, because there they buried the people who lusted.
units.rightText: So they called that place Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had craved other food.
leftNotes: 11:34 Kibroth Hattaavah means “graves of lust”
rightNotes: 11:34 Kibroth-hattaavah means graves of craving.

units.leftText: From Kibroth Hattaavah the people traveled to Hazeroth; and they stayed at Hazeroth.
units.rightText: From Kibroth-hattaavah the people moved on to Hazeroth, where they remained for some time.

units.leftText: Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Cushite woman whom he had married; for he had married a Cushite woman.
units.rightText: Then Miriam and Aaron criticized Moses because of the Cushite woman he had married, for he had taken a Cushite wife.

units.leftText: They said, “Has the LORD indeed spoken only with Moses? Hasn’t he spoken also with us?” And the LORD heard it.
units.rightText: “Does the LORD speak only through Moses?” they said. “Does He not also speak through us?” And the LORD heard this.

units.leftText: Now the man Moses was very humble, more than all the men who were on the surface of the earth.
units.rightText: Now Moses was a very humble man, more so than any man on the face of the earth.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke suddenly to Moses, to Aaron, and to Miriam, “You three come out to the Tent of Meeting!” The three of them came out.
units.rightText: And suddenly the LORD said to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, “You three, come out to the Tent of Meeting.” So the three went out,

units.leftText: The LORD came down in a pillar of cloud, and stood at the door of the Tent, and called Aaron and Miriam; and they both came forward.
units.rightText: and the LORD came down in a pillar of cloud, stood at the entrance to the Tent, and summoned Aaron and Miriam. When both of them had stepped forward,

units.leftText: He said, “Now hear my words. If there is a prophet among you, I, the LORD, will make myself known to him in a vision. I will speak with him in a dream.
units.rightText: He said, “Hear now My words: If there is a prophet among you, I, the LORD, will reveal Myself to him in a vision; I will speak to him in a dream.

units.leftText: My servant Moses is not so. He is faithful in all my house.
units.rightText: But this is not so with My servant Moses; he is faithful in all My house.
rightNotes: 12:7 Cited in Hebrews 3:5|HEB 3:5*

units.leftText: With him, I will speak mouth to mouth, even plainly, and not in riddles; and he shall see the LORD’s form. Why then were you not afraid to speak against my servant, against Moses?”
units.rightText: I speak with him face to face, clearly and not in riddles; he sees the form of the LORD.

units.leftText: The LORD’s anger burned against them; and he departed.
units.rightText: So the anger of the LORD burned against them, and He departed.

units.leftText: The cloud departed from over the Tent; and behold, Miriam was leprous, as white as snow. Aaron looked at Miriam, and behold, she was leprous.
units.rightText: As the cloud lifted from above the Tent, suddenly Miriam became leprous, white as snow. Aaron turned toward her, saw that she was leprous,
rightNotes: 12:10 The Hebrew word traditionally translated as leprous was used for various skin diseases; see Leviticus 13.

units.leftText: Aaron said to Moses, “Oh, my lord, please don’t count this sin against us, in which we have done foolishly, and in which we have sinned.
units.rightText: and said to Moses, “My lord, please do not hold against us this sin we have so foolishly committed.

units.leftText: Let her not, I pray, be as one dead, of whom the flesh is half consumed when he comes out of his mother’s womb.”
units.rightText: Please do not let her be like a stillborn infant whose flesh is half consumed when he comes out of his mother’s womb.”

units.leftText: Moses cried to the LORD, saying, “Heal her, God, I beg you!”
units.rightText: So Moses cried out to the LORD, “O God, please heal her!”

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “If her father had but spit in her face, shouldn’t she be ashamed seven days? Let her be shut up outside of the camp seven days, and after that she shall be brought in again.”
units.rightText: But the LORD answered Moses, “If her father had but spit in her face, would she not have been in disgrace for seven days? Let her be confined outside the camp for seven days; after that she may be brought back in.”

units.leftText: Miriam was shut up outside of the camp seven days, and the people didn’t travel until Miriam was brought in again.
units.rightText: So Miriam was confined outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not move on until she was brought in again.

units.leftText: Afterward the people traveled from Hazeroth, and encamped in the wilderness of Paran.
units.rightText: After that, the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the Wilderness of Paran.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: And the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Send men, that they may spy out the land of Canaan, which I give to the children of Israel. Of every tribe of their fathers, you shall send a man, every one a prince among them.”
units.rightText: “Send out for yourself men to spy out the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites. From each of their fathers’ tribes send one man who is a leader among them.”

units.leftText: Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran according to the commandment of the LORD. All of them were men who were heads of the children of Israel.
units.rightText: So at the command of the LORD, Moses sent them out from the Wilderness of Paran. All the men were leaders of the Israelites,
rightNotes: 13:3 Literally according to the mouth

units.leftText: These were their names: Of the tribe of Reuben, Shammua the son of Zaccur.
units.rightText: and these were their names: From the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur;

units.leftText: Of the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat the son of Hori.
units.rightText: from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori;

units.leftText: Of the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh.
units.rightText: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;

units.leftText: Of the tribe of Issachar, Igal the son of Joseph.
units.rightText: from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph;

units.leftText: Of the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Nun.
units.rightText: from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;

units.leftText: Of the tribe of Benjamin, Palti the son of Raphu.
units.rightText: from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu;

units.leftText: Of the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel the son of Sodi.
units.rightText: from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi;

units.leftText: Of the tribe of Joseph, of the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi the son of Susi.
units.rightText: from the tribe of Manasseh (a tribe of Joseph), Gaddi son of Susi;

units.leftText: Of the tribe of Dan, Ammiel the son of Gemalli.
units.rightText: from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli;

units.leftText: Of the tribe of Asher, Sethur the son of Michael.
units.rightText: from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael;

units.leftText: Of the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi the son of Vophsi.
units.rightText: from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi;

units.leftText: Of the tribe of Gad, Geuel the son of Machi.
units.rightText: and from the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi.

units.leftText: These are the names of the men who Moses sent to spy out the land. Moses called Hoshea the son of Nun Joshua.
units.rightText: These were the names of the men Moses sent to spy out the land; and Moses gave to Hoshea son of Nun the name Joshua.

units.leftText: Moses sent them to spy out the land of Canaan, and said to them, “Go up this way by the South, and go up into the hill country.
units.rightText: When Moses sent them to spy out the land of Canaan, he told them, “Go up through the Negev and into the hill country.

units.leftText: See the land, what it is; and the people who dwell therein, whether they are strong or weak, whether they are few or many;
units.rightText: See what the land is like and whether its people are strong or weak, few or many.

units.leftText: and what the land is that they dwell in, whether it is good or bad; and what cities they are that they dwell in, whether in camps, or in strongholds;
units.rightText: Is the land where they live good or bad? Are the cities where they dwell open camps or fortifications?

units.leftText: and what the land is, whether it is fertile or poor, whether there is wood therein, or not. Be courageous, and bring some of the fruit of the land.” Now the time was the time of the first-ripe grapes.
units.rightText: Is the soil fertile or unproductive? Are there trees in it or not? Be courageous and bring back some of the fruit of the land.” (It was the season for the first ripe grapes.)

units.leftText: So they went up, and spied out the land from the wilderness of Zin to Rehob, to the entrance of Hamath.
units.rightText: So they went up and spied out the land from the Wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, toward Lebo-hamath.

units.leftText: They went up by the South, and came to Hebron; and Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the children of Anak, were there. (Now Hebron was built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.)
units.rightText: They went up through the Negev and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the descendants of Anak, dwelled. It had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.

units.leftText: They came to the valley of Eshcol, and cut down from there a branch with one cluster of grapes, and they bore it on a staff between two. They also brought some of the pomegranates and figs.
units.rightText: When they came to the Valley of Eshcol, they cut down a branch with a single cluster of grapes, which they carried on a pole between two men. They also took some pomegranates and figs.
rightNotes: 13:23 Eshcol means cluster; also in verse 24.

units.leftText: That place was called the valley of Eshcol, because of the cluster which the children of Israel cut down from there.
units.rightText: Because of the cluster of grapes the Israelites cut there, that place was called the Valley of Eshcol. The Reports of the Spies

units.leftText: They returned from spying out the land at the end of forty days.
units.rightText: After forty days the men returned from spying out the land,

units.leftText: They went and came to Moses, to Aaron, and to all the congregation of the children of Israel, to the wilderness of Paran, to Kadesh; and brought back word to them and to all the congregation. They showed them the fruit of the land.
units.rightText: and they went back to Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation of Israel in the Wilderness of Paran at Kadesh. They brought back a report for the whole congregation and showed them the fruit of the land.

units.leftText: They told him, and said, “We came to the land where you sent us. Surely it flows with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.
units.rightText: And they gave this account to Moses: “We went into the land to which you sent us, and indeed, it is flowing with milk and honey. Here is some of its fruit!

units.leftText: However, the people who dwell in the land are strong, and the cities are fortified and very large. Moreover, we saw the children of Anak there.
units.rightText: Nevertheless, the people living in the land are strong, and the cities are large and fortified. We even saw the descendants of Anak there.

units.leftText: Amalek dwells in the land of the South. The Hittite, the Jebusite, and the Amorite dwell in the hill country. The Canaanite dwells by the sea, and along the side of the Jordan.”
units.rightText: The Amalekites live in the land of the Negev; the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the hill country; and the Canaanites live by the sea and along the Jordan.”

units.leftText: Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, “Let’s go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it!”
units.rightText: Then Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said, “We must go up and take possession of the land, for we can certainly conquer it!”

units.leftText: But the men who went up with him said, “We aren’t able to go up against the people; for they are stronger than we.”
units.rightText: But the men who had gone up with him replied, “We cannot go up against the people, for they are stronger than we are!”

units.leftText: They brought up an evil report of the land which they had spied out to the children of Israel, saying, “The land, through which we have gone to spy it out, is a land that eats up its inhabitants; and all the people who we saw in it are men of great stature.
units.rightText: So they gave the Israelites a bad report about the land that they had spied out: “The land we explored devours its inhabitants, and all the people we saw there are great in stature.

units.leftText: There we saw the Nephilim, the sons of Anak, who come from the Nephilim. We were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.”
units.rightText: We even saw the Nephilim there— the descendants of Anak that come from the Nephilim! We seemed like grasshoppers in our own sight, and we must have seemed the same to them!”
leftNotes: 13:33 or, giants
13:33 or, giants

units.leftText: All the congregation lifted up their voice, and cried; and the people wept that night.
units.rightText: Then the whole congregation lifted up their voices and cried out, and that night the people wept.

units.leftText: All the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron. The whole congregation said to them, “We wish that we had died in the land of Egypt, or that we had died in this wilderness!
units.rightText: All the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole congregation said to them, “If only we had died in the land of Egypt, or if only we had died in this wilderness!

units.leftText: Why does the LORD bring us to this land, to fall by the sword? Our wives and our little ones will be captured or killed! Wouldn’t it be better for us to return into Egypt?”
units.rightText: Why is the LORD bringing us into this land to fall by the sword? Our wives and children will become plunder. Would it not be better for us to go back to Egypt?”

units.leftText: They said to one another, “Let’s choose a leader, and let’s return into Egypt.”
units.rightText: So they said to one another, “Let us appoint a leader and return to Egypt.”

units.leftText: Then Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before all the assembly of the congregation of the children of Israel.
units.rightText: Then Moses and Aaron fell facedown before the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel.

units.leftText: Joshua the son of Nun and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, who were of those who spied out the land, tore their clothes.
units.rightText: Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among those who had spied out the land, tore their clothes

units.leftText: They spoke to all the congregation of the children of Israel, saying, “The land, which we passed through to spy it out, is an exceedingly good land.
units.rightText: and said to the whole congregation of Israel, “The land we passed through and explored is an exceedingly good land.

units.leftText: If the LORD delights in us, then he will bring us into this land, and give it to us: a land which flows with milk and honey.
units.rightText: If the LORD delights in us, He will bring us into this land, a land flowing with milk and honey, and He will give it to us.

units.leftText: Only don’t rebel against the LORD, neither fear the people of the land; for they are bread for us. Their defense is removed from over them, and the LORD is with us. Don’t fear them.”
units.rightText: Only do not rebel against the LORD, and do not be afraid of the people of the land, for they will be like bread for us. Their protection has been removed, and the LORD is with us. Do not be afraid of them!”

units.leftText: But all the congregation threatened to stone them with stones. The LORD’s glory appeared in the Tent of Meeting to all the children of Israel.
units.rightText: But the whole congregation threatened to stone Joshua and Caleb.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “How long will this people despise me? How long will they not believe in me, for all the signs which I have worked among them?
units.rightText: And the LORD said to Moses, “How long will this people treat Me with contempt? How long will they refuse to believe in Me, despite all the signs I have performed among them?

units.leftText: I will strike them with the pestilence, and disinherit them, and will make of you a nation greater and mightier than they.”
units.rightText: I will strike them with a plague and destroy them — and I will make you into a nation greater and mightier than they are.” Moses Intercedes for Israel

units.leftText: Moses said to the LORD, “Then the Egyptians will hear it; for you brought up this people in your might from among them.
units.rightText: But Moses said to the LORD, “The Egyptians will hear of it, for by Your strength You brought this people from among them.

units.leftText: They will tell it to the inhabitants of this land. They have heard that you LORD are among this people; for you LORD are seen face to face, and your cloud stands over them, and you go before them, in a pillar of cloud by day, and in a pillar of fire by night.
units.rightText: And they will tell it to the inhabitants of this land. They have already heard that You, O LORD, are in the midst of this people, that You, O LORD, have been seen face to face, that Your cloud stands over them, and that You go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.

units.leftText: Now if you killed this people as one man, then the nations which have heard the fame of you will speak, saying,
units.rightText: If You kill this people as one man, the nations who have heard of Your fame will say,

units.leftText: ‘Because the LORD was not able to bring this people into the land which he swore to them, therefore he has slain them in the wilderness.’
units.rightText: ‘Because the LORD was unable to bring this people into the land He swore to give them, He has slaughtered them in the wilderness.’

units.leftText: Now please let the power of the Lord be great, according as you have spoken, saying,
units.rightText: So now I pray, may the power of my Lord be magnified, just as You have declared:
leftNotes: 14:17 The word translated “Lord” is “Adonai.”

units.leftText: ‘The LORD is slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, forgiving iniquity and disobedience; and he will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, on the third and on the fourth generation.’
units.rightText: ‘The LORD is slow to anger and abounding in loving devotion, forgiving iniquity and transgression. Yet He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished; He will visit the iniquity of the fathers upon their children to the third and fourth generation.’
rightNotes: 14:18 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: Please pardon the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of your loving kindness, and just as you have forgiven this people, from Egypt even until now.”
units.rightText: Pardon, I pray, the iniquity of this people, in keeping with the greatness of Your loving devotion, just as You have forgiven them ever since they left Egypt.” God’s Forgiveness and Judgment (Deuteronomy 1:34–40|DEU 1:34-40*)

units.leftText: The LORD said, “I have pardoned according to your word;
units.rightText: “I have pardoned them as you requested,” the LORD replied.

units.leftText: but in very deed—as I live, and as all the earth shall be filled with the LORD’s glory—
units.rightText: “Yet as surely as I live and as surely as the whole earth is filled with the glory of the LORD,

units.leftText: because all those men who have seen my glory and my signs, which I worked in Egypt and in the wilderness, yet have tempted me these ten times, and have not listened to my voice;
units.rightText: not one of the men who have seen My glory and the signs I performed in Egypt and in the wilderness — yet have tested Me and disobeyed Me these ten times —

units.leftText: surely they shall not see the land which I swore to their fathers, neither shall any of those who despised me see it.
units.rightText: not one will ever see the land that I swore to give their fathers. None of those who have treated Me with contempt will see it.

units.leftText: But my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and has followed me fully, him I will bring into the land into which he went. His offspring shall possess it.
units.rightText: But because My servant Caleb has a different spirit and has followed Me wholeheartedly, I will bring him into the land he has entered, and his descendants will inherit it.

units.leftText: Since the Amalekite and the Canaanite dwell in the valley, tomorrow turn and go into the wilderness by the way to the Red Sea.”
units.rightText: Now since the Amalekites and Canaanites are living in the valleys, turn back tomorrow and head for the wilderness along the route to the Red Sea. ”
rightNotes: 14:25 Or the Sea of Reeds

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,

units.leftText: “How long shall I bear with this evil congregation that complain against me? I have heard the complaints of the children of Israel, which they complain against me.
units.rightText: “How long will this wicked congregation grumble against Me? I have heard the complaints that the Israelites are making against Me.

units.leftText: Tell them, ‘As I live, says the LORD, surely as you have spoken in my ears, so I will do to you.
units.rightText: So tell them: As surely as I live, declares the LORD, I will do to you exactly as I heard you say.

units.leftText: Your dead bodies shall fall in this wilderness; and all who were counted of you, according to your whole number, from twenty years old and upward, who have complained against me,
units.rightText: Your bodies will fall in this wilderness— all who were numbered in the census, everyone twenty years of age or older— because you have grumbled against Me.

units.leftText: surely you shall not come into the land concerning which I swore that I would make you dwell therein, except Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.
units.rightText: Surely none of you will enter the land in which I swore to settle you, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

units.leftText: But I will bring in your little ones that you said should be captured or killed, and they shall know the land which you have rejected.
units.rightText: But I will bring your children, whom you said would become plunder, into the land you have rejected — and they will enjoy it.

units.leftText: But as for you, your dead bodies shall fall in this wilderness.
units.rightText: As for you, however, your bodies will fall in this wilderness.

units.leftText: Your children shall be wanderers in the wilderness forty years, and shall bear your prostitution, until your dead bodies are consumed in the wilderness.
units.rightText: Your children will be shepherds in the wilderness for forty years, and they will suffer for your unfaithfulness until the last of your bodies lies in the wilderness.

units.leftText: After the number of the days in which you spied out the land, even forty days, for every day a year, you will bear your iniquities, even forty years, and you will know my alienation.’
units.rightText: In keeping with the forty days you spied out the land, you shall bear your guilt forty years — a year for each day — and you will experience My alienation.

units.leftText: I, the LORD, have spoken. I will surely do this to all this evil congregation who are gathered together against me. In this wilderness they shall be consumed, and there they shall die.”
units.rightText: I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will surely do these things to this entire wicked congregation, which has conspired against Me. They will meet their end in the wilderness, and there they will die.” The Plague on the Ten Spies

units.leftText: The men whom Moses sent to spy out the land, who returned and made all the congregation to murmur against him by bringing up an evil report against the land,
units.rightText: So the men Moses had sent to spy out the land, who had returned and made the whole congregation grumble against him by bringing out a bad report about the land—

units.leftText: even those men who brought up an evil report of the land, died by the plague before the LORD.
units.rightText: those men who had brought out the bad report about the land— were struck down by a plague before the LORD.

units.leftText: But Joshua the son of Nun and Caleb the son of Jephunneh remained alive of those men who went to spy out the land.
units.rightText: Of those men who had gone to spy out the land, only Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh remained alive.

units.leftText: Moses told these words to all the children of Israel, and the people mourned greatly.
units.rightText: And when Moses relayed these words to all the Israelites, the people mourned bitterly. The Defeat at Hormah (Deuteronomy 1:41–46|DEU 1:41-46*)

units.leftText: They rose up early in the morning and went up to the top of the mountain, saying, “Behold, we are here, and will go up to the place which the LORD has promised; for we have sinned.”
units.rightText: Early the next morning they got up and went up toward the ridge of the hill country. “We have indeed sinned,” they said, “but we will go to the place the LORD has promised.”

units.leftText: Moses said, “Why now do you disobey the commandment of the LORD, since it shall not prosper?
units.rightText: But Moses said, “Why are you transgressing the commandment of the LORD? This will not succeed!

units.leftText: Don’t go up, for the LORD isn’t among you; that way you won’t be struck down before your enemies.
units.rightText: Do not go up, lest you be struck down by your enemies, because the LORD is not among you.

units.leftText: For there the Amalekite and the Canaanite are before you, and you will fall by the sword because you turned back from following the LORD; therefore the LORD will not be with you.”
units.rightText: For there the Amalekites and Canaanites will face you, and you will fall by the sword. Because you have turned away from the LORD, He will not be with you.”

units.leftText: But they presumed to go up to the top of the mountain. Nevertheless, the ark of the LORD’s covenant and Moses didn’t depart out of the camp.
units.rightText: But they dared to go up to the ridge of the hill country, though neither Moses nor the ark of the covenant of the LORD moved from the camp.

units.leftText: Then the Amalekites came down, and the Canaanites who lived in that mountain, and struck them and beat them down even to Hormah.
units.rightText: Then the Amalekites and Canaanites who lived in that part of the hill country came down, attacked them, and routed them all the way to Hormah.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘When you have come into the land of your habitations, which I give to you,
units.rightText: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: After you enter the land that I am giving you as a home

units.leftText: and will make an offering by fire to the LORD—a burnt offering, or a sacrifice, to accomplish a vow, or as a free will offering, or in your set feasts, to make a pleasant aroma to the LORD, of the herd, or of the flock—
units.rightText: and you present a food offering to the LORD from the herd or flock to produce a pleasing aroma to the LORD — either a burnt offering or a sacrifice, for a special vow or freewill offering or appointed feast—

units.leftText: then he who offers his offering shall offer to the LORD a meal offering of one tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with one fourth of a hin of oil.
units.rightText: then the one presenting his offering to the LORD shall also present a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter hin of olive oil.
leftNotes: 15:4 1 ephah is about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel
15:4 A hin is about 6.5 liters or 1.7 gallons.
rightNotes: 15:4 A tenth of an ephah is approximately 2 dry quarts or 2.2 liters (probably about 2.6 pounds or 1.2 kilograms of flour).
15:4 Or a quarter hin of oil; that is, approximately 0.97 quarts or 0.92 liters; similarly in verse 5

units.leftText: You shall prepare wine for the drink offering, one fourth of a hin, with the burnt offering or for the sacrifice, for each lamb.
units.rightText: With the burnt offering or sacrifice of each lamb, you are to prepare a quarter hin of wine as a drink offering.

units.leftText: “‘For a ram, you shall prepare for a meal offering two tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with the third part of a hin of oil;
units.rightText: With a ram you are to prepare a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a third of a hin of olive oil,
leftNotes: 15:6 1 ephah is about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel
rightNotes: 15:6 Two-tenths of an ephah is approximately 4 dry quarts or 4.4 liters (probably about 5.1 pounds or 2.3 kilograms of flour).
15:6 Or a third of a hin of oil; that is, approximately 1.3 quarts or 1.2 liters; similarly in verse 7

units.leftText: and for the drink offering you shall offer the third part of a hin of wine, of a pleasant aroma to the LORD.
units.rightText: and a third of a hin of wine as a drink offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

units.leftText: When you prepare a bull for a burnt offering or for a sacrifice, to accomplish a vow, or for peace offerings to the LORD,
units.rightText: When you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering or sacrifice to fulfill a vow or as a peace offering to the LORD,

units.leftText: then he shall offer with the bull a meal offering of three tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil;
units.rightText: present with the bull a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of olive oil.
leftNotes: 15:9 1 ephah is about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel
rightNotes: 15:9 Three-tenths of an ephah is approximately 6 dry quarts or 6.6 liters (probably about 7.6 pounds or 3.5 kilograms of flour).
15:9 Or half a hin of oil; that is, approximately 1.9 quarts or 1.8 liters; similarly in verse 10

units.leftText: and you shall offer for the drink offering half a hin of wine, for an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to the LORD.
units.rightText: Also present half a hin of wine as a drink offering. It is a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

units.leftText: Thus it shall be done for each bull, for each ram, for each of the male lambs, or of the young goats.
units.rightText: This is to be done for each bull, ram, lamb, or goat.

units.leftText: According to the number that you shall prepare, so you shall do to everyone according to their number.
units.rightText: This is how you must prepare each one, no matter how many.

units.leftText: “‘All who are native-born shall do these things in this way, in offering an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to the LORD.
units.rightText: Everyone who is native-born shall prepare these things in this way when he presents a food offering as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

units.leftText: If a stranger lives as a foreigner with you, or whoever may be among you throughout your generations, and will offer an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to the LORD, as you do, so he shall do.
units.rightText: And for the generations to come, if a foreigner residing with you or someone else among you wants to prepare a food offering as a pleasing aroma to the LORD, he is to do exactly as you do.

units.leftText: For the assembly, there shall be one statute for you and for the stranger who lives as a foreigner, a statute forever throughout your generations. As you are, so the foreigner shall be before the LORD.
units.rightText: The assembly is to have the same statute both for you and for the foreign resident; it is a permanent statute for the generations to come. You and the foreigner shall be the same before the LORD.

units.leftText: One law and one ordinance shall be for you and for the stranger who lives as a foreigner with you.’”
units.rightText: The same law and the same ordinance will apply both to you and to the foreigner residing with you.”

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘When you come into the land where I bring you,
units.rightText: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you enter the land to which I am bringing you

units.leftText: then it shall be that when you eat of the bread of the land, you shall offer up a wave offering to the LORD.
units.rightText: and you eat the food of the land, you shall lift up an offering to the LORD.

units.leftText: Of the first of your dough you shall offer up a cake for a wave offering. As the wave offering of the threshing floor, so you shall heave it.
units.rightText: From the first of your dough, you are to lift up a cake as a contribution; offer it just like an offering from the threshing floor.

units.leftText: Of the first of your dough, you shall give to the LORD a wave offering throughout your generations.
units.rightText: Throughout your generations, you are to give the LORD an offering from the first of your dough. Offerings for Unintentional Sins

units.leftText: “‘When you err, and don’t observe all these commandments which the LORD has spoken to Moses—
units.rightText: Now if you stray unintentionally and do not obey all these commandments that the LORD has spoken to Moses—

units.leftText: even all that the LORD has commanded you by Moses, from the day that the LORD gave commandment and onward throughout your generations—
units.rightText: all that the LORD has commanded you through Moses from the day the LORD gave them and continuing through the generations to come—

units.leftText: then it shall be, if it was done unwittingly, without the knowledge of the congregation, that all the congregation shall offer one young bull for a burnt offering, for a pleasant aroma to the LORD, with its meal offering and its drink offering, according to the ordinance, and one male goat for a sin offering.
units.rightText: and if it was done unintentionally without the knowledge of the congregation, then the whole congregation is to prepare one young bull as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD, with its grain offering and drink offering according to the regulation, and one male goat as a sin offering.

units.leftText: The priest shall make atonement for all the congregation of the children of Israel, and they shall be forgiven; for it was an error, and they have brought their offering, an offering made by fire to the LORD, and their sin offering before the LORD, for their error.
units.rightText: The priest is to make atonement for the whole congregation of Israel, so that they may be forgiven; for the sin was unintentional and they have brought to the LORD a food offering and a sin offering, presented before the LORD for their unintentional sin.

units.leftText: All the congregation of the children of Israel shall be forgiven, as well as the stranger who lives as a foreigner among them; for with regard to all the people, it was done unwittingly.
units.rightText: Then the whole congregation of Israel and the foreigners residing among them will be forgiven, since it happened to all the people unintentionally.

units.leftText: “‘If a person sins unwittingly, then he shall offer a female goat a year old for a sin offering.
units.rightText: Also, if one person sins unintentionally, he is to present a year-old female goat as a sin offering.

units.leftText: The priest shall make atonement for the soul who errs when he sins unwittingly before the LORD. He shall make atonement for him; and he shall be forgiven.
units.rightText: And the priest shall make atonement before the LORD on behalf of the person who erred by sinning unintentionally; and when atonement has been made for him, he will be forgiven.

units.leftText: You shall have one law for him who does anything unwittingly, for him who is native-born among the children of Israel, and for the stranger who lives as a foreigner among them.
units.rightText: You shall have the same law for the one who acts in error, whether he is a native-born Israelite or a foreigner residing among you.

units.leftText: “‘But the soul who does anything with a high hand, whether he is native-born or a foreigner, blasphemes the LORD. That soul shall be cut off from among his people.
units.rightText: But the person who sins defiantly, whether a native or foreigner, blasphemes the LORD. That person shall be cut off from among his people.

units.leftText: Because he has despised the LORD’s word, and has broken his commandment, that soul shall be utterly cut off. His iniquity shall be on him.’”
units.rightText: He shall certainly be cut off, because he has despised the word of the LORD and broken His commandment; his guilt remains on him.” A Sabbath-Breaker Stoned (Exodus 31:12–17|EXO 31:12-17*)

units.leftText: While the children of Israel were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering sticks on the Sabbath day.
units.rightText: While the Israelites were in the wilderness, a man was found gathering wood on the Sabbath day.

units.leftText: Those who found him gathering sticks brought him to Moses and Aaron, and to all the congregation.
units.rightText: Those who found the man gathering wood brought him to Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation,

units.leftText: They put him in custody, because it had not been declared what should be done to him.
units.rightText: and because it had not been declared what should be done to him, they placed him in custody.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “The man shall surely be put to death. All the congregation shall stone him with stones outside of the camp.”
units.rightText: And the LORD said to Moses, “The man must surely be put to death. The whole congregation is to stone him outside the camp.”

units.leftText: All the congregation brought him outside of the camp, and stoned him to death with stones, as the LORD commanded Moses.
units.rightText: So the whole congregation took the man outside the camp and stoned him to death, as the LORD had commanded Moses. The Law of Tassels

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: And the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them that they should make themselves fringes on the borders of their garments throughout their generations, and that they put on the fringe of each border a cord of blue.
units.rightText: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them that throughout the generations to come they are to make for themselves tassels for the corners of their garments, with a blue cord on each tassel.
leftNotes: 15:38 or, tassels (Hebrew צִיצִ֛ת)
15:38 or, tassel

units.leftText: It shall be to you for a fringe, that you may see it, and remember all the LORD’s commandments, and do them; and that you don’t follow your own heart and your own eyes, after which you used to play the prostitute;
units.rightText: These will serve as tassels for you to look at, so that you may remember all the commandments of the LORD, that you may obey them and not prostitute yourselves by following your own heart and your own eyes.
leftNotes: 15:39 or, tassel

units.leftText: so that you may remember and do all my commandments, and be holy to your God.
units.rightText: Then you will remember and obey all My commandments, and you will be holy to your God.

units.leftText: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God: I am the LORD your God.”
units.rightText: I am the LORD your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD your God.”

units.leftText: Now Korah, the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, with Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On, the son of Peleth, sons of Reuben, took some men.
units.rightText: Now Korah son of Izhar, the son of Kohath son of Levi, along with some Reubenites — Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth — conducted

units.leftText: They rose up before Moses, with some of the children of Israel, two hundred fifty princes of the congregation, called to the assembly, men of renown.
units.rightText: a rebellion against Moses, along with 250 men of Israel renowned as leaders of the congregation and representatives in the assembly.

units.leftText: They assembled themselves together against Moses and against Aaron, and said to them, “You take too much on yourself, since all the congregation are holy, everyone of them, and the LORD is among them! Why do you lift yourselves up above the LORD’s assembly?”
units.rightText: They came together against Moses and Aaron and told them, “You have taken too much upon yourselves! For everyone in the entire congregation is holy, and the LORD is in their midst. Why then do you exalt yourselves above the assembly of the LORD?”
rightNotes: 16:3 Figuratively You have gone too far or You have appropriated too much authority to yourselves; similarly in verse 7

units.leftText: When Moses heard it, he fell on his face.
units.rightText: When Moses heard this, he fell facedown.

units.leftText: He said to Korah and to all his company, “In the morning, the LORD will show who are his, and who is holy, and will cause him to come near to him. Even him whom he shall choose, he will cause to come near to him.
units.rightText: Then he said to Korah and all his followers, “Tomorrow morning the LORD will reveal who belongs to Him and who is holy, and He will bring that person near to Himself. The one He chooses He will bring near to Himself.
rightNotes: 16:5 LXX God has visited and knows those who are His; cited in 2 Timothy 2:19|2TI 2:19*

units.leftText: Do this: have Korah and all his company take censers,
units.rightText: You, Korah, and all your followers are to do as follows: Take censers,

units.leftText: put fire in them, and put incense on them before the LORD tomorrow. It shall be that the man whom the LORD chooses, he shall be holy. You have gone too far, you sons of Levi!”
units.rightText: and tomorrow you are to place fire and incense in them in the presence of the LORD. Then the man the LORD chooses will be the one who is holy. It is you sons of Levi who have taken too much upon yourselves!”

units.leftText: Moses said to Korah, “Hear now, you sons of Levi!
units.rightText: Moses also said to Korah, “Now listen, you sons of Levi!

units.leftText: Is it a small thing to you that the God of Israel has separated you from the congregation of Israel, to bring you near to himself, to do the service of the LORD’s tabernacle, and to stand before the congregation to minister to them;
units.rightText: Is it not enough for you that the God of Israel has separated you from the congregation of Israel and brought you near to Himself to perform the work at the LORD’s tabernacle, and to stand before the congregation to minister to them?

units.leftText: and that he has brought you near, and all your brothers the sons of Levi with you? Do you seek the priesthood also?
units.rightText: He has brought you near, you and all your fellow Levites, but you are seeking the priesthood as well.

units.leftText: Therefore you and all your company have gathered together against the LORD! What is Aaron that you complain against him?”
units.rightText: Therefore, it is you and all your followers who have conspired against the LORD! As for Aaron, who is he that you should grumble against him?”

units.leftText: Moses sent to call Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab; and they said, “We won’t come up!
units.rightText: Then Moses summoned Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, but they said, “We will not come!

units.leftText: Is it a small thing that you have brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey, to kill us in the wilderness, but you must also make yourself a prince over us?
units.rightText: Is it not enough that you have brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness? Must you also appoint yourself as ruler over us?

units.leftText: Moreover you haven’t brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, nor given us inheritance of fields and vineyards. Will you put out the eyes of these men? We won’t come up.”
units.rightText: Moreover, you have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey or given us an inheritance of fields and vineyards. Will you gouge out the eyes of these men? No, we will not come!”

units.leftText: Moses was very angry, and said to the LORD, “Don’t respect their offering. I have not taken one donkey from them, neither have I hurt one of them.”
units.rightText: Then Moses became very angry and said to the LORD, “Do not regard their offering. I have not taken one donkey from them or mistreated a single one of them.”

units.leftText: Moses said to Korah, “You and all your company go before the LORD, you, and they, and Aaron, tomorrow.
units.rightText: And Moses said to Korah, “You and all your followers are to appear before the LORD tomorrow— you and they and Aaron.

units.leftText: Each man take his censer and put incense on it, and each man bring before the LORD his censer, two hundred fifty censers; you also, and Aaron, each with his censer.”
units.rightText: Each man is to take his censer, place incense in it, and present it before the LORD— 250 censers. You and Aaron are to present your censers as well.”

units.leftText: They each took his censer, and put fire in it, and laid incense on it, and stood at the door of the Tent of Meeting with Moses and Aaron.
units.rightText: So each man took his censer, put fire and incense in it, and stood with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

units.leftText: Korah assembled all the congregation opposite them to the door of the Tent of Meeting. The LORD’s glory appeared to all the congregation.
units.rightText: When Korah had gathered his whole assembly against them at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, the glory of the LORD appeared to the whole congregation.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
units.rightText: And the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,

units.leftText: “Separate yourselves from among this congregation, that I may consume them in a moment!”
units.rightText: “Separate yourselves from this congregation so that I may consume them in an instant.”

units.leftText: They fell on their faces, and said, “God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and will you be angry with all the congregation?”
units.rightText: But Moses and Aaron fell facedown and said, “O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, when one man sins, will You be angry with the whole congregation?” Moses Separates the People

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Speak to the congregation, saying, ‘Get away from around the tent of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram!’”
units.rightText: “Tell the congregation to move away from the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.”

units.leftText: Moses rose up and went to Dathan and Abiram; and the elders of Israel followed him.
units.rightText: So Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel followed him.

units.leftText: He spoke to the congregation, saying, “Depart, please, from the tents of these wicked men, and touch nothing of theirs, lest you be consumed in all their sins!”
units.rightText: And he warned the congregation, “Move away now from the tents of these wicked men. Do not touch anything that belongs to them, or you will be swept away because of all their sins.”

units.leftText: So they went away from the tent of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram, on every side. Dathan and Abiram came out, and stood at the door of their tents with their wives, their sons, and their little ones.
units.rightText: So they moved away from the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Meanwhile, Dathan and Abiram had come out and stood at the entrances to their tents with their wives and children and infants. The Earth Swallows Korah

units.leftText: Moses said, “Hereby you shall know that the LORD has sent me to do all these works; for they are not from my own mind.
units.rightText: Then Moses said, “This is how you will know that the LORD has sent me to do all these things, for it was not my own doing:

units.leftText: If these men die the common death of all men, or if they experience what all men experience, then the LORD hasn’t sent me.
units.rightText: If these men die a natural death, or if they suffer the fate of all men, then the LORD has not sent me.

units.leftText: But if the LORD makes a new thing, and the ground opens its mouth, and swallows them up with all that belong to them, and they go down alive into Sheol, then you shall understand that these men have despised the LORD.”
units.rightText: But if the LORD brings about something unprecedented, and the earth opens its mouth and swallows them and all that belongs to them so that they go down alive into Sheol, then you will know that these men have treated the LORD with contempt.”
leftNotes: 16:30 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: As he finished speaking all these words, the ground that was under them split apart.
units.rightText: As soon as Moses had finished saying all this, the ground beneath them split open,

units.leftText: The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up with their households, all of Korah’s men, and all their goods.
units.rightText: and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households — all Korah’s men and all their possessions.

units.leftText: So they, and all that belonged to them went down alive into Sheol. The earth closed on them, and they perished from among the assembly.
units.rightText: They went down alive into Sheol with all they owned. The earth closed over them, and they vanished from the assembly.
leftNotes: 16:33 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: All Israel that were around them fled at their cry; for they said, “Lest the earth swallow us up!”
units.rightText: At their cries, all the people of Israel who were around them fled, saying, “The earth may swallow us too!”

units.leftText: Fire came out from the LORD, and devoured the two hundred fifty men who offered the incense.
units.rightText: And fire came forth from the LORD and consumed the 250 men who were offering the incense. The Censers Reserved for Holy Use

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Speak to Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, that he take up the censers out of the burning, and scatter the fire away from the camp; for they are holy,
units.rightText: “Tell Eleazar son of Aaron the priest to remove the censers from the flames and to scatter the coals far away, because the censers are holy.

units.leftText: even the censers of those who sinned against their own lives. Let them be beaten into plates for a covering of the altar, for they offered them before the LORD. Therefore they are holy. They shall be a sign to the children of Israel.”
units.rightText: As for the censers of those who sinned at the cost of their own lives, hammer them into sheets to overlay the altar, for these were presented before the LORD, and so have become holy. They will serve as a sign to the Israelites.”

units.leftText: Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers which those who were burned had offered; and they beat them out for a covering of the altar,
units.rightText: So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers brought by those who had been burned up, and he had them hammered out to overlay the altar,

units.leftText: to be a memorial to the children of Israel, to the end that no stranger who isn’t of the offspring of Aaron, would come near to burn incense before the LORD, that he not be as Korah and as his company; as the LORD spoke to him by Moses.
units.rightText: just as the LORD commanded him through Moses. This was to be a reminder to the Israelites that no outsider who is not a descendant of Aaron should approach to offer incense before the LORD, lest he become like Korah and his followers. Murmuring and Plague (1 Corinthians 10:1–13|1CO 10:1-13*)
