units.leftText: But on the next day all the congregation of the children of Israel complained against Moses and against Aaron, saying, “You have killed the LORD’s people!”
units.rightText: The next day the whole congregation of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron, saying, “You have killed the LORD’s people!”

units.leftText: When the congregation was assembled against Moses and against Aaron, they looked toward the Tent of Meeting. Behold, the cloud covered it, and the LORD’s glory appeared.
units.rightText: But when the congregation gathered against them, Moses and Aaron turned toward the Tent of Meeting, and suddenly the cloud covered it and the glory of the LORD appeared.

units.leftText: Moses and Aaron came to the front of the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: Then Moses and Aaron went to the front of the Tent of Meeting,

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: and the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Get away from among this congregation, that I may consume them in a moment!” They fell on their faces.
units.rightText: “Get away from this congregation so that I may consume them in an instant.” And Moses and Aaron fell facedown.

units.leftText: Moses said to Aaron, “Take your censer, put fire from the altar in it, lay incense on it, carry it quickly to the congregation, and make atonement for them; for wrath has gone out from the LORD! The plague has begun.”
units.rightText: Moses said to Aaron, “Take your censer, place fire from the altar in it, and add incense. Go quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them, because wrath has come out from the LORD; the plague has begun.”

units.leftText: Aaron did as Moses said, and ran into the middle of the assembly. The plague had already begun among the people. He put on the incense, and made atonement for the people.
units.rightText: So Aaron took the censer as Moses had ordered and ran into the midst of the assembly. And seeing that the plague had begun among the people, he offered the incense and made atonement for the people.

units.leftText: He stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed.
units.rightText: He stood between the living and the dead, and the plague was halted.

units.leftText: Now those who died by the plague were fourteen thousand seven hundred, in addition to those who died about the matter of Korah.
units.rightText: But those who died from the plague numbered 14,700, in addition to those who had died on account of Korah.

units.leftText: Aaron returned to Moses to the door of the Tent of Meeting, and the plague was stopped.
units.rightText: Then Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, since the plague had been halted.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: And the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Speak to the children of Israel, and take rods from them, one for each fathers’ house, of all their princes according to their fathers’ houses, twelve rods. Write each man’s name on his rod.
units.rightText: “Speak to the Israelites and take from them twelve staffs, one from the leader of each tribe. Write each man’s name on his staff,

units.leftText: You shall write Aaron’s name on Levi’s rod. There shall be one rod for each head of their fathers’ houses.
units.rightText: and write Aaron’s name on the staff of Levi, because there must be one staff for the head of each tribe.

units.leftText: You shall lay them up in the Tent of Meeting before the covenant, where I meet with you.
units.rightText: Place the staffs in the Tent of Meeting in front of the Testimony, where I meet with you.
rightNotes: 17:4 The Testimony refers to the stone tablets in the ark of the covenant inscribed with the Ten Commandments; also in verse 10.

units.leftText: It shall happen that the rod of the man whom I shall choose shall bud. I will make the murmurings of the children of Israel, which they murmur against you, cease from me.”
units.rightText: The staff belonging to the man I choose will sprout, and I will rid Myself of the constant grumbling of the Israelites against you.”

units.leftText: Moses spoke to the children of Israel; and all their princes gave him rods, for each prince one, according to their fathers’ houses, a total of twelve rods. Aaron’s rod was among their rods.
units.rightText: So Moses spoke to the Israelites, and each of their leaders gave him a staff — one for each of the leaders of their tribes, twelve staffs in all. And Aaron’s staff was among them.

units.leftText: Moses laid up the rods before the LORD in the Tent of the Testimony.
units.rightText: Then Moses placed the staffs before the LORD in the Tent of the Testimony.

units.leftText: On the next day, Moses went into the Tent of the Testimony; and behold, Aaron’s rod for the house of Levi had sprouted, budded, produced blossoms, and bore ripe almonds.
units.rightText: The next day Moses entered the Tent of the Testimony and saw that Aaron’s staff, representing the house of Levi, had sprouted, put forth buds, blossomed, and produced almonds.

units.leftText: Moses brought out all the rods from before the LORD to all the children of Israel. They looked, and each man took his rod.
units.rightText: Then Moses brought out all the staffs from the LORD’s presence to all the Israelites. They saw them, and each man took his own staff.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “Put back the rod of Aaron before the covenant, to be kept for a token against the children of rebellion; that you may make an end of their complaining against me, that they not die.”
units.rightText: The LORD said to Moses, “Put Aaron’s staff back in front of the Testimony, to be kept as a sign for the rebellious, so that you may put an end to their grumbling against Me, lest they die.”

units.leftText: Moses did so. As the LORD commanded him, so he did.
units.rightText: So Moses did as the LORD had commanded him.

units.leftText: The children of Israel spoke to Moses, saying, “Behold, we perish! We are undone! We are all undone!
units.rightText: Then the Israelites declared to Moses, “Look, we are perishing! We are lost; we are all lost!

units.leftText: Everyone who keeps approaching the LORD’s tabernacle, dies! Will we all perish?”
units.rightText: Anyone who comes near the tabernacle of the LORD will die. Are we all going to perish?”

units.leftText: The LORD said to Aaron, “You and your sons and your fathers’ house with you shall bear the iniquity of the sanctuary; and you and your sons with you shall bear the iniquity of your priesthood.
units.rightText: So the LORD said to Aaron, “You and your sons and your father’s house must bear the iniquity involving the sanctuary. And you and your sons alone must bear the iniquity involving your priesthood.

units.leftText: Bring your brothers also, the tribe of Levi, the tribe of your father, near with you, that they may be joined to you, and minister to you; but you and your sons with you shall be before the Tent of the Testimony.
units.rightText: But bring with you also your brothers from the tribe of Levi, the tribe of your father, that they may join you and assist you and your sons before the Tent of the Testimony.

units.leftText: They shall keep your commands and the duty of the whole Tent; only they shall not come near to the vessels of the sanctuary and to the altar, that they not die, neither they nor you.
units.rightText: And they shall attend to your duties and to all the duties of the Tent; but they must not come near to the furnishings of the sanctuary or the altar, or both they and you will die.

units.leftText: They shall be joined to you and keep the responsibility of the Tent of Meeting, for all the service of the Tent. A stranger shall not come near to you.
units.rightText: They are to join you and attend to the duties of the Tent of Meeting, doing all the work at the Tent; but no outsider may come near you.

units.leftText: “You shall perform the duty of the sanctuary and the duty of the altar, that there be no more wrath on the children of Israel.
units.rightText: And you shall attend to the duties of the sanctuary and of the altar, so that wrath may not fall on the Israelites again.

units.leftText: Behold, I myself have taken your brothers the Levites from among the children of Israel. They are a gift to you, dedicated to the LORD, to do the service of the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: Behold, I Myself have selected your fellow Levites from the Israelites as a gift to you, dedicated to the LORD to perform the service for the Tent of Meeting.

units.leftText: You and your sons with you shall keep your priesthood for everything of the altar, and for that within the veil. You shall serve. I give you the service of the priesthood as a gift. The stranger who comes near shall be put to death.”
units.rightText: But only you and your sons shall attend to your priesthood for everything concerning the altar and what is inside the veil, and you are to perform that service. I am giving you the work of the priesthood as a gift, but any outsider who comes near the sanctuary must be put to death.” Offerings for Priests and Levites

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Aaron, “Behold, I myself have given you the command of my wave offerings, even all the holy things of the children of Israel. I have given them to you by reason of the anointing, and to your sons, as a portion forever.
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Aaron, “Behold, I have put you in charge of My offerings. As for all the sacred offerings of the Israelites, I have given them to you and your sons as a portion and a permanent statute.

units.leftText: This shall be yours of the most holy things from the fire: every offering of theirs, even every meal offering of theirs, and every sin offering of theirs, and every trespass offering of theirs, which they shall give to me, shall be most holy for you and for your sons.
units.rightText: A portion of the most holy offerings reserved from the fire will be yours. From all the offerings they render to Me as most holy offerings, whether grain offerings or sin offerings or guilt offerings, that part belongs to you and your sons.

units.leftText: You shall eat of it like the most holy things. Every male shall eat of it. It shall be holy to you.
units.rightText: You are to eat it as a most holy offering, and every male may eat it. You shall regard it as holy.
rightNotes: 18:10 Or You are to eat it in a most holy place

units.leftText: “This is yours, too: the wave offering of their gift, even all the wave offerings of the children of Israel. I have given them to you, and to your sons and to your daughters with you, as a portion forever. Everyone who is clean in your house shall eat of it.
units.rightText: And this is yours as well: the offering of their gifts, along with all the wave offerings of the Israelites. I have given this to you and your sons and daughters as a permanent statute. Every ceremonially clean person in your household may eat it.

units.leftText: “I have given to you all the best of the oil, all the best of the vintage, and of the grain, the first fruits of them which they give to the LORD.
units.rightText: I give you all the freshest olive oil and all the finest new wine and grain that the Israelites give to the LORD as their firstfruits.

units.leftText: The first-ripe fruits of all that is in their land, which they bring to the LORD, shall be yours. Everyone who is clean in your house shall eat of it.
units.rightText: The firstfruits of everything in their land that they bring to the LORD will belong to you. Every ceremonially clean person in your household may eat them.

units.leftText: “Everything devoted in Israel shall be yours.
units.rightText: Every devoted thing in Israel belongs to you.

units.leftText: Everything that opens the womb, of all flesh which they offer to the LORD, both of man and animal, shall be yours. Nevertheless, you shall surely redeem the firstborn of man, and you shall redeem the firstborn of unclean animals.
units.rightText: The firstborn of every womb, whether man or beast, that is offered to the LORD belongs to you. But you must surely redeem every firstborn son and every firstborn male of unclean animals.

units.leftText: You shall redeem those who are to be redeemed of them from a month old, according to your estimation, for five shekels of money, according to the shekel of the sanctuary, which weighs twenty gerahs.
units.rightText: You are to pay the redemption price for a month-old male according to your valuation: five shekels of silver, according to the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty gerahs.
leftNotes: 18:16 A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces.
18:16 A gerah is about 0.5 grams or about 7.7 grains.
rightNotes: 18:16 5 shekels is approximately 2 ounces or 57 grams of silver.
18:16 20 gerahs is equivalent to one shekel (approximately 0.4 ounces or 11.4 grams).

units.leftText: “But you shall not redeem the firstborn of a cow, or the firstborn of a sheep, or the firstborn of a goat. They are holy. You shall sprinkle their blood on the altar, and shall burn their fat for an offering made by fire, for a pleasant aroma to the LORD.
units.rightText: But you must not redeem the firstborn of an ox, a sheep, or a goat; they are holy. You are to splatter their blood on the altar and burn their fat as a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

units.leftText: Their meat shall be yours, as the wave offering breast and as the right thigh, it shall be yours.
units.rightText: And their meat belongs to you, just as the breast and right thigh of the wave offering belong to you.

units.leftText: All the wave offerings of the holy things which the children of Israel offer to the LORD, I have given you and your sons and your daughters with you, as a portion forever. It is a covenant of salt forever before the LORD to you and to your offspring with you.”
units.rightText: All the holy offerings that the Israelites present to the LORD I give to you and to your sons and daughters as a permanent statute. It is a permanent covenant of salt before the LORD for you and your offspring.”
rightNotes: 18:19 That is, a perpetual covenant

units.leftText: The LORD said to Aaron, “You shall have no inheritance in their land, neither shall you have any portion among them. I am your portion and your inheritance among the children of Israel.
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Aaron, “You will have no inheritance in their land, nor will you have any portion among them. I am your portion and your inheritance among the Israelites.

units.leftText: “To the children of Levi, behold, I have given all the tithe in Israel for an inheritance, in return for their service which they serve, even the service of the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: Behold, I have given to the Levites all the tithes in Israel as an inheritance in return for the work they do, the service of the Tent of Meeting.

units.leftText: Henceforth the children of Israel shall not come near the Tent of Meeting, lest they bear sin, and die.
units.rightText: No longer may the Israelites come near to the Tent of Meeting, or they will incur guilt and die.

units.leftText: But the Levites shall do the service of the Tent of Meeting, and they shall bear their iniquity. It shall be a statute forever throughout your generations. Among the children of Israel, they shall have no inheritance.
units.rightText: The Levites are to perform the work of the Tent of Meeting, and they must bear their iniquity. This is a permanent statute for the generations to come. The Levites will not receive an inheritance among the Israelites.

units.leftText: For the tithe of the children of Israel, which they offer as a wave offering to the LORD, I have given to the Levites for an inheritance. Therefore I have said to them, ‘Among the children of Israel they shall have no inheritance.’”
units.rightText: For I have given to the Levites as their inheritance the tithe that the Israelites present to the LORD as a contribution. That is why I told them that they would not receive an inheritance among the Israelites.”

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: And the LORD instructed Moses,

units.leftText: “Moreover you shall speak to the Levites, and tell them, ‘When you take of the children of Israel the tithe which I have given you from them for your inheritance, then you shall offer up a wave offering of it for the LORD, a tithe of the tithe.
units.rightText: “Speak to the Levites and tell them: ‘When you receive from the Israelites the tithe that I have given you as your inheritance, you must present part of it as an offering to the LORD— a tithe of the tithe.

units.leftText: Your wave offering shall be credited to you, as though it were the grain of the threshing floor, and as the fullness of the wine press.
units.rightText: Your offering will be reckoned to you as grain from the threshing floor or juice from the winepress.

units.leftText: Thus you also shall offer a wave offering to the LORD of all your tithes, which you receive of the children of Israel; and of it you shall give the LORD’s wave offering to Aaron the priest.
units.rightText: So you are to present an offering to the LORD from all the tithes you receive from the Israelites, and from these you are to give the LORD’s offering to Aaron the priest.

units.leftText: Out of all your gifts, you shall offer every wave offering to the LORD, of all its best parts, even the holy part of it.’
units.rightText: You must present the offering due the LORD from all the best of every gift, the holiest part of it.’

units.leftText: “Therefore you shall tell them, ‘When you heave its best from it, then it shall be credited to the Levites as the increase of the threshing floor, and as the increase of the wine press.
units.rightText: Therefore say to the Levites, ‘When you have presented the best part, it will be reckoned to you as the produce of the threshing floor or winepress.

units.leftText: You may eat it anywhere, you and your households, for it is your reward in return for your service in the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: And you and your households may eat the rest of it anywhere; it is the compensation for your work at the Tent of Meeting.

units.leftText: You shall bear no sin by reason of it, when you have heaved from it its best. You shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel, that you not die.’”
units.rightText: Once you have presented the best part of it, you will not incur guilt because of it. But you must not defile the sacred offerings of the Israelites, or else you will die.’”

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,

units.leftText: “This is the statute of the law which the LORD has commanded. Tell the children of Israel to bring you a red heifer without spot, in which is no defect, and which was never yoked.
units.rightText: “This is the statute of the law that the LORD has commanded: Instruct the Israelites to bring you an unblemished red heifer that has no defect and has never been placed under a yoke.

units.leftText: You shall give her to Eleazar the priest, and he shall bring her outside of the camp, and one shall kill her before his face.
units.rightText: Give it to Eleazar the priest, and he will have it brought outside the camp and slaughtered in his presence.

units.leftText: Eleazar the priest shall take some of her blood with his finger, and sprinkle her blood toward the front of the Tent of Meeting seven times.
units.rightText: Eleazar the priest is to take some of its blood on his finger and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the Tent of Meeting.

units.leftText: One shall burn the heifer in his sight; her skin, and her meat, and her blood, with her dung, shall he burn.
units.rightText: Then the heifer must be burned in his sight. Its hide, its flesh, and its blood are to be burned, along with its dung.

units.leftText: The priest shall take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet, and cast it into the middle of the burning of the heifer.
units.rightText: The priest is to take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet wool and throw them onto the burning heifer.

units.leftText: Then the priest shall wash his clothes, and he shall bathe his flesh in water, and afterward he shall come into the camp, and the priest shall be unclean until the evening.
units.rightText: Then the priest must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water; after that he may enter the camp, but he will be ceremonially unclean until evening.

units.leftText: He who burns her shall wash his clothes in water, and bathe his flesh in water, and shall be unclean until the evening.
units.rightText: The one who burned the heifer must also wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and he too will be ceremonially unclean until evening.

units.leftText: “A man who is clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer, and lay them up outside of the camp in a clean place; and it shall be kept for the congregation of the children of Israel for use in water for cleansing impurity. It is a sin offering.
units.rightText: Then a man who is ceremonially clean is to gather up the ashes of the heifer and store them in a ceremonially clean place outside the camp. They must be kept by the congregation of Israel for preparing the water of purification; this is for purification from sin.

units.leftText: He who gathers the ashes of the heifer shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the evening. It shall be to the children of Israel, and to the stranger who lives as a foreigner among them, for a statute forever.
units.rightText: The man who has gathered up the ashes of the heifer must also wash his clothes, and he will be ceremonially unclean until evening. This is a permanent statute for the Israelites and for the foreigner residing among them. Purification of the Unclean

units.leftText: “He who touches the dead body of any man shall be unclean seven days.
units.rightText: Whoever touches any dead body will be unclean for seven days.

units.leftText: He shall purify himself with water on the third day, and on the seventh day he shall be clean; but if he doesn’t purify himself the third day, then the seventh day he shall not be clean.
units.rightText: He must purify himself with the water on the third day and on the seventh day; then he will be clean. But if he does not purify himself on the third and seventh days, he will not be clean.

units.leftText: Whoever touches a dead person, the body of a man who has died, and doesn’t purify himself, defiles the LORD’s tabernacle; and that soul shall be cut off from Israel; because the water for impurity was not sprinkled on him, he shall be unclean. His uncleanness is yet on him.
units.rightText: Anyone who touches a human corpse and fails to purify himself defiles the tabernacle of the LORD. That person must be cut off from Israel. He remains unclean, because the water of purification has not been sprinkled on him, and his uncleanness is still on him.

units.leftText: “This is the law when a man dies in a tent: everyone who comes into the tent, and everyone who is in the tent, shall be unclean seven days.
units.rightText: This is the law when a person dies in a tent: Everyone who enters the tent and everyone already in the tent will be unclean for seven days,

units.leftText: Every open vessel, which has no covering bound on it, is unclean.
units.rightText: and any open container without a lid fastened on it is unclean.

units.leftText: “Whoever in the open field touches one who is slain with a sword, or a dead body, or a bone of a man, or a grave, shall be unclean seven days.
units.rightText: Anyone in the open field who touches someone who has been killed by the sword or has died of natural causes, or anyone who touches a human bone or a grave, will be unclean for seven days.

units.leftText: “For the unclean, they shall take of the ashes of the burning of the sin offering; and running water shall be poured on them in a vessel.
units.rightText: For the purification of the unclean person, take some of the ashes of the burnt sin offering, put them in a jar, and pour fresh water over them.
rightNotes: 19:17 Or flowing water or living water

units.leftText: A clean person shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it on the tent, on all the vessels, on the persons who were there, and on him who touched the bone, or the slain, or the dead, or the grave.
units.rightText: Then a man who is ceremonially clean is to take some hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle the tent, all the furnishings, and the people who were there. He is also to sprinkle the one who touched a bone, a grave, or a person who has died or been slain.

units.leftText: The clean person shall sprinkle on the unclean on the third day, and on the seventh day. On the seventh day, he shall purify him. He shall wash his clothes and bathe himself in water, and shall be clean at evening.
units.rightText: The man who is ceremonially clean is to sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. After he purifies the unclean person on the seventh day, the one being cleansed must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and that evening he will be clean.

units.leftText: But the man who shall be unclean, and shall not purify himself, that soul shall be cut off from among the assembly, because he has defiled the sanctuary of the LORD. The water for impurity has not been sprinkled on him. He is unclean.
units.rightText: But if a person who is unclean does not purify himself, he will be cut off from the assembly, because he has defiled the sanctuary of the LORD. The water of purification has not been sprinkled on him; he is unclean.

units.leftText: It shall be a perpetual statute to them. He who sprinkles the water for impurity shall wash his clothes, and he who touches the water for impurity shall be unclean until evening.
units.rightText: This is a permanent statute for the people: The one who sprinkles the water of purification must wash his clothes, and whoever touches the water of purification will be unclean until evening.

units.leftText: “Whatever the unclean person touches shall be unclean; and the soul that touches it shall be unclean until evening.”
units.rightText: Anything the unclean person touches will become unclean, and anyone who touches it will be unclean until evening.”

units.leftText: The children of Israel, even the whole congregation, came into the wilderness of Zin in the first month. The people stayed in Kadesh. Miriam died there, and was buried there.
units.rightText: In the first month, the whole congregation of Israel entered the Wilderness of Zin and stayed in Kadesh. There Miriam died and was buried.

units.leftText: There was no water for the congregation; and they assembled themselves together against Moses and against Aaron.
units.rightText: Now there was no water for the congregation, so they gathered against Moses and Aaron.

units.leftText: The people quarreled with Moses, and spoke, saying, “We wish that we had died when our brothers died before the LORD!
units.rightText: The people quarreled with Moses and said, “If only we had perished with our brothers before the LORD!

units.leftText: Why have you brought the LORD’s assembly into this wilderness, that we should die there, we and our animals?
units.rightText: Why have you brought the LORD’s assembly into this wilderness for us and our livestock to die here?

units.leftText: Why have you made us to come up out of Egypt, to bring us in to this evil place? It is no place of seed, or of figs, or of vines, or of pomegranates; neither is there any water to drink.”
units.rightText: Why have you led us up out of Egypt to bring us to this wretched place? It is not a place of grain, figs, vines, or pomegranates — and there is no water to drink!”

units.leftText: Moses and Aaron went from the presence of the assembly to the door of the Tent of Meeting, and fell on their faces. The LORD’s glory appeared to them.
units.rightText: Then Moses and Aaron went from the presence of the assembly to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. They fell facedown, and the glory of the LORD appeared to them.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: And the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Take the rod, and assemble the congregation, you, and Aaron your brother, and speak to the rock before their eyes, that it pour out its water. You shall bring water to them out of the rock; so you shall give the congregation and their livestock drink.”
units.rightText: “Take the staff and assemble the congregation. You and your brother Aaron are to speak to the rock while they watch, and it will pour out its water. You will bring out water from the rock and provide drink for the congregation and their livestock.”

units.leftText: Moses took the rod from before the LORD, as he commanded him.
units.rightText: So Moses took the staff from the LORD’s presence, just as he had been commanded.

units.leftText: Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly together before the rock, and he said to them, “Hear now, you rebels! Shall we bring water out of this rock for you?”
units.rightText: Then Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly in front of the rock, and Moses said to them, “Listen now, you rebels, must we bring you water out of this rock?”

units.leftText: Moses lifted up his hand, and struck the rock with his rod twice, and water came out abundantly. The congregation and their livestock drank.
units.rightText: Then Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff, so that a great amount of water gushed out, and the congregation and their livestock were able to drink.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you didn’t believe in me, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore you shall not bring this assembly into the land which I have given them.”
units.rightText: But the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you did not trust Me to show My holiness in the sight of the Israelites, you will not bring this assembly into the land that I have given them.”

units.leftText: These are the waters of Meribah; because the children of Israel strove with the LORD, and he was sanctified in them.
units.rightText: These were the waters of Meribah, where the Israelites quarreled with the LORD, and He showed His holiness among them. Edom Refuses Passage
leftNotes: 20:13 “Meribah” means “quarreling”.
rightNotes: 20:13 Meribah means quarreling; also in verse 24; see Exodus 17:7|EXO 17:7*.

units.leftText: Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom, saying: “Your brother Israel says: You know all the travail that has happened to us;
units.rightText: From Kadesh, Moses sent messengers to tell the king of Edom, “This is what your brother Israel says: You know all the hardship that has befallen us,

units.leftText: how our fathers went down into Egypt, and we lived in Egypt a long time. The Egyptians mistreated us and our fathers.
units.rightText: how our fathers went down to Egypt, where we lived many years. The Egyptians mistreated us and our fathers,

units.leftText: When we cried to the LORD, he heard our voice, sent an angel, and brought us out of Egypt. Behold, we are in Kadesh, a city in the edge of your border.
units.rightText: and when we cried out to the LORD, He heard our voice, sent an angel, and brought us out of Egypt.

units.leftText: “Please let us pass through your land. We will not pass through field or through vineyard, neither will we drink from the water of the wells. We will go along the king’s highway. We will not turn away to the right hand nor to the left, until we have passed your border.”
units.rightText: Please let us pass through your land. We will not go through any field or vineyard, or drink water from any well. We will stay on the King’s Highway; we will not turn to the right or to the left until we have passed through your territory.”

units.leftText: Edom said to him, “You shall not pass through me, lest I come out with the sword against you.”
units.rightText: But Edom answered, “You may not travel through our land, or we will come out and confront you with the sword.”

units.leftText: The children of Israel said to him, “We will go up by the highway; and if we drink your water, I and my livestock, then I will give its price. Only let me, without doing anything else, pass through on my feet.”
units.rightText: “We will stay on the main road,” the Israelites replied, “and if we or our herds drink your water, we will pay for it. There will be no problem; only let us pass through on foot.”

units.leftText: He said, “You shall not pass through.” Edom came out against him with many people, and with a strong hand.
units.rightText: But Edom insisted, “You may not pass through.” And they came out to confront the Israelites with a large army and a strong hand.

units.leftText: Thus Edom refused to give Israel passage through his border, so Israel turned away from him.
units.rightText: So Edom refused to allow Israel to pass through their territory, and Israel turned away from them. The Death of Aaron

units.leftText: They traveled from Kadesh, and the children of Israel, even the whole congregation, came to Mount Hor.
units.rightText: After they had set out from Kadesh, the whole congregation of Israel came to Mount Hor.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron in Mount Hor, by the border of the land of Edom, saying,
units.rightText: And at Mount Hor, near the border of the land of Edom, the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,

units.leftText: “Aaron shall be gathered to his people; for he shall not enter into the land which I have given to the children of Israel, because you rebelled against my word at the waters of Meribah.
units.rightText: “Aaron will be gathered to his people; he will not enter the land that I have given the Israelites, because both of you rebelled against My command at the waters of Meribah.

units.leftText: Take Aaron and Eleazar his son, and bring them up to Mount Hor;
units.rightText: Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up Mount Hor.

units.leftText: and strip Aaron of his garments, and put them on Eleazar his son. Aaron shall be gathered, and shall die there.”
units.rightText: Remove Aaron’s priestly garments and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron will be gathered to his people and will die there.”

units.leftText: Moses did as the LORD commanded. They went up onto Mount Hor in the sight of all the congregation.
units.rightText: So Moses did as the LORD had commanded, and they climbed Mount Hor in the sight of the whole congregation.

units.leftText: Moses stripped Aaron of his garments, and put them on Eleazar his son. Aaron died there on the top of the mountain, and Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
units.rightText: After Moses had removed Aaron’s garments and put them on his son Eleazar, Aaron died there on top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.

units.leftText: When all the congregation saw that Aaron was dead, they wept for Aaron thirty days, even all the house of Israel.
units.rightText: When the whole congregation saw that Aaron had died, the entire house of Israel mourned for him thirty days.

units.leftText: The Canaanite, the king of Arad, who lived in the South, heard that Israel came by the way of Atharim. He fought against Israel, and took some of them captive.
units.rightText: When the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming along the road to Atharim, he attacked Israel and captured some prisoners.

units.leftText: Israel vowed a vow to the LORD, and said, “If you will indeed deliver this people into my hand, then I will utterly destroy their cities.”
units.rightText: So Israel made a vow to the LORD: “If You will deliver this people into our hands, we will devote their cities to destruction. ”
rightNotes: 21:2 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering; also in verse 3.

units.leftText: The LORD listened to the voice of Israel, and delivered up the Canaanites; and they utterly destroyed them and their cities. The name of the place was called Hormah.
units.rightText: And the LORD heard Israel’s plea and delivered up the Canaanites. Israel devoted them and their cities to destruction; so they named the place Hormah. The Bronze Serpent
leftNotes: 21:3 “Hormah” means “destruction”.
rightNotes: 21:3 Hormah means destruction.

units.leftText: They traveled from Mount Hor by the way to the Red Sea, to go around the land of Edom. The soul of the people was very discouraged because of the journey.
units.rightText: Then they set out from Mount Hor along the route to the Red Sea, in order to bypass the land of Edom. But the people grew impatient on the journey
rightNotes: 21:4 Or the Sea of Reeds

units.leftText: The people spoke against God and against Moses: “Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? For there is no bread, there is no water, and our soul loathes this disgusting food!”
units.rightText: and spoke against God and against Moses: “Why have you led us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? There is no bread or water, and we detest this wretched food!”

units.leftText: The LORD sent venomous snakes among the people, and they bit the people. Many people of Israel died.
units.rightText: So the LORD sent venomous snakes among the people, and many of the Israelites were bitten and died.

units.leftText: The people came to Moses, and said, “We have sinned, because we have spoken against the LORD and against you. Pray to the LORD, that he take away the serpents from us.” Moses prayed for the people.
units.rightText: Then the people came to Moses and said, “We have sinned by speaking against the LORD and against you. Intercede with the LORD so He will take the snakes away from us.” So Moses interceded for the people.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “Make a venomous snake, and set it on a pole. It shall happen that everyone who is bitten, when he sees it, shall live.”
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Make a fiery serpent and mount it on a pole. When anyone who is bitten looks at it, he will live.”

units.leftText: Moses made a serpent of bronze, and set it on the pole. If a serpent had bitten any man, when he looked at the serpent of bronze, he lived.
units.rightText: So Moses made a bronze snake and mounted it on a pole. If anyone who was bitten looked at the bronze snake, he would live. The Journey to Moab

units.leftText: The children of Israel traveled, and encamped in Oboth.
units.rightText: Then the Israelites set out and camped at Oboth.

units.leftText: They traveled from Oboth, and encamped at Iyeabarim, in the wilderness which is before Moab, toward the sunrise.
units.rightText: They journeyed from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim in the wilderness opposite Moab to the east.

units.leftText: From there they traveled, and encamped in the valley of Zered.
units.rightText: From there they set out and camped in the Valley of Zered.

units.leftText: From there they traveled, and encamped on the other side of the Arnon, which is in the wilderness that comes out of the border of the Amorites; for the Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.
units.rightText: From there they moved on and camped on the other side of the Arnon, in the wilderness that extends into the Amorite territory.

units.leftText: Therefore it is said in The Book of the Wars of the LORD*, “Vaheb in Suphah, the valleys of the Arnon,
units.rightText: Therefore it is stated in the Book of the Wars of the LORD: “Waheb in Suphah and the wadis of the Arnon,

units.leftText: the slope of the valleys that incline toward the dwelling of Ar, leans on the border of Moab.”
units.rightText: even the slopes of the wadis that extend to the site of Ar and lie along the border of Moab.”

units.leftText: From there they traveled to Beer; that is the well of which the LORD said to Moses, “Gather the people together, and I will give them water.”
units.rightText: From there they went on to Beer, the well where the LORD said to Moses, “Gather the people so that I may give them water.”
rightNotes: 21:16 Beer means well.

units.leftText: Then Israel sang this song: “Spring up, well! Sing to it,
units.rightText: Then Israel sang this song: “Spring up, O well, all of you sing to it!

units.leftText: the well, which the princes dug, which the nobles of the people dug, with the scepter, and with their poles.” From the wilderness they traveled to Mattanah;
units.rightText: The princes dug the well; the nobles of the people hollowed it out with their scepters and with their staffs.”

units.leftText: and from Mattanah to Nahaliel; and from Nahaliel to Bamoth;
units.rightText: and from Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth,

units.leftText: and from Bamoth to the valley that is in the field of Moab, to the top of Pisgah, which looks down on the desert.
units.rightText: and from Bamoth to the valley in Moab where the top of Pisgah overlooks the wasteland. The Defeat of Sihon (Deuteronomy 2:24–37|DEU 2:24-37*)
rightNotes: 21:20 Or Jeshimon

units.leftText: Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, saying,
units.rightText: Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, saying,

units.leftText: “Let me pass through your land. We will not turn away into field or vineyard. We will not drink of the water of the wells. We will go by the king’s highway, until we have passed your border.”
units.rightText: “Let us pass through your land. We will not turn aside into any field or vineyard, or drink water from any well. We will stay on the King’s Highway until we have passed through your territory.”

units.leftText: Sihon would not allow Israel to pass through his border, but Sihon gathered all his people together, and went out against Israel into the wilderness, and came to Jahaz. He fought against Israel.
units.rightText: But Sihon would not let Israel pass through his territory. Instead, he gathered his whole army and went out to confront Israel in the wilderness. When he came to Jahaz, he fought against Israel.
rightNotes: 21:23 Jahaz is a variant of Jahzah; see 1 Chronicles 6:78|1CH 6:78*.

units.leftText: Israel struck him with the edge of the sword, and possessed his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, even to the children of Ammon; for the border of the children of Ammon was fortified.
units.rightText: And Israel put him to the sword and took possession of his land, from the Arnon to the Jabbok — but only up to the border of the Ammonites, because it was fortified.
rightNotes: 21:24 Or because the territory was rugged; literally because it was strong

units.leftText: Israel took all these cities. Israel lived in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon, and in all its villages.
units.rightText: Israel captured all the cities of the Amorites and occupied them, including Heshbon and all its villages.

units.leftText: For Heshbon was the city of Sihon the king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab, and taken all his land out of his hand, even to the Arnon.
units.rightText: Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab and taken all his land as far as the Arnon.

units.leftText: Therefore those who speak in proverbs say, “Come to Heshbon. Let the city of Sihon be built and established;
units.rightText: That is why the poets say: “Come to Heshbon, let it be rebuilt; let the city of Sihon be restored.

units.leftText: for a fire has gone out of Heshbon, a flame from the city of Sihon. It has devoured Ar of Moab, The lords of the high places of the Arnon.
units.rightText: For a fire went out from Heshbon, a blaze from the city of Sihon. It consumed Ar of Moab, the rulers of Arnon’s heights.

units.leftText: Woe to you, Moab! You are undone, people of Chemosh! He has given his sons as fugitives, and his daughters into captivity, to Sihon king of the Amorites.
units.rightText: Woe to you, O Moab! You are destroyed, O people of Chemosh! He gave up his sons as refugees, and his daughters into captivity to Sihon king of the Amorites.

units.leftText: We have shot at them. Heshbon has perished even to Dibon. We have laid waste even to Nophah, Which reaches to Medeba.”
units.rightText: But we have overthrown them; Heshbon is destroyed as far as Dibon. We demolished them as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba. ” The Defeat of Og (Deuteronomy 3:1–11|DEU 3:1-11*)
rightNotes: 21:30 Or We demolished them until fire spread to Medeba

units.leftText: Thus Israel lived in the land of the Amorites.
units.rightText: So Israel lived in the land of the Amorites.

units.leftText: Moses sent to spy out Jazer. They took its villages, and drove out the Amorites who were there.
units.rightText: After Moses had sent spies to Jazer, Israel captured its villages and drove out the Amorites who were there.

units.leftText: They turned and went up by the way of Bashan. Og the king of Bashan went out against them, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.
units.rightText: Then they turned and went up the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan and his whole army came out to meet them in battle at Edrei.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “Don’t fear him, for I have delivered him into your hand, with all his people, and his land. You shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived at Heshbon.”
units.rightText: But the LORD said to Moses, “Do not fear him, for I have delivered him into your hand, along with all his people and his land. Do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.”

units.leftText: So they struck him, with his sons and all his people, until there were no survivors; and they possessed his land.
units.rightText: So they struck down Og, along with his sons and his whole army, until no remnant was left. And they took possession of his land.

units.leftText: The children of Israel traveled, and encamped in the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan at Jericho.
units.rightText: Then the Israelites traveled on and camped in the plains of Moab near the Jordan, across from Jericho.

units.leftText: Balak the son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites.
units.rightText: Now Balak son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites,

units.leftText: Moab was very afraid of the people, because they were many. Moab was distressed because of the children of Israel.
units.rightText: and Moab was terrified of the people because they were numerous. Indeed, Moab dreaded the Israelites.

units.leftText: Moab said to the elders of Midian, “Now this multitude will lick up all that is around us, as the ox licks up the grass of the field.” Balak the son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time.
units.rightText: So the Moabites said to the elders of Midian, “This horde will devour everything around us, as an ox licks up the grass of the field.”

units.leftText: He sent messengers to Balaam the son of Beor, to Pethor, which is by the River, to the land of the children of his people, to call him, saying, “Behold, there is a people who came out of Egypt. Behold, they cover the surface of the earth, and they are staying opposite me.
units.rightText: he sent messengers to summon Balaam son of Beor at Pethor, which is by the Euphrates in the land of his people.
rightNotes: 22:5 Hebrew the River

units.leftText: Please come now therefore, and curse this people for me; for they are too mighty for me. Perhaps I shall prevail, that we may strike them, and that I may drive them out of the land; for I know that he whom you bless is blessed, and he whom you curse is cursed.”
units.rightText: So please come now and put a curse on this people, because they are too mighty for me. Perhaps I may be able to defeat them and drive them out of the land; for I know that those you bless are blessed, and those you curse are cursed.”

units.leftText: The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian departed with the rewards of divination in their hand. They came to Balaam, and spoke to him the words of Balak.
units.rightText: The elders of Moab and Midian departed with the fees for divination in hand. They came to Balaam and relayed to him the words of Balak.

units.leftText: He said to them, “Lodge here this night, and I will bring you word again, as the LORD shall speak to me.” The princes of Moab stayed with Balaam.
units.rightText: “Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and I will give you the answer that the LORD speaks to me.” So the princes of Moab stayed with Balaam.

units.leftText: God came to Balaam, and said, “Who are these men with you?”
units.rightText: Then God came to Balaam and asked, “Who are these men with you?”

units.leftText: Balaam said to God, “Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, has said to me,
units.rightText: And Balaam said to God, “Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, sent me this message:

units.leftText: ‘Behold, the people that has come out of Egypt covers the surface of the earth. Now, come curse them for me. Perhaps I shall be able to fight against them, and shall drive them out.’”
units.rightText: ‘Behold, a people has come out of Egypt, and they cover the face of the land. Now come and put a curse on them for me. Perhaps I may be able to fight against them and drive them away.’”

units.leftText: God said to Balaam, “You shall not go with them. You shall not curse the people, for they are blessed.”
units.rightText: But God said to Balaam, “Do not go with them. You are not to curse this people, for they are blessed.”

units.leftText: Balaam rose up in the morning, and said to the princes of Balak, “Go to your land; for the LORD refuses to permit me to go with you.”
units.rightText: So Balaam got up the next morning and said to Balak’s princes, “Go back to your homeland, because the LORD has refused to let me go with you.”

units.leftText: The princes of Moab rose up, and they went to Balak, and said, “Balaam refuses to come with us.”
units.rightText: And the princes of Moab arose, returned to Balak, and said, “Balaam refused to come with us.”

units.leftText: Balak again sent princes, more, and more honorable than they.
units.rightText: Then Balak sent other princes, more numerous and more distinguished than the first messengers.

units.leftText: They came to Balaam, and said to him, “Balak the son of Zippor says, ‘Please let nothing hinder you from coming to me,
units.rightText: They came to Balaam and said, “This is what Balak son of Zippor says: ‘Please let nothing hinder you from coming to me,

units.leftText: for I will promote you to very great honor, and whatever you say to me I will do. Please come therefore, and curse this people for me.’”
units.rightText: for I will honor you richly and do whatever you say. So please come and put a curse on this people for me!’”

units.leftText: Balaam answered the servants of Balak, “If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I can’t go beyond the word of the LORD my God, to do less or more.
units.rightText: But Balaam replied to the servants of Balak, “If Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not do anything small or great to go beyond the command of the LORD my God.

units.leftText: Now therefore please stay here tonight as well, that I may know what else the LORD will speak to me.”
units.rightText: So now, please stay here overnight as the others did, that I may find out what else the LORD has to tell me.”

units.leftText: God came to Balaam at night, and said to him, “If the men have come to call you, rise up, go with them; but only the word which I speak to you, that you shall do.”
units.rightText: That night God came to Balaam and said, “Since these men have come to summon you, get up and go with them, but you must only do what I tell you.”

units.leftText: Balaam rose up in the morning, and saddled his donkey, and went with the princes of Moab.
units.rightText: So in the morning Balaam got up, saddled his donkey, and went with the princes of Moab. The Angel and Balaam’s Donkey

units.leftText: God’s anger burned because he went; and the LORD’s angel placed himself in the way as an adversary against him. Now he was riding on his donkey, and his two servants were with him.
units.rightText: Then God’s anger was kindled because Balaam was going along, and the angel of the LORD stood in the road to oppose him. Balaam was riding his donkey, and his two servants were with him.
rightNotes: 22:22 Or Angel; here through the rest of chapter 22; corresponding pronouns may also be capitalized.

units.leftText: The donkey saw the LORD’s angel standing in the way, with his sword drawn in his hand; and the donkey turned out of the path, and went into the field. Balaam struck the donkey, to turn her into the path.
units.rightText: When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand, she turned off the path and went into a field. So Balaam beat her to return her to the path.

units.leftText: Then the LORD’s angel stood in a narrow path between the vineyards, a wall being on this side, and a wall on that side.
units.rightText: Then the angel of the LORD stood in a narrow passage between two vineyards, with walls on either side.

units.leftText: The donkey saw the LORD’s angel, and she thrust herself to the wall, and crushed Balaam’s foot against the wall. He struck her again.
units.rightText: And the donkey saw the angel of the LORD and pressed herself against the wall, crushing Balaam’s foot against it. So he beat her once again.

units.leftText: The LORD’s angel went further, and stood in a narrow place, where there was no way to turn either to the right hand or to the left.
units.rightText: And the angel of the LORD moved on ahead and stood in a narrow place where there was no room to turn to the right or left.

units.leftText: The donkey saw the LORD’s angel, and she lay down under Balaam. Balaam’s anger burned, and he struck the donkey with his staff.
units.rightText: When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, she lay down under Balaam, and he became furious and beat her with his staff.

units.leftText: The LORD opened the mouth of the donkey, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?”
units.rightText: Then the LORD opened the donkey’s mouth, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you that you have beaten me these three times?”

units.leftText: Balaam said to the donkey, “Because you have mocked me, I wish there were a sword in my hand, for now I would have killed you.”
units.rightText: Balaam answered the donkey, “You have made a fool of me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you right now!”

units.leftText: The donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not your donkey, on which you have ridden all your life long until today? Was I ever in the habit of doing so to you?” He said, “No.”
units.rightText: But the donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not the donkey you have ridden all your life until today? Have I ever treated you this way before?” “No,” he replied.

units.leftText: Then the LORD opened the eyes of Balaam, and he saw the LORD’s angel standing in the way, with his sword drawn in his hand; and he bowed his head, and fell on his face.
units.rightText: Then the LORD opened Balaam’s eyes, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand. And Balaam bowed low and fell facedown.

units.leftText: The LORD’s angel said to him, “Why have you struck your donkey these three times? Behold, I have come out as an adversary, because your way is perverse before me.
units.rightText: The angel of the LORD asked him, “Why have you beaten your donkey these three times? Behold, I have come out to oppose you, because your way is perverse before me.
rightNotes: 22:32 Or reckless or contrary

units.leftText: The donkey saw me, and turned away before me these three times. Unless she had turned away from me, surely now I would have killed you, and saved her alive.”
units.rightText: The donkey saw me and turned away from me these three times. If she had not turned away, then by now I would surely have killed you and let her live.”

units.leftText: Balaam said to the LORD’s angel, “I have sinned; for I didn’t know that you stood in the way against me. Now therefore, if it displeases you, I will go back again.”
units.rightText: “I have sinned,” Balaam said to the angel of the LORD, “for I did not realize that you were standing in the road to confront me. And now, if this is displeasing in your sight, I will go back home.”

units.leftText: The LORD’s angel said to Balaam, “Go with the men; but you shall only speak the word that I shall speak to you.” So Balaam went with the princes of Balak.
units.rightText: But the angel of the LORD said to Balaam, “Go with the men, but you are to speak only what I tell you.” So Balaam went with the princes of Balak.

units.leftText: When Balak heard that Balaam had come, he went out to meet him to the City of Moab, which is on the border of the Arnon, which is in the utmost part of the border.
units.rightText: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went out to meet him at the Moabite city on the Arnon border, at the edge of his territory.

units.leftText: Balak said to Balaam, “Didn’t I earnestly send for you to summon you? Why didn’t you come to me? Am I not able indeed to promote you to honor?”
units.rightText: And he said to Balaam, “Did I not send you an urgent summons? Why did you not come to me? Am I really not able to reward you richly?”

units.leftText: Balaam said to Balak, “Behold, I have come to you. Have I now any power at all to speak anything? I will speak the word that God puts in my mouth.”
units.rightText: “See, I have come to you,” Balaam replied, “but can I say just anything? I must speak only the word that God puts in my mouth.”

units.leftText: Balaam went with Balak, and they came to Kiriath Huzoth.
units.rightText: So Balaam accompanied Balak, and they came to Kiriath-huzoth.

units.leftText: Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep, and sent to Balaam, and to the princes who were with him.
units.rightText: Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep, and he gave portions to Balaam and the princes who were with him.

units.leftText: In the morning, Balak took Balaam, and brought him up into the high places of Baal; and he saw from there part of the people.
units.rightText: The next morning, Balak took Balaam and brought him up to Bamoth-baal. From there he could see the outskirts of the camp of the people.

units.leftText: Balaam said to Balak, “Build here seven altars for me, and prepare here seven bulls and seven rams for me.”
units.rightText: Then Balaam said to Balak, “Build for me seven altars here, and prepare for me seven bulls and seven rams.”

units.leftText: Balak did as Balaam had spoken; and Balak and Balaam offered on every altar a bull and a ram.
units.rightText: So Balak did as Balaam had instructed, and Balak and Balaam offered a bull and a ram on each altar.

units.leftText: Balaam said to Balak, “Stand by your burnt offering, and I will go. Perhaps the LORD will come to meet me. Whatever he shows me I will tell you.” He went to a bare height.
units.rightText: “Stay here by your burnt offering while I am gone,” Balaam said to Balak. “Perhaps the LORD will meet with me. And whatever He reveals to me, I will tell you.”

units.leftText: God met Balaam, and he said to him, “I have prepared the seven altars, and I have offered up a bull and a ram on every altar.”
units.rightText: and God met with him. “I have set up seven altars,” Balaam said, “and on each altar I have offered a bull and a ram.”

units.leftText: The LORD put a word in Balaam’s mouth, and said, “Return to Balak, and thus you shall speak.”
units.rightText: Then the LORD put a message in Balaam’s mouth, saying, “Return to Balak and give him this message.”

units.leftText: He returned to him, and behold, he was standing by his burnt offering, he, and all the princes of Moab.
units.rightText: So he returned to Balak, who was standing there beside his burnt offering, with all the princes of Moab.

units.leftText: He took up his parable, and said, “From Aram has Balak brought me, the king of Moab from the mountains of the East. Come, curse Jacob for me. Come, defy Israel.
units.rightText: And Balaam lifted up an oracle, saying: “Balak brought me from Aram, the king of Moab from the mountains of the east. ‘Come,’ he said, ‘put a curse on Jacob for me; come and denounce Israel!’

units.leftText: How shall I curse whom God has not cursed? How shall I defy whom the LORD has not defied?
units.rightText: How can I curse those whom God has not cursed? How can I denounce those whom the LORD has not denounced?

units.leftText: For from the top of the rocks I see him. From the hills I see him. Behold, it is a people that dwells alone, and shall not be listed among the nations.
units.rightText: For I see them from atop the rocky cliffs, and I watch them from the hills. Behold, a people dwelling apart, not reckoning themselves among the nations.

units.leftText: Who can count the dust of Jacob, or count the fourth part of Israel? Let me die the death of the righteous! Let my last end be like his!”
units.rightText: Who can count the dust of Jacob or number even a fourth of Israel? Let me die the death of the righteous; let my end be like theirs!”

units.leftText: Balak said to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I took you to curse my enemies, and behold, you have blessed them altogether.”
units.rightText: Then Balak said to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I brought you here to curse my enemies, and behold, you have only blessed them!”

units.leftText: He answered and said, “Must I not take heed to speak that which the LORD puts in my mouth?”
units.rightText: But Balaam replied, “Should I not speak exactly what the LORD puts in my mouth?” Balaam’s Second Oracle

units.leftText: Balak said to him, “Please come with me to another place, where you may see them. You shall see just part of them, and shall not see them all. Curse them from there for me.”
units.rightText: Then Balak said to him, “Please come with me to another place where you can see them. You will only see the outskirts of their camp — not all of them. And from there, curse them for me.”

units.leftText: He took him into the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, and built seven altars, and offered up a bull and a ram on every altar.
units.rightText: So Balak took him to the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, where he built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.

units.leftText: He said to Balak, “Stand here by your burnt offering, while I meet God over there.”
units.rightText: Balaam said to Balak, “Stay here beside your burnt offering while I meet the LORD over there.”

units.leftText: The LORD met Balaam, and put a word in his mouth, and said, “Return to Balak, and say this.”
units.rightText: And the LORD met with Balaam and put a message in his mouth, saying, “Return to Balak and speak what I tell you.”

units.leftText: He came to him, and behold, he was standing by his burnt offering, and the princes of Moab with him. Balak said to him, “What has the LORD spoken?”
units.rightText: So he returned to Balak, who was standing there by his burnt offering with the princes of Moab. “What did the LORD say?” Balak asked.

units.leftText: He took up his parable, and said, “Rise up, Balak, and hear! Listen to me, you son of Zippor.
units.rightText: Then Balaam lifted up an oracle, saying: “Arise, O Balak, and listen; give ear to me, O son of Zippor.

units.leftText: God is not a man, that he should lie, nor a son of man, that he should repent. Has he said, and he won’t do it? Or has he spoken, and he won’t make it good?
units.rightText: God is not a man, that He should lie, or a son of man, that He should change His mind. Does He speak and not act? Does He promise and not fulfill?

units.leftText: Behold, I have received a command to bless. He has blessed, and I can’t reverse it.
units.rightText: I have indeed received a command to bless; He has blessed, and I cannot change it.

units.leftText: He has not seen iniquity in Jacob. Neither has he seen perverseness in Israel. The LORD his God is with him. The shout of a king is among them.
units.rightText: He considers no disaster for Jacob; He sees no trouble for Israel. The LORD their God is with them, and the shout of the King is among them.

units.leftText: God brings them out of Egypt. He has as it were the strength of the wild ox.
units.rightText: God brought them out of Egypt with strength like a wild ox.

units.leftText: Surely there is no enchantment with Jacob; neither is there any divination with Israel. Now it shall be said of Jacob and of Israel, ‘What has God done!’
units.rightText: For there is no spell against Jacob and no divination against Israel. It will now be said of Jacob and Israel, ‘What great things God has done!’

units.leftText: Behold, a people rises up as a lioness. As a lion he lifts himself up. He shall not lie down until he eats of the prey, and drinks the blood of the slain.”
units.rightText: Behold, the people rise like a lioness; they rouse themselves like a lion, not resting until they devour their prey and drink the blood of the slain.”

units.leftText: Balak said to Balaam, “Neither curse them at all, nor bless them at all.”
units.rightText: Now Balak said to Balaam, “Then neither curse them at all nor bless them at all!”

units.leftText: But Balaam answered Balak, “Didn’t I tell you, saying, ‘All that the LORD speaks, that I must do’?”
units.rightText: But Balaam replied, “Did I not tell you that whatever the LORD says, I must do?”

units.leftText: Balak said to Balaam, “Come now, I will take you to another place; perhaps it will please God that you may curse them for me from there.”
units.rightText: “Please come,” said Balak, “I will take you to another place. Perhaps it will please God that you curse them for me from there.”

units.leftText: Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, that looks down on the desert.
units.rightText: And Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, which overlooks the wasteland.
rightNotes: 23:28 Or Jeshimon

units.leftText: Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars for me here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.”
units.rightText: Then Balaam said, “Build for me seven altars here, and prepare for me seven bulls and seven rams.”

units.leftText: Balak did as Balaam had said, and offered up a bull and a ram on every altar.
units.rightText: So Balak did as Balaam had instructed, and he offered a bull and a ram on each altar.

units.leftText: When Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he didn’t go, as at the other times, to use divination, but he set his face toward the wilderness.
units.rightText: And when Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he did not seek omens as on previous occasions, but he turned his face toward the wilderness.

units.leftText: Balaam lifted up his eyes, and he saw Israel dwelling according to their tribes; and the Spirit of God came on him.
units.rightText: When Balaam looked up and saw Israel encamped tribe by tribe, the Spirit of God came upon him,

units.leftText: He took up his parable, and said, “Balaam the son of Beor says, the man whose eyes are open says;
units.rightText: and he lifted up an oracle, saying: “This is the prophecy of Balaam son of Beor, the prophecy of a man whose eyes are open,

units.leftText: he says, who hears the words of God, who sees the vision of the Almighty, falling down, and having his eyes open:
units.rightText: the prophecy of one who hears the words of God, who sees a vision from the Almighty, who bows down with eyes wide open:
rightNotes: 24:4 Hebrew Shaddai; also in verse 16

units.leftText: How goodly are your tents, Jacob, and your dwellings, Israel!
units.rightText: How lovely are your tents, O Jacob, your dwellings, O Israel!

units.leftText: As valleys they are spread out, as gardens by the riverside, as aloes which the LORD has planted, as cedar trees beside the waters.
units.rightText: They spread out like palm groves, like gardens beside a stream, like aloes the LORD has planted, like cedars beside the waters.
rightNotes: 24:6 Or like valleys

units.leftText: Water shall flow from his buckets. His seed shall be in many waters. His king shall be higher than Agag. His kingdom shall be exalted.
units.rightText: Water will flow from his buckets, and his seed will have abundant water. His king will be greater than Agag, and his kingdom will be exalted.

units.leftText: God brings him out of Egypt. He has as it were the strength of the wild ox. He shall consume the nations his adversaries, shall break their bones in pieces, and pierce them with his arrows.
units.rightText: God brought him out of Egypt with strength like a wild ox, to devour hostile nations and crush their bones, to pierce them with arrows.

units.leftText: He couched, he lay down as a lion, as a lioness; who shall rouse him up? Everyone who blesses you is blessed. Everyone who curses you is cursed.”
units.rightText: He crouches, he lies down like a lion, like a lioness— who dares to rouse him? Blessed are those who bless you and cursed are those who curse you.” Balak Dismisses Balaam

units.leftText: Balak’s anger burned against Balaam, and he struck his hands together. Balak said to Balaam, “I called you to curse my enemies, and, behold, you have altogether blessed them these three times.
units.rightText: Then Balak’s anger burned against Balaam, and he struck his hands together and said to Balaam, “I summoned you to curse my enemies, but behold, you have persisted in blessing them these three times.

units.leftText: Therefore, flee to your place, now! I thought to promote you to great honor; but, behold, the LORD has kept you back from honor.”
units.rightText: Therefore , flee at once to your home! I said I would reward you richly, but instead the LORD has denied your reward.”

units.leftText: Balaam said to Balak, “Didn’t I also tell your messengers whom you sent to me, saying,
units.rightText: Balaam answered Balak, “Did I not already tell the messengers you sent me

units.leftText: ‘If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I can’t go beyond the LORD’s word, to do either good or bad from my own mind. I will say what the LORD says’?
units.rightText: that even if Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not do anything of my own accord, good or bad, to go beyond the command of the LORD? I must speak whatever the LORD says.

units.leftText: Now, behold, I go to my people. Come, I will inform you what this people shall do to your people in the latter days.”
units.rightText: Now I am going back to my people, but come, let me warn you what this people will do to your people in the days to come.” Balaam’s Fourth Oracle

units.leftText: He took up his parable, and said, “Balaam the son of Beor says, the man whose eyes are open says;
units.rightText: Then Balaam lifted up an oracle, saying, “This is the prophecy of Balaam son of Beor, the prophecy of a man whose eyes are open,

units.leftText: he says, who hears the words of God, knows the knowledge of the Most High, and who sees the vision of the Almighty, falling down, and having his eyes open:
units.rightText: the prophecy of one who hears the words of God, who has knowledge from the Most High, who sees a vision from the Almighty, who bows down with eyes wide open:

units.leftText: I see him, but not now. I see him, but not near. A star will come out of Jacob. A scepter will rise out of Israel, and shall strike through the corners of Moab, and crush all the sons of Sheth.
units.rightText: I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star will come forth from Jacob, and a scepter will arise from Israel. He will crush the skulls of Moab and strike down all the sons of Sheth.
rightNotes: 24:17 SP foreheads; Hebrew corners (of the head); LXX princes

units.leftText: Edom shall be a possession. Seir, his enemy, also shall be a possession, while Israel does valiantly.
units.rightText: Edom will become a possession, as will Seir, his enemy; but Israel will perform with valor.

units.leftText: Out of Jacob shall one have dominion, and shall destroy the remnant from the city.”
units.rightText: A ruler will come from Jacob and destroy the survivors of the city.” Balaam’s Final Three Oracles

units.leftText: He looked at Amalek, and took up his parable, and said, “Amalek was the first of the nations, but his latter end shall come to destruction.”
units.rightText: Then Balaam saw Amalek and lifted up an oracle, saying: “Amalek was first among the nations, but his end is destruction.”

units.leftText: He looked at the Kenite, and took up his parable, and said, “Your dwelling place is strong. Your nest is set in the rock.
units.rightText: Next he saw the Kenites and lifted up an oracle, saying: “Your dwelling place is secure, and your nest is set in a cliff.

units.leftText: Nevertheless Kain shall be wasted, until Asshur carries you away captive.”
units.rightText: Yet Kain will be destroyed when Asshur takes you captive.”
rightNotes: 24:22 Or Assyria; also in verse 24

units.leftText: He took up his parable, and said, “Alas, who shall live when God does this?
units.rightText: Once more Balaam lifted up an oracle, saying: “Ah, who can live unless God has ordained it?

units.leftText: But ships shall come from the coast of Kittim. They shall afflict Asshur, and shall afflict Eber. He also shall come to destruction.”
units.rightText: Ships will come from the coasts of Cyprus; they will subdue Asshur and Eber, but they too will perish forever.”
rightNotes: 24:24 Hebrew Kittim

units.leftText: Balaam rose up, and went and returned to his place; and Balak also went his way.
units.rightText: Then Balaam arose and returned to his homeland, and Balak also went on his way.

units.leftText: Israel stayed in Shittim; and the people began to play the prostitute with the daughters of Moab;
units.rightText: While Israel was staying in Shittim, the men began to indulge in sexual immorality with the daughters of Moab,
rightNotes: 25:1 Or Acacia Grove

units.leftText: for they called the people to the sacrifices of their gods. The people ate and bowed down to their gods.
units.rightText: who also invited them to the sacrifices for their gods. And the people ate and bowed down to these gods.

units.leftText: Israel joined himself to Baal Peor, and the LORD’s anger burned against Israel.
units.rightText: So Israel joined in worshiping Baal of Peor, and the anger of the LORD burned against them.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “Take all the chiefs of the people, and hang them up to the LORD before the sun, that the fierce anger of the LORD may turn away from Israel.”
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Take all the leaders of the people and execute them in broad daylight before the LORD, so that His fierce anger may turn away from Israel.”

units.leftText: Moses said to the judges of Israel, “Everyone kill his men who have joined themselves to Baal Peor.”
units.rightText: So Moses told the judges of Israel, “Each of you must kill all of his men who have joined in worshiping Baal of Peor.” The Zeal of Phinehas

units.leftText: Behold, one of the children of Israel came and brought to his brothers a Midianite woman in the sight of Moses, and in the sight of all the congregation of the children of Israel, while they were weeping at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: Just then an Israelite man brought to his family a Midianite woman in the sight of Moses and the whole congregation of Israel while they were weeping at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

units.leftText: When Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from the middle of the congregation, and took a spear in his hand.
units.rightText: On seeing this, Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, got up from the assembly, took a spear in his hand,

units.leftText: He went after the man of Israel into the pavilion, and thrust both of them through, the man of Israel, and the woman through her body. So the plague was stopped among the children of Israel.
units.rightText: followed the Israelite into the tent, and drove the spear through both of them— through the Israelite and on through the belly of the woman.

units.leftText: Those who died by the plague were twenty-four thousand.
units.rightText: but those who died in the plague numbered 24,000.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned my wrath away from the children of Israel, in that he was jealous with my jealousy among them, so that I didn’t consume the children of Israel in my jealousy.
units.rightText: “Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned My wrath away from the Israelites; for he was zealous for My sake among them, so that I did not consume the Israelites in My zeal.

units.leftText: Therefore say, ‘Behold, I give to him my covenant of peace.
units.rightText: Declare, therefore, that I am granting him My covenant of peace.

units.leftText: It shall be to him, and to his offspring after him, the covenant of an everlasting priesthood, because he was jealous for his God, and made atonement for the children of Israel.’”
units.rightText: It will be a covenant of permanent priesthood for him and his descendants, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites.”

units.leftText: Now the name of the man of Israel that was slain, who was slain with the Midianite woman, was Zimri, the son of Salu, a prince of a fathers’ house among the Simeonites.
units.rightText: The name of the Israelite who was slain with the Midianite woman was Zimri son of Salu, the leader of a Simeonite family.

units.leftText: The name of the Midianite woman who was slain was Cozbi, the daughter of Zur. He was head of the people of a fathers’ house in Midian.
units.rightText: And the name of the slain Midianite woman was Cozbi, the daughter of Zur, a tribal chief of a Midianite family.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: And the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Harass the Midianites, and strike them;
units.rightText: “Attack the Midianites and strike them dead.

units.leftText: for they harassed you with their wiles, wherein they have deceived you in the matter of Peor, and in the incident regarding Cozbi, the daughter of the prince of Midian, their sister, who was slain on the day of the plague in the matter of Peor.”
units.rightText: For they assailed you deceitfully when they seduced you in the matter of Peor and their sister Cozbi, the daughter of the Midianite leader, the woman who was killed on the day the plague came because of Peor.”

units.leftText: After the plague, the LORD spoke to Moses and to Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, saying,
units.rightText: After the plague had ended, the LORD said to Moses and Eleazar son of Aaron the priest,

units.leftText: “Take a census of all the congregation of the children of Israel, from twenty years old and upward, by their fathers’ houses, all who are able to go out to war in Israel.”
units.rightText: “Take a census of the whole congregation of Israel by the houses of their fathers — all those twenty years of age or older who can serve in the army of Israel.”
