units.leftText: Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke with them in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying,
units.rightText: So on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho, Moses and Eleazar the priest issued the instruction,

units.leftText: “Take a census, from twenty years old and upward, as the LORD commanded Moses and the children of Israel.” These are those who came out of the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: “Take a census of the men twenty years of age or older, as the LORD has commanded Moses.” And these were the Israelites who came out of the land of Egypt: The Tribe of Reuben
rightNotes: 26:4 Take a census of the men is implied but not included in the Hebrew; see verse 2.

units.leftText: Reuben, the firstborn of Israel; the sons of Reuben: of Hanoch, the family of the Hanochites; of Pallu, the family of the Palluites;
units.rightText: Reuben was the firstborn of Israel. These were the descendants of Reuben: The Hanochite clan from Hanoch, the Palluite clan from Pallu,

units.leftText: of Hezron, the family of the Hezronites; of Carmi, the family of the Carmites.
units.rightText: the Hezronite clan from Hezron, and the Carmite clan from Carmi.

units.leftText: These are the families of the Reubenites; and those who were counted of them were forty-three thousand seven hundred thirty.
units.rightText: These were the clans of Reuben, and their registration numbered 43,730.

units.leftText: The son of Pallu: Eliab.
units.rightText: Now the son of Pallu was Eliab,

units.leftText: The sons of Eliab: Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These are that Dathan and Abiram who were called by the congregation, who rebelled against Moses and against Aaron in the company of Korah when they rebelled against the LORD;
units.rightText: and the sons of Eliab were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram.

units.leftText: and the earth opened its mouth, and swallowed them up together with Korah when that company died; at the time the fire devoured two hundred fifty men, and they became a sign.
units.rightText: And the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them along with Korah, whose followers died when the fire consumed 250 men. They serve as a warning sign.

units.leftText: Notwithstanding, the sons of Korah didn’t die.
units.rightText: However, the line of Korah did not die out. The Tribe of Simeon

units.leftText: The sons of Simeon after their families: of Nemuel, the family of the Nemuelites; of Jamin, the family of the Jaminites; of Jachin, the family of the Jachinites;
units.rightText: These were the descendants of Simeon by their clans: The Nemuelite clan from Nemuel, the Jaminite clan from Jamin, the Jachinite clan from Jachin,
rightNotes: 26:12 Nemuel is another name for Jemuel; see Genesis 46:10|GEN 46:10*.

units.leftText: of Zerah, the family of the Zerahites; of Shaul, the family of the Shaulites.
units.rightText: the Zerahite clan from Zerah, and the Shaulite clan from Shaul.
rightNotes: 26:13 Zerah is a variant of Zohar; see Genesis 46:10|GEN 46:10* and Exodus 6:15.

units.leftText: These are the families of the Simeonites, twenty-two thousand two hundred.
units.rightText: These were the clans of Simeon, and there were 22,200 men. The Tribe of Gad

units.leftText: The sons of Gad after their families: of Zephon, the family of the Zephonites; of Haggi, the family of the Haggites; of Shuni, the family of the Shunites;
units.rightText: These were the descendants of Gad by their clans: The Zephonite clan from Zephon, the Haggite clan from Haggi, the Shunite clan from Shuni,

units.leftText: of Ozni, the family of the Oznites; of Eri, the family of the Erites;
units.rightText: the Oznite clan from Ozni, the Erite clan from Eri,

units.leftText: of Arod, the family of the Arodites; of Areli, the family of the Arelites.
units.rightText: the Arodite clan from Arod, and the Arelite clan from Areli.
rightNotes: 26:17 SP and Syriac Arodi; see Genesis 46:16|GEN 46:16*.

units.leftText: These are the families of the sons of Gad according to those who were counted of them, forty thousand and five hundred.
units.rightText: These were the clans of Gad, and their registration numbered . . . 40,500. The Tribe of Judah

units.leftText: The sons of Judah: Er and Onan. Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
units.rightText: The sons of Judah were Er and Onan, but they died in the land of Canaan.

units.leftText: The sons of Judah after their families were: of Shelah, the family of the Shelanites; of Perez, the family of the Perezites; of Zerah, the family of the Zerahites.
units.rightText: These were the descendants of Judah by their clans: The Shelanite clan from Shelah, the Perezite clan from Perez, and the Zerahite clan from Zerah.

units.leftText: The sons of Perez were: of Hezron, the family of the Hezronites; of Hamul, the family of the Hamulites.
units.rightText: And these were the descendants of Perez: the Hezronite clan from Hezron and the Hamulite clan from Hamul.

units.leftText: These are the families of Judah according to those who were counted of them, seventy-six thousand five hundred.
units.rightText: These were the clans of Judah, and their registration numbered . . . 76,500. The Tribe of Issachar

units.leftText: The sons of Issachar after their families: of Tola, the family of the Tolaites; of Puvah, the family of the Punites;
units.rightText: These were the descendants of Issachar by their clans: The Tolaite clan from Tola, the Punite clan from Puvah,
rightNotes: 26:23 SP, LXX, Vulgate, and Syriac the Puite clan from Puah; see 1 Chronicles 7:1|1CH 7:1*.

units.leftText: of Jashub, the family of the Jashubites; of Shimron, the family of the Shimronites.
units.rightText: the Jashubite clan from Jashub, and the Shimronite clan from Shimron.
rightNotes: 26:24 Jashub is a variant of Job; see Genesis 46:13|GEN 46:13*.

units.leftText: These are the families of Issachar according to those who were counted of them, sixty-four thousand three hundred.
units.rightText: These were the clans of Issachar, and their registration numbered . . . 64,300. The Tribe of Zebulun

units.leftText: The sons of Zebulun after their families: of Sered, the family of the Seredites; of Elon, the family of the Elonites; of Jahleel, the family of the Jahleelites.
units.rightText: These were the descendants of Zebulun by their clans: The Seredite clan from Sered, the Elonite clan from Elon, and the Jahleelite clan from Jahleel.

units.leftText: These are the families of the Zebulunites according to those who were counted of them, sixty thousand five hundred.
units.rightText: These were the clans of Zebulun, and their registration numbered . . . 60,500. The Tribe of Manasseh

units.leftText: The sons of Joseph after their families: Manasseh and Ephraim.
units.rightText: The descendants of Joseph included the clans of Manasseh and Ephraim.

units.leftText: The sons of Manasseh: of Machir, the family of the Machirites; and Machir became the father of Gilead; of Gilead, the family of the Gileadites.
units.rightText: These were the descendants of Manasseh: The Machirite clan from Machir, the father of Gilead, and the Gileadite clan from Gilead.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Gilead: of Iezer, the family of the Iezerites; of Helek, the family of the Helekites;
units.rightText: These were the descendants of Gilead: the Iezerite clan from Iezer, the Helekite clan from Helek,
rightNotes: 26:30 Iezer is a variant of Abiezer; see Joshua 17:2|JOS 17:2*.

units.leftText: and Asriel, the family of the Asrielites; and Shechem, the family of the Shechemites;
units.rightText: the Asrielite clan from Asriel, the Shechemite clan from Shechem,

units.leftText: and Shemida, the family of the Shemidaites; and Hepher, the family of the Hepherites.
units.rightText: the Shemidaite clan from Shemida, and the Hepherite clan from Hepher.

units.leftText: Zelophehad the son of Hepher had no sons, but daughters: and the names of the daughters of Zelophehad were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
units.rightText: Now Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons but only daughters. The names of his daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

units.leftText: These are the families of Manasseh. Those who were counted of them were fifty-two thousand seven hundred.
units.rightText: These were the clans of Manasseh, and their registration numbered . . . 52,700. The Tribe of Ephraim

units.leftText: These are the sons of Ephraim after their families: of Shuthelah, the family of the Shuthelahites; of Becher, the family of the Becherites; of Tahan, the family of the Tahanites.
units.rightText: These were the descendants of Ephraim by their clans: The Shuthelahite clan from Shuthelah, the Becherite clan from Becher, and the Tahanite clan from Tahan.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Shuthelah: of Eran, the family of the Eranites.
units.rightText: And the descendants of Shuthelah were the Eranite clan from Eran.

units.leftText: These are the families of the sons of Ephraim according to those who were counted of them, thirty-two thousand five hundred. These are the sons of Joseph after their families.
units.rightText: These were the clans of Ephraim, and their registration numbered . . . 32,500. These clans were the descendants of Joseph. The Tribe of Benjamin

units.leftText: The sons of Benjamin after their families: of Bela, the family of the Belaites; of Ashbel, the family of the Ashbelites; of Ahiram, the family of the Ahiramites;
units.rightText: These were the descendants of Benjamin by their clans: The Belaite clan from Bela, the Ashbelite clan from Ashbel, the Ahiramite clan from Ahiram,

units.leftText: of Shephupham, the family of the Shuphamites; of Hupham, the family of the Huphamites.
units.rightText: the Shuphamite clan from Shupham, and the Huphamite clan from Hupham.
rightNotes: 26:39 A few MT manuscripts, SP, Vulgate, and Syriac (see also LXX); most MT manuscripts Shephupham

units.leftText: The sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman: the family of the Ardites; and of Naaman, the family of the Naamites.
units.rightText: And the descendants of Bela from Ard and Naaman were the Ardite clan from Ard and the Naamite clan from Naaman.
rightNotes: 26:40 SP and Vulgate (see also LXX); MT does not include from Ard.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Benjamin after their families; and those who were counted of them were forty-five thousand six hundred.
units.rightText: These were the clans of Benjamin, and their registration numbered . . . 45,600. The Tribe of Dan

units.leftText: These are the sons of Dan after their families: of Shuham, the family of the Shuhamites. These are the families of Dan after their families.
units.rightText: These were the descendants of Dan by their clans: The Shuhamite clan from Shuham.

units.leftText: All the families of the Shuhamites, according to those who were counted of them, were sixty-four thousand four hundred.
units.rightText: All of them were Shuhamite clans, and their registration numbered . . . 64,400. The Tribe of Asher

units.leftText: The sons of Asher after their families: of Imnah, the family of the Imnites; of Ishvi, the family of the Ishvites; of Beriah, the family of the Berites.
units.rightText: These were the descendants of Asher by their clans: The Imnite clan from Imnah, the Ishvite clan from Ishvi, and the Beriite clan from Beriah.

units.leftText: Of the sons of Beriah: of Heber, the family of the Heberites; of Malchiel, the family of the Malchielites.
units.rightText: And these were the descendants of Beriah: the Heberite clan from Heber and the Malchielite clan from Malchiel.

units.leftText: The name of the daughter of Asher was Serah.
units.rightText: And the name of Asher’s daughter was Serah.

units.leftText: These are the families of the sons of Asher according to those who were counted of them, fifty-three thousand four hundred.
units.rightText: These were the clans of Asher, and their registration numbered . . . 53,400. The Tribe of Naphtali

units.leftText: The sons of Naphtali after their families: of Jahzeel, the family of the Jahzeelites; of Guni, the family of the Gunites;
units.rightText: These were the descendants of Naphtali by their clans: The Jahzeelite clan from Jahzeel, the Gunite clan from Guni,

units.leftText: of Jezer, the family of the Jezerites; of Shillem, the family of the Shillemites.
units.rightText: the Jezerite clan from Jezer, and the Shillemite clan from Shillem.

units.leftText: These are the families of Naphtali according to their families; and those who were counted of them were forty-five thousand four hundred.
units.rightText: These were the clans of Naphtali, and their registration numbered . . . 45,400.

units.leftText: These are those who were counted of the children of Israel, six hundred one thousand seven hundred thirty.
units.rightText: These men of Israel numbered 601,730 in all. Inheritance by Lot

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “To these the land shall be divided for an inheritance according to the number of names.
units.rightText: “The land is to be divided among the tribes as an inheritance, according to the number of names.

units.leftText: To the more you shall give the more inheritance, and to the fewer you shall give the less inheritance. To everyone according to those who were counted of him shall his inheritance be given.
units.rightText: Increase the inheritance for a large tribe and decrease it for a small one; each tribe is to receive its inheritance according to the number of those registered.

units.leftText: Notwithstanding, the land shall be divided by lot. According to the names of the tribes of their fathers they shall inherit.
units.rightText: Indeed, the land must be divided by lot; they shall receive their inheritance according to the names of the tribes of their fathers.

units.leftText: According to the lot shall their inheritance be divided between the more and the fewer.”
units.rightText: Each inheritance is to be divided by lot among the larger and smaller tribes.” The Levites Numbered

units.leftText: These are those who were counted of the Levites after their families: of Gershon, the family of the Gershonites; of Kohath, the family of the Kohathites; of Merari, the family of the Merarites.
units.rightText: Now these were the Levites numbered by their clans: The Gershonite clan from Gershon, the Kohathite clan from Kohath, and the Merarite clan from Merari.

units.leftText: These are the families of Levi: the family of the Libnites, the family of the Hebronites, the family of the Mahlites, the family of the Mushites, and the family of the Korahites. Kohath became the father of Amram.
units.rightText: These were the families of the Levites: The Libnite clan, the Hebronite clan, the Mahlite clan, the Mushite clan, and the Korahite clan.

units.leftText: The name of Amram’s wife was Jochebed, the daughter of Levi, who was born to Levi in Egypt. She bore to Amram Aaron and Moses, and Miriam their sister.
units.rightText: and Amram’s wife was named Jochebed. She was also a daughter of Levi, born to Levi in Egypt. To Amram she bore Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam.

units.leftText: To Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
units.rightText: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar were born to Aaron,

units.leftText: Nadab and Abihu died when they offered strange fire before the LORD.
units.rightText: but Nadab and Abihu died when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD.
rightNotes: 26:61 Or strange

units.leftText: Those who were counted of them were twenty-three thousand, every male from a month old and upward; for they were not counted among the children of Israel, because there was no inheritance given them among the children of Israel.
units.rightText: The registration of the Levites totaled 23,000, every male a month old or more; they were not numbered among the other Israelites, because no inheritance was given to them among the Israelites. Only Caleb and Joshua Remain

units.leftText: These are those who were counted by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who counted the children of Israel in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
units.rightText: These were the ones numbered by Moses and Eleazar the priest when they counted the Israelites on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho.

units.leftText: But among these there was not a man of them who were counted by Moses and Aaron the priest, who counted the children of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai.
units.rightText: Among all these, however, there was not one who had been numbered by Moses and Aaron the priest when they counted the Israelites in the Wilderness of Sinai.

units.leftText: For the LORD had said of them, “They shall surely die in the wilderness.” There was not a man left of them, except Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.
units.rightText: For the LORD had told them that they would surely die in the wilderness. Not one was left except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

units.leftText: Then the daughters of Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, of the families of Manasseh the son of Joseph came near. These are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
units.rightText: Now the daughters of Zelophehad son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, belonged to the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph. These were the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. They approached

units.leftText: They stood before Moses, before Eleazar the priest, and before the princes and all the congregation, at the door of the Tent of Meeting, saying,
units.rightText: the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the whole congregation, and said,

units.leftText: “Our father died in the wilderness. He was not among the company of those who gathered themselves together against the LORD in the company of Korah, but he died in his own sin. He had no sons.
units.rightText: “Our father died in the wilderness, but he was not among the followers of Korah who gathered together against the LORD. Instead, he died because of his own sin, and he had no sons.

units.leftText: Why should the name of our father be taken away from among his family, because he had no son? Give to us a possession among the brothers of our father.”
units.rightText: Why should the name of our father disappear from his clan because he had no sons? Give us property among our father’s brothers.”

units.leftText: Moses brought their cause before the LORD.
units.rightText: So Moses brought their case before the LORD,

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: and the LORD answered him,

units.leftText: “The daughters of Zelophehad speak right. You shall surely give them a possession of an inheritance among their father’s brothers. You shall cause the inheritance of their father to pass to them.
units.rightText: “The daughters of Zelophehad speak correctly. You certainly must give them property as an inheritance among their father’s brothers and transfer their father’s inheritance to them.

units.leftText: You shall speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘If a man dies, and has no son, then you shall cause his inheritance to pass to his daughter.
units.rightText: Furthermore, you shall say to the Israelites, ‘If a man dies and leaves no son, you are to transfer his inheritance to his daughter.

units.leftText: If he has no daughter, then you shall give his inheritance to his brothers.
units.rightText: If he has no daughter, give his inheritance to his brothers.

units.leftText: If he has no brothers, then you shall give his inheritance to his father’s brothers.
units.rightText: If he has no brothers, give his inheritance to his father’s brothers.

units.leftText: If his father has no brothers, then you shall give his inheritance to his kinsman who is next to him of his family, and he shall possess it. This shall be a statute and ordinance for the children of Israel, as the LORD commanded Moses.’”
units.rightText: And if his father has no brothers, give his inheritance to the next of kin from his clan, that he may take possession of it. This is to be a statutory ordinance for the Israelites, as the LORD has commanded Moses.’” Moses Requests a Successor (Deuteronomy 3:23–29|DEU 3:23-29*)

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “Go up into this mountain of Abarim, and see the land which I have given to the children of Israel.
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go up this mountain of the Abarim range and see the land that I have given the Israelites.
rightNotes: 27:12 LXX Go up Mount Nebo beyond the Jordan

units.leftText: When you have seen it, you also shall be gathered to your people, as Aaron your brother was gathered;
units.rightText: After you have seen it, you too will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was;

units.leftText: because in the strife of the congregation, you rebelled against my word in the wilderness of Zin, to honor me as holy at the waters before their eyes.” (These are the waters of Meribah of Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.)
units.rightText: for when the congregation contended in the Wilderness of Zin, both of you rebelled against My command to show My holiness in their sight regarding the waters.” Those were the waters of Meribah in Kadesh, in the Wilderness of Zin.
rightNotes: 27:14 Meribah means quarreling; see Exodus 17:7|EXO 17:7*.

units.leftText: Moses spoke to the LORD, saying,
units.rightText: So Moses appealed to the LORD,

units.leftText: “Let the LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation,
units.rightText: “May the LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation

units.leftText: who may go out before them, and who may come in before them, and who may lead them out, and who may bring them in, that the congregation of the LORD may not be as sheep which have no shepherd.”
units.rightText: who will go out and come in before them, and who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the congregation of the LORD will not be like sheep without a shepherd.” Joshua to Succeed Moses (Deuteronomy 31:1–8|DEU 31:1-8*)

units.leftText: The LORD said to Moses, “Take Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the Spirit, and lay your hand on him.
units.rightText: And the LORD replied to Moses, “Take Joshua son of Nun, a man with the Spirit in him, and lay your hands on him.

units.leftText: Set him before Eleazar the priest, and before all the congregation; and commission him in their sight.
units.rightText: Have him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation, and commission him in their sight.

units.leftText: You shall give authority to him, that all the congregation of the children of Israel may obey.
units.rightText: Confer on him some of your authority, so that the whole congregation of Israel will obey him.

units.leftText: He shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall inquire for him by the judgment of the Urim before the LORD. At his word they shall go out, and at his word they shall come in, both he and all the children of Israel with him, even all the congregation.”
units.rightText: He shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who will seek counsel for him before the LORD by the judgment of the Urim. At his command, he and all the Israelites with him— the entire congregation— will go out and come in.”
rightNotes: 27:21 Literally the Lights

units.leftText: Moses did as the LORD commanded him. He took Joshua, and set him before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation.
units.rightText: Moses did as the LORD had commanded him. He took Joshua, had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation,

units.leftText: He laid his hands on him and commissioned him, as the LORD spoke by Moses.
units.rightText: and laid his hands on him and commissioned him, as the LORD had instructed through Moses.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Command the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘See that you present my offering, my food for my offerings made by fire, as a pleasant aroma to me, in their due season.’
units.rightText: “Command the Israelites and say to them: See that you present to Me at its appointed time the food for My food offerings, as a pleasing aroma to Me.

units.leftText: You shall tell them, ‘This is the offering made by fire which you shall offer to the LORD: male lambs a year old without defect, two day by day, for a continual burnt offering.
units.rightText: And tell them that this is the food offering you are to present to the LORD as a regular burnt offering each day: two unblemished year-old male lambs.

units.leftText: You shall offer the one lamb in the morning, and you shall offer the other lamb at evening,
units.rightText: Offer one lamb in the morning and the other at twilight,
rightNotes: 28:4 Hebrew between the two evenings; also in verse 8

units.leftText: with one tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a meal offering, mixed with the fourth part of a hin of beaten oil.
units.rightText: along with a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a grain offering, mixed with a quarter hin of oil from pressed olives.
leftNotes: 28:5 1 ephah is about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel
28:5 A hin is about 6.5 liters or 1.7 gallons.
rightNotes: 28:5 A tenth of an ephah is approximately 2 dry quarts or 2.2 liters (probably about 2.6 pounds or 1.2 kilograms of flour); also in verses 13, 21, and 29.
28:5 Or a quarter hin of pure olive oil; Hebrew a quarter hin of pressed oil; that is, approximately 0.97 quarts or 0.92 liters; similarly in verses 7 and 14

units.leftText: It is a continual burnt offering which was ordained in Mount Sinai for a pleasant aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
units.rightText: This is a regular burnt offering established at Mount Sinai as a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.

units.leftText: Its drink offering shall be the fourth part of a hin for each lamb. You shall pour out a drink offering of strong drink to the LORD in the holy place.
units.rightText: The drink offering accompanying each lamb shall be a quarter hin. Pour out the offering of fermented drink to the LORD in the sanctuary area.
leftNotes: 28:7 One hin is about 6.5 liters, so 1/4 hin is about 1.6 liters or 1.7 quarts.

units.leftText: The other lamb you shall offer at evening. As the meal offering of the morning, and as its drink offering, you shall offer it, an offering made by fire, for a pleasant aroma to the LORD.
units.rightText: And offer the second lamb at twilight, with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning. It is a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD. The Sabbath Offerings

units.leftText: “‘On the Sabbath day, you shall offer two male lambs a year old without defect, and two tenths of an ephah of fine flour for a meal offering mixed with oil, and its drink offering:
units.rightText: On the Sabbath day, present two unblemished year-old male lambs, accompanied by a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, as well as a drink offering.
leftNotes: 28:9 1 ephah is about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel
rightNotes: 28:9 Two-tenths of an ephah is approximately 4 dry quarts or 4.4 liters (probably about 5.1 pounds or 2.3 kilograms of flour); also in verses 12, 20, and 28.

units.leftText: this is the burnt offering of every Sabbath, in addition to the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.
units.rightText: This is the burnt offering for every Sabbath, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering. The Monthly Offerings

units.leftText: “‘In the beginnings of your months, you shall offer a burnt offering to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram, seven male lambs a year old without defect,
units.rightText: At the beginning of every month, you are to present to the LORD a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished,

units.leftText: and three tenths of an ephah of fine flour for a meal offering mixed with oil, for each bull; and two tenth parts of fine flour for a meal offering mixed with oil, for the one ram;
units.rightText: along with three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering with each bull, two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering with the ram,
leftNotes: 28:12 1 ephah is about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel
rightNotes: 28:12 Three-tenths of an ephah is approximately 6 dry quarts or 6.6 liters (probably about 7.6 pounds or 3.5 kilograms of flour); also in verses 20 and 28.

units.leftText: and one tenth part of fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering to every lamb, as a burnt offering of a pleasant aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
units.rightText: and a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering with each lamb. This is a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.

units.leftText: Their drink offerings shall be half a hin of wine for a bull, the third part of a hin for the ram, and the fourth part of a hin for a lamb. This is the burnt offering of every month throughout the months of the year.
units.rightText: Their drink offerings shall be half a hin of wine with each bull, a third of a hin with the ram, and a quarter hin with each lamb. This is the monthly burnt offering to be made at each new moon throughout the year.
rightNotes: 28:14 Half a hin is approximately 1.9 quarts or 1.8 liters of wine.
28:14 A third of a hin is approximately 1.3 quarts or 1.2 liters of wine.

units.leftText: Also, one male goat for a sin offering to the LORD shall be offered in addition to the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.
units.rightText: In addition to the regular burnt offering with its drink offering, one male goat is to be presented to the LORD as a sin offering. Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread (Exodus 12:14–28|EXO 12:14-28*; Leviticus 23:4–8|LEV 23:4-8*; Deuteronomy 16:1–8|DEU 16:1-8*)

units.leftText: “‘In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, is the LORD’s Passover.
units.rightText: The fourteenth day of the first month is the LORD’s Passover.

units.leftText: On the fifteenth day of this month shall be a feast. Unleavened bread shall be eaten for seven days.
units.rightText: On the fifteenth day of this month, there shall be a feast; for seven days unleavened bread is to be eaten.

units.leftText: In the first day shall be a holy convocation. You shall do no regular work,
units.rightText: On the first day there is to be a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work.

units.leftText: but you shall offer an offering made by fire, a burnt offering to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old. They shall be without defect,
units.rightText: Present to the LORD a food offering, a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished.

units.leftText: with their meal offering, fine flour mixed with oil. You shall offer three tenths for a bull, and two tenths for the ram.
units.rightText: The grain offering shall consist of fine flour mixed with oil; offer three-tenths of an ephah with each bull, two-tenths of an ephah with the ram,

units.leftText: You shall offer one tenth for every lamb of the seven lambs;
units.rightText: and a tenth of an ephah with each of the seven lambs.

units.leftText: and one male goat for a sin offering, to make atonement for you.
units.rightText: Include one male goat as a sin offering to make atonement for you.

units.leftText: You shall offer these in addition to the burnt offering of the morning, which is for a continual burnt offering.
units.rightText: You are to present these in addition to the regular morning burnt offering.

units.leftText: In this way you shall offer daily, for seven days, the food of the offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to the LORD. It shall be offered in addition to the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.
units.rightText: Offer the same food each day for seven days as a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD. It is to be offered with its drink offering and the regular burnt offering.

units.leftText: On the seventh day you shall have a holy convocation. You shall do no regular work.
units.rightText: On the seventh day you shall hold a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work. The Feast of Weeks (Deuteronomy 16:9–12|DEU 16:9-12*)

units.leftText: “‘Also in the day of the first fruits, when you offer a new meal offering to the LORD in your feast of weeks, you shall have a holy convocation. You shall do no regular work;
units.rightText: On the day of firstfruits, when you present an offering of new grain to the LORD during the Feast of Weeks, you are to hold a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work.
rightNotes: 28:26 That is, Shavuot, the late spring feast of pilgrimage to Jerusalem; it is also known as the Feast of Harvest(see Exodus 23:16|EXO 23:16*) or the Feast of Pentecost(see Acts 2:1|ACT 2:1*).

units.leftText: but you shall offer a burnt offering for a pleasant aroma to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram, seven male lambs a year old;
units.rightText: Present a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old as a pleasing aroma to the LORD,

units.leftText: and their meal offering, fine flour mixed with oil, three tenths for each bull, two tenths for the one ram,
units.rightText: together with their grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil— three-tenths of an ephah with each bull, two-tenths of an ephah with the ram,

units.leftText: one tenth for every lamb of the seven lambs;
units.rightText: and a tenth of an ephah with each of the seven lambs.

units.leftText: and one male goat, to make atonement for you.
units.rightText: Include one male goat to make atonement for you.

units.leftText: Besides the continual burnt offering and its meal offering, you shall offer them and their drink offerings. See that they are without defect.
units.rightText: Offer them with their drink offerings in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain offering. The animals must be unblemished.[’’]

units.leftText: “‘In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall have a holy convocation; you shall do no regular work. It is a day of blowing of trumpets to you.
units.rightText: “On the first day of the seventh month, you are to hold a sacred assembly, and you must not do any regular work. This will be a day for you to sound the trumpets.

units.leftText: You shall offer a burnt offering for a pleasant aroma to the LORD: one young bull, one ram, seven male lambs a year old without defect;
units.rightText: As a pleasing aroma to the LORD, you are to present a burnt offering of one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished,

units.leftText: and their meal offering, fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for the bull, two tenths for the ram,
units.rightText: together with their grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil— three-tenths of an ephah with the bull, two-tenths of an ephah with the ram,
rightNotes: 29:3 Three-tenths of an ephah is approximately 6 dry quarts or 6.6 liters (probably about 7.6 pounds or 3.5 kilograms of flour); also in verses 9 and 14.
29:3 Two-tenths of an ephah is approximately 4 dry quarts or 4.4 liters (probably about 5.1 pounds or 2.3 kilograms of flour); also in verses 9 and 14.

units.leftText: and one tenth for every lamb of the seven lambs;
units.rightText: and a tenth of an ephah with each of the seven male lambs.
rightNotes: 29:4 A tenth of an ephah is approximately 2 dry quarts or 2.2 liters (probably about 2.6 pounds or 1.2 kilograms of flour); also in verses 10 and 15.

units.leftText: and one male goat for a sin offering, to make atonement for you;
units.rightText: Include one male goat as a sin offering to make atonement for you.

units.leftText: in addition to the burnt offering of the new moon with its meal offering, and the continual burnt offering with its meal offering, and their drink offerings, according to their ordinance, for a pleasant aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
units.rightText: These are in addition to the monthly and daily burnt offerings with their prescribed grain offerings and drink offerings. They are a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD. The Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:1–34|LEV 16:1-34*; Leviticus 23:26–32|LEV 23:26-32*)

units.leftText: “‘On the tenth day of this seventh month you shall have a holy convocation. You shall afflict your souls. You shall do no kind of work;
units.rightText: On the tenth day of this seventh month, you are to hold a sacred assembly, and you shall humble yourselves; you must not do any work.
rightNotes: 29:7 Or afflict your souls or deny yourselves

units.leftText: but you shall offer a burnt offering to the LORD for a pleasant aroma: one young bull, one ram, seven male lambs a year old, all without defect;
units.rightText: Present as a pleasing aroma to the LORD a burnt offering of one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished,

units.leftText: and their meal offering, fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for the bull, two tenths for the one ram,
units.rightText: together with their grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil— three-tenths of an ephah with the bull, two-tenths of an ephah with the ram,

units.leftText: one tenth for every lamb of the seven lambs;
units.rightText: and a tenth of an ephah with each of the seven lambs.

units.leftText: one male goat for a sin offering, in addition to the sin offering of atonement, and the continual burnt offering, and its meal offering, and their drink offerings.
units.rightText: Include one male goat for a sin offering, in addition to the sin offering of atonement and the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offerings. The Feast of Tabernacles (Deuteronomy 16:13–17|DEU 16:13-17*)

units.leftText: “‘On the fifteenth day of the seventh month you shall have a holy convocation. You shall do no regular work. You shall keep a feast to the LORD seven days.
units.rightText: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, you are to hold a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work, and you shall observe a feast to the LORD for seven days.

units.leftText: You shall offer a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to the LORD: thirteen young bulls, two rams, fourteen male lambs a year old, all without defect;
units.rightText: As a pleasing aroma to the LORD, you are to present a food offering, a burnt offering of thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,

units.leftText: and their meal offering, fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for every bull of the thirteen bulls, two tenths for each ram of the two rams,
units.rightText: along with the grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil with each of the thirteen bulls, two-tenths of an ephah with each of the two rams,

units.leftText: and one tenth for every lamb of the fourteen lambs;
units.rightText: and a tenth of an ephah with each of the fourteen lambs.

units.leftText: and one male goat for a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering, its meal offering, and its drink offering.
units.rightText: Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

units.leftText: “‘On the second day you shall offer twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old without defect;
units.rightText: On the second day you are to present twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,

units.leftText: and their meal offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, after the ordinance;
units.rightText: along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.

units.leftText: and one male goat for a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering, with its meal offering and their drink offerings.
units.rightText: Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

units.leftText: “‘On the third day: eleven bulls, two rams, fourteen male lambs a year old without defect;
units.rightText: On the third day you are to present eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,

units.leftText: and their meal offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, after the ordinance;
units.rightText: along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.

units.leftText: and one male goat for a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering, and its meal offering, and its drink offering.
units.rightText: Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

units.leftText: “‘On the fourth day ten bulls, two rams, fourteen male lambs a year old without defect;
units.rightText: On the fourth day you are to present ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,

units.leftText: their meal offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, after the ordinance;
units.rightText: along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.

units.leftText: and one male goat for a sin offering; in addition to the continual burnt offering, its meal offering, and its drink offering.
units.rightText: Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

units.leftText: “‘On the fifth day: nine bulls, two rams, fourteen male lambs a year old without defect;
units.rightText: On the fifth day you are to present nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,

units.leftText: and their meal offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, after the ordinance,
units.rightText: along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.

units.leftText: and one male goat for a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering, and its meal offering, and its drink offering.
units.rightText: Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

units.leftText: “‘On the sixth day: eight bulls, two rams, fourteen male lambs a year old without defect;
units.rightText: On the sixth day you are to present eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,

units.leftText: and their meal offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, after the ordinance,
units.rightText: along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.

units.leftText: and one male goat for a sin offering; in addition to the continual burnt offering, its meal offering, and the drink offerings of it.
units.rightText: Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

units.leftText: “‘On the seventh day: seven bulls, two rams, fourteen male lambs a year old without defect;
units.rightText: On the seventh day you are to present seven bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,

units.leftText: and their meal offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, according to their number, after the ordinance,
units.rightText: along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.

units.leftText: and one male goat for a sin offering; in addition to the continual burnt offering, its meal offering, and its drink offering.
units.rightText: Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

units.leftText: “‘On the eighth day you shall have a solemn assembly. You shall do no regular work;
units.rightText: On the eighth day you are to hold a solemn assembly; you must not do any regular work.

units.leftText: but you shall offer a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a pleasant aroma to the LORD: one bull, one ram, seven male lambs a year old without defect;
units.rightText: As a pleasing aroma to the LORD, you are to present a food offering, a burnt offering of one bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished,

units.leftText: their meal offering and their drink offerings for the bull, for the ram, and for the lambs, shall be according to their number, after the ordinance,
units.rightText: along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.

units.leftText: and one male goat for a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering, with its meal offering, and its drink offering.
units.rightText: Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

units.leftText: “‘You shall offer these to the LORD in your set feasts—in addition to your vows and your free will offerings—for your burnt offerings, your meal offerings, your drink offerings, and your peace offerings.’”
units.rightText: You are to present these offerings to the LORD at your appointed times, in addition to your vow and freewill offerings, whether burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings, or peace offerings.”

units.leftText: Moses told the children of Israel according to all that the LORD commanded Moses.
units.rightText: So Moses spoke all this to the Israelites just as the LORD had commanded him.

units.leftText: Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes of the children of Israel, saying, “This is the thing which the LORD has commanded.
units.rightText: Then Moses said to the heads of the tribes of Israel, “This is what the LORD has commanded:

units.leftText: When a man vows a vow to the LORD, or swears an oath to bind his soul with a bond, he shall not break his word. He shall do according to all that proceeds out of his mouth.
units.rightText: If a man makes a vow to the LORD or swears an oath to obligate himself by a pledge, he must not break his word; he must do everything he has promised.
rightNotes: 30:2 Cited in Matthew 5:33|MAT 5:33*

units.leftText: “Also, when a woman vows a vow to the LORD and binds herself by a pledge, being in her father’s house, in her youth,
units.rightText: And if a woman in her father’s house during her youth makes a vow to the LORD or obligates herself by a pledge,

units.leftText: and her father hears her vow and her pledge with which she has bound her soul, and her father says nothing to her, then all her vows shall stand, and every pledge with which she has bound her soul shall stand.
units.rightText: and her father hears about her vow or pledge but says nothing to her, then all the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand.

units.leftText: But if her father forbids her in the day that he hears, none of her vows or of her pledges with which she has bound her soul, shall stand. The LORD will forgive her, because her father has forbidden her.
units.rightText: But if her father prohibits her on the day he hears about it, then none of the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand. The LORD will absolve her because her father has prohibited her.

units.leftText: “If she has a husband, while her vows are on her, or the rash utterance of her lips with which she has bound her soul,
units.rightText: If a woman marries while under a vow or rash promise by which she has bound herself,

units.leftText: and her husband hears it, and says nothing to her in the day that he hears it; then her vows shall stand, and her pledges with which she has bound her soul shall stand.
units.rightText: and her husband hears of it but says nothing to her on that day, then the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand.

units.leftText: But if her husband forbids her in the day that he hears it, then he makes void her vow which is on her and the rash utterance of her lips, with which she has bound her soul. The LORD will forgive her.
units.rightText: But if her husband prohibits her when he hears of it, he nullifies the vow that binds her or the rash promise she has made, and the LORD will absolve her.

units.leftText: “But the vow of a widow, or of her who is divorced, everything with which she has bound her soul shall stand against her.
units.rightText: Every vow a widow or divorced woman pledges to fulfill is binding on her.

units.leftText: “If she vowed in her husband’s house or bound her soul by a bond with an oath,
units.rightText: If a woman in her husband’s house has made a vow or put herself under an obligation with an oath,

units.leftText: and her husband heard it, and held his peace at her and didn’t disallow her, then all her vows shall stand, and every pledge with which she bound her soul shall stand.
units.rightText: and her husband hears of it but says nothing to her and does not prohibit her, then all the vows or pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand.

units.leftText: But if her husband made them null and void in the day that he heard them, then whatever proceeded out of her lips concerning her vows, or concerning the bond of her soul, shall not stand. Her husband has made them void. The LORD will forgive her.
units.rightText: But if her husband nullifies them on the day he hears of them, then nothing that came from her lips, whether her vows or pledges, shall stand. Her husband has nullified them, and the LORD will absolve her.

units.leftText: Every vow, and every binding oath to afflict the soul, her husband may establish it, or her husband may make it void.
units.rightText: Her husband may confirm or nullify any vow or any sworn pledge to deny herself.
rightNotes: 30:13 Or to fast

units.leftText: But if her husband says nothing to her from day to day, then he establishes all her vows or all her pledges which are on her. He has established them, because he said nothing to her in the day that he heard them.
units.rightText: But if her husband says nothing to her from day to day, then he confirms all the vows and pledges that bind her. He has confirmed them, because he said nothing to her on the day he heard about them.

units.leftText: But if he makes them null and void after he has heard them, then he shall bear her iniquity.”
units.rightText: But if he nullifies them after he hears of them, then he will bear her iniquity.”

units.leftText: These are the statutes which the LORD commanded Moses, between a man and his wife, between a father and his daughter, being in her youth, in her father’s house.
units.rightText: These are the statutes that the LORD commanded Moses concerning the relationship between a man and his wife, and between a father and a young daughter still in his home.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: And the LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Avenge the children of Israel on the Midianites. Afterward you shall be gathered to your people.”
units.rightText: “Take vengeance on the Midianites for the Israelites. After that, you will be gathered to your people.”

units.leftText: Moses spoke to the people, saying, “Arm men from among you for war, that they may go against Midian, to execute the LORD’s vengeance on Midian.
units.rightText: So Moses told the people, “Arm some of your men for war, that they may go against the Midianites and execute the LORD’s vengeance on them.

units.leftText: You shall send one thousand out of every tribe, throughout all the tribes of Israel, to the war.”
units.rightText: Send into battle a thousand men from each tribe of Israel.”

units.leftText: So there were delivered, out of the thousands of Israel, a thousand from every tribe, twelve thousand armed for war.
units.rightText: So a thousand men were recruited from each tribe of Israel— twelve thousand armed for war.

units.leftText: Moses sent them, one thousand of every tribe, to the war with Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, to the war, with the vessels of the sanctuary and the trumpets for the alarm in his hand.
units.rightText: And Moses sent the thousand from each tribe into battle, along with Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, who took with him the vessels of the sanctuary and the trumpets for signaling.

units.leftText: They fought against Midian, as the LORD commanded Moses. They killed every male.
units.rightText: Then they waged war against Midian, as the LORD had commanded Moses, and they killed every male.

units.leftText: They killed the kings of Midian with the rest of their slain: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam the son of Beor with the sword.
units.rightText: Among the slain were Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba— the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword.

units.leftText: The children of Israel took the women of Midian captive with their little ones; and all their livestock, all their flocks, and all their goods, they took as plunder.
units.rightText: The Israelites captured the Midianite women and their children, and they plundered all their herds, flocks, and goods.

units.leftText: All their cities in the places in which they lived, and all their encampments, they burned with fire.
units.rightText: Then they burned all the cities where the Midianites had lived, as well as all their encampments,

units.leftText: They took all the captives, and all the plunder, both of man and of animal.
units.rightText: and carried away all the plunder and spoils, both people and animals.

units.leftText: They brought the captives with the prey and the plunder, to Moses, and to Eleazar the priest, and to the congregation of the children of Israel, to the camp at the plains of Moab, which are by the Jordan at Jericho.
units.rightText: They brought the captives, spoils, and plunder to Moses, to Eleazar the priest, and to the congregation of Israel at the camp on the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho.

units.leftText: Moses and Eleazar the priest, with all the princes of the congregation, went out to meet them outside of the camp.
units.rightText: And Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the congregation went to meet them outside the camp.

units.leftText: Moses was angry with the officers of the army, the captains of thousands and the captains of hundreds, who came from the service of the war.
units.rightText: But Moses was angry with the officers of the army — the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds — who were returning from the battle.

units.leftText: Moses said to them, “Have you saved all the women alive?
units.rightText: “Have you spared all the women?” he asked them.

units.leftText: Behold, these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the LORD in the matter of Peor, and so the plague was among the congregation of the LORD.
units.rightText: “Look, these women caused the sons of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to turn unfaithfully against the LORD at Peor, so that the plague struck the congregation of the LORD.

units.leftText: Now therefore kill every male among the little ones, and kill every woman who has known man by lying with him.
units.rightText: So now, kill all the boys, as well as every woman who has had relations with a man,

units.leftText: But all the girls, who have not known man by lying with him, keep alive for yourselves.
units.rightText: but spare for yourselves every girl who has never had relations with a man.

units.leftText: “Encamp outside of the camp for seven days. Whoever has killed any person, and whoever has touched any slain, purify yourselves on the third day and on the seventh day, you and your captives.
units.rightText: All of you who have killed a person or touched the dead are to remain outside the camp for seven days. On the third day and the seventh day you are to purify both yourselves and your captives.

units.leftText: You shall purify every garment, and all that is made of skin, and all work of goats’ hair, and all things made of wood.”
units.rightText: And purify every garment and leather good, everything made of goat’s hair, and every article of wood.”

units.leftText: Eleazar the priest said to the men of war who went to the battle, “This is the statute of the law which the LORD has commanded Moses.
units.rightText: Then Eleazar the priest said to the soldiers who had gone into battle, “This is the statute of the law which the LORD has commanded Moses:

units.leftText: However the gold, and the silver, the bronze, the iron, the tin, and the lead,
units.rightText: Only the gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, and lead—

units.leftText: everything that may withstand the fire, you shall make to go through the fire, and it shall be clean; nevertheless it shall be purified with the water for impurity. All that doesn’t withstand the fire you shall make to go through the water.
units.rightText: everything that can withstand the fire— must be put through the fire, and it will be clean. But it must still be purified with the water of purification. And everything that cannot withstand the fire must pass through the water.

units.leftText: You shall wash your clothes on the seventh day, and you shall be clean. Afterward you shall come into the camp.”
units.rightText: On the seventh day you are to wash your clothes, and you will be clean. After that you may enter the camp.” Division of the Spoils

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.rightText: The LORD said to Moses,

units.leftText: “Count the plunder that was taken, both of man and of animal, you, and Eleazar the priest, and the heads of the fathers’ households of the congregation;
units.rightText: “You and Eleazar the priest and the family heads of the congregation are to take a count of what was captured, both of man and beast.

units.leftText: and divide the plunder into two parts: between the men skilled in war, who went out to battle, and all the congregation.
units.rightText: Then divide the captives between the troops who went out to battle and the rest of the congregation.

units.leftText: Levy a tribute to the LORD of the men of war who went out to battle: one soul of five hundred; of the persons, of the cattle, of the donkeys, and of the flocks.
units.rightText: Set aside a tribute for the LORD from what belongs to the soldiers who went into battle: one out of every five hundred, whether persons, cattle, donkeys, or sheep.

units.leftText: Take it from their half, and give it to Eleazar the priest, for the LORD’s wave offering.
units.rightText: Take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as an offering to the LORD.

units.leftText: Of the children of Israel’s half, you shall take one drawn out of every fifty, of the persons, of the cattle, of the donkeys, and of the flocks, of all the livestock, and give them to the Levites, who perform the duty of the LORD’s tabernacle.”
units.rightText: From the Israelites’ half, take one out of every fifty, whether persons, cattle, donkeys, sheep, or other animals, and give them to the Levites who keep charge of the tabernacle of the LORD.”

units.leftText: Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the LORD commanded Moses.
units.rightText: So Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the LORD had commanded Moses,

units.leftText: Now the plunder, over and above the booty which the men of war took, was six hundred seventy-five thousand sheep,
units.rightText: and this plunder remained from the spoils the soldiers had taken: 675,000 sheep,

units.leftText: seventy-two thousand head of cattle,
units.rightText: 72,000 cattle,

units.leftText: sixty-one thousand donkeys,
units.rightText: 61,000 donkeys,

units.leftText: and thirty-two thousand persons in all, of the women who had not known man by lying with him.
units.rightText: and 32,000 women who had not slept with a man.

units.leftText: The half, which was the portion of those who went out to war, was in number three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep;
units.rightText: This was the half portion for those who had gone to war:

units.leftText: and the LORD’s tribute of the sheep was six hundred seventy-five.
units.rightText: including a tribute to the LORD of 675,

units.leftText: The cattle were thirty-six thousand, of which the LORD’s tribute was seventy-two.
units.rightText: 36,000 cattle, including a tribute to the LORD of 72,

units.leftText: The donkeys were thirty thousand five hundred, of which the LORD’s tribute was sixty-one.
units.rightText: 30,500 donkeys, including a tribute to the LORD of 61,

units.leftText: The persons were sixteen thousand, of whom the LORD’s tribute was thirty-two persons.
units.rightText: and 16,000 people, including a tribute to the LORD of 32.

units.leftText: Moses gave the tribute, which was the LORD’s wave offering, to Eleazar the priest, as the LORD commanded Moses.
units.rightText: Moses gave the tribute to Eleazar the priest as an offering for the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

units.leftText: Of the children of Israel’s half, which Moses divided off from the men who fought
units.rightText: From the Israelites’ half, which Moses had set apart from the men who had gone to war,

units.leftText: (now the congregation’s half was three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep,
units.rightText: this half belonged to the congregation: 337,500 sheep,

units.leftText: thirty-six thousand head of cattle,
units.rightText: 36,000 cattle,

units.leftText: thirty thousand five hundred donkeys,
units.rightText: 30,500 donkeys,

units.leftText: and sixteen thousand persons),
units.rightText: and 16,000 people.

units.leftText: even of the children of Israel’s half, Moses took one drawn out of every fifty, both of man and of animal, and gave them to the Levites, who performed the duty of the LORD’s tabernacle, as the LORD commanded Moses.
units.rightText: From the Israelites’ half, Moses took one out of every fifty persons and animals and gave them to the Levites who kept charge of the tabernacle of the LORD, as the LORD had commanded him. The Voluntary Offering

units.leftText: The officers who were over the thousands of the army, the captains of thousands, and the captains of hundreds, came near to Moses.
units.rightText: Then the officers who were over the units of the army — the commanders of thousands and of hundreds — approached Moses

units.leftText: They said to Moses, “Your servants have taken the sum of the men of war who are under our command, and there lacks not one man of us.
units.rightText: and said, “Your servants have counted the soldiers under our command, and not one of us is missing.

units.leftText: We have brought the LORD’s offering, what every man found: gold ornaments, armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and necklaces, to make atonement for our souls before the LORD.”
units.rightText: So we have brought to the LORD an offering of the gold articles each man acquired— armlets, bracelets, rings, earrings, and necklaces— to make atonement for ourselves before the LORD.”

units.leftText: Moses and Eleazar the priest took their gold, even all worked jewels.
units.rightText: So Moses and Eleazar the priest received from them all the articles made out of gold.

units.leftText: All the gold of the wave offering that they offered up to the LORD, of the captains of thousands, and of the captains of hundreds, was sixteen thousand seven hundred fifty shekels.
units.rightText: All the gold that the commanders of thousands and of hundreds presented as an offering to the LORD weighed 16,750 shekels.
leftNotes: 31:52 A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces, so 16,750 shekels is about 167.5 kilograms or about 368.5 pounds.
rightNotes: 31:52 16,750 shekels is approximately 420.8 pounds or 190.9 kilograms.

units.leftText: The men of war had taken booty, every man for himself.
units.rightText: Each of the soldiers had taken plunder for himself.

units.leftText: Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold of the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and brought it into the Tent of Meeting for a memorial for the children of Israel before the LORD.
units.rightText: And Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from the commanders of thousands and of hundreds and brought it into the Tent of Meeting as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD.

units.leftText: Now the children of Reuben and the children of Gad had a very great multitude of livestock. They saw the land of Jazer, and the land of Gilead. Behold, the place was a place for livestock.
units.rightText: Now the Reubenites and Gadites, who had very large herds and flocks, surveyed the lands of Jazer and Gilead, and they saw that the region was suitable for livestock.

units.leftText: Then the children of Gad and the children of Reuben came and spoke to Moses, and to Eleazar the priest, and to the princes of the congregation, saying,
units.rightText: So the Gadites and Reubenites came to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the congregation, and said,

units.leftText: “Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon,
units.rightText: “Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon,
rightNotes: 32:3 Hebrew; see verse 38, and similarly in SP and LXX Sibmah

units.leftText: the land which the LORD struck before the congregation of Israel, is a land for livestock; and your servants have livestock.”
units.rightText: which the LORD conquered before the congregation of Israel, are suitable for livestock — and your servants have livestock.”

units.leftText: They said, “If we have found favor in your sight, let this land be given to your servants for a possession. Don’t bring us over the Jordan.”
units.rightText: “If we have found favor in your sight,” they said, “let this land be given to your servants as a possession. Do not make us cross the Jordan.”

units.leftText: Moses said to the children of Gad, and to the children of Reuben, “Shall your brothers go to war while you sit here?
units.rightText: But Moses asked the Gadites and Reubenites, “Shall your brothers go to war while you sit here?

units.leftText: Why do you discourage the heart of the children of Israel from going over into the land which the LORD has given them?
units.rightText: Why are you discouraging the Israelites from crossing into the land that the LORD has given them?

units.leftText: Your fathers did so when I sent them from Kadesh Barnea to see the land.
units.rightText: This is what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to inspect the land.

units.leftText: For when they went up to the valley of Eshcol, and saw the land, they discouraged the heart of the children of Israel, that they should not go into the land which the LORD had given them.
units.rightText: For when your fathers went up to the Valley of Eshcol and saw the land, they discouraged the Israelites from entering the land that the LORD had given them.

units.leftText: The LORD’s anger burned in that day, and he swore, saying,
units.rightText: So the anger of the LORD was kindled that day, and He swore an oath, saying,

units.leftText: ‘Surely none of the men who came up out of Egypt, from twenty years old and upward, shall see the land which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; because they have not wholly followed me,
units.rightText: ‘Because they did not follow Me wholeheartedly, not one of the men twenty years of age or older who came out of Egypt will see the land that I swore to give Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—

units.leftText: except Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, and Joshua the son of Nun, because they have followed the LORD completely.’
units.rightText: not one except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun— because they did follow the LORD wholeheartedly.’

units.leftText: The LORD’s anger burned against Israel, and he made them wander back and forth in the wilderness forty years, until all the generation who had done evil in the LORD’s sight was consumed.
units.rightText: The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He made them wander in the wilderness forty years, until the whole generation who had done evil in His sight was gone.

units.leftText: “Behold, you have risen up in your fathers’ place, an increase of sinful men, to increase the fierce anger of the LORD toward Israel.
units.rightText: Now behold, you, a brood of sinners, have risen up in place of your fathers to further stoke the burning anger of the LORD against Israel.

units.leftText: For if you turn away from after him, he will yet again leave them in the wilderness; and you will destroy all these people.”
units.rightText: For if you turn away from following Him, He will once again leave this people in the wilderness, and you will be the cause of their destruction.”

units.leftText: They came near to him, and said, “We will build sheepfolds here for our livestock, and cities for our little ones;
units.rightText: Then the Gadites and Reubenites approached Moses and said, “We want to build sheepfolds here for our livestock and cities for our little ones.

units.leftText: but we ourselves will be ready armed to go before the children of Israel, until we have brought them to their place. Our little ones shall dwell in the fortified cities because of the inhabitants of the land.
units.rightText: But we will arm ourselves and be ready to go ahead of the Israelites until we have brought them into their place. Meanwhile, our little ones will remain in the fortified cities for protection from the inhabitants of the land.
rightNotes: 32:17 LXX we will arm ourselves for battle

units.leftText: We will not return to our houses until the children of Israel have all received their inheritance.
units.rightText: We will not return to our homes until every Israelite has taken possession of his inheritance.

units.leftText: For we will not inherit with them on the other side of the Jordan and beyond, because our inheritance has come to us on this side of the Jordan eastward.”
units.rightText: Yet we will not have an inheritance with them across the Jordan and beyond, because our inheritance has come to us on the east side of the Jordan.”

units.leftText: Moses said to them: “If you will do this thing, if you will arm yourselves to go before the LORD to the war,
units.rightText: Moses replied, “If you will do this— if you will arm yourselves before the LORD for battle,

units.leftText: and every one of your armed men will pass over the Jordan before the LORD until he has driven out his enemies from before him,
units.rightText: and if every one of your armed men crosses the Jordan before the LORD, until He has driven His enemies out before Him,

units.leftText: and the land is subdued before the LORD; then afterward you shall return, and be clear of obligation to the LORD and to Israel. Then this land shall be your possession before the LORD.
units.rightText: then when the land is subdued before the LORD, you may return and be free of obligation to the LORD and to Israel. And this land will belong to you as a possession before the LORD.

units.leftText: “But if you will not do so, behold, you have sinned against the LORD; and be sure your sin will find you out.
units.rightText: But if you do not do this, you will certainly sin against the LORD — and be assured that your sin will find you out.

units.leftText: Build cities for your little ones, and folds for your sheep; and do that which has proceeded out of your mouth.”
units.rightText: Build cities for your little ones and folds for your flocks, but do what you have promised.”

units.leftText: The children of Gad and the children of Reuben spoke to Moses, saying, “Your servants will do as my lord commands.
units.rightText: The Gadites and Reubenites said to Moses, “Your servants will do just as our lord commands.

units.leftText: Our little ones, our wives, our flocks, and all our livestock shall be there in the cities of Gilead;
units.rightText: Our children, our wives, our livestock, and all our animals will remain here in the cities of Gilead.

units.leftText: but your servants will pass over, every man who is armed for war, before the LORD to battle, as my lord says.”
units.rightText: But your servants are equipped for war, and every man will cross over to the battle before the LORD, just as our lord says.”

units.leftText: So Moses commanded concerning them to Eleazar the priest, and to Joshua the son of Nun, and to the heads of the fathers’ households of the tribes of the children of Israel.
units.rightText: So Moses gave orders about them to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun, and to the family leaders of the tribes of Israel.

units.leftText: Moses said to them, “If the children of Gad and the children of Reuben will pass with you over the Jordan, every man who is armed to battle before the LORD, and the land is subdued before you, then you shall give them the land of Gilead for a possession;
units.rightText: And Moses said to them, “If the Gadites and Reubenites cross the Jordan with you, with every man armed for battle before the LORD, and the land is subdued before you, then you are to give them the land of Gilead as a possession.

units.leftText: but if they will not pass over with you armed, they shall have possessions among you in the land of Canaan.”
units.rightText: But if they do not arm themselves and go across with you, then they must accept their possession among you in the land of Canaan.”

units.leftText: The children of Gad and the children of Reuben answered, saying, “As the LORD has said to your servants, so will we do.
units.rightText: The Gadites and Reubenites replied, “As the LORD has spoken to your servants, so we will do.

units.leftText: We will pass over armed before the LORD into the land of Canaan, and the possession of our inheritance shall remain with us beyond the Jordan.”
units.rightText: We will cross over into the land of Canaan armed before the LORD, that we may have our inheritance on this side of the Jordan.”

units.leftText: Moses gave to them, even to the children of Gad, and to the children of Reuben, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh the son of Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan; the land, according to its cities and borders, even the cities of the surrounding land.
units.rightText: So Moses gave to the Gadites, to the Reubenites, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan — the land including its cities and the territory surrounding them.

units.leftText: The children of Gad built Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
units.rightText: And the Gadites built up Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,

units.leftText: Atroth-shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah,
units.rightText: Atroth-shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah,

units.leftText: Beth Nimrah, and Beth Haran: fortified cities and folds for sheep.
units.rightText: Beth-nimrah, and Beth-haran as fortified cities, and they built folds for their flocks.

units.leftText: The children of Reuben built Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,
units.rightText: The Reubenites built up Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,

units.leftText: Nebo, and Baal Meon, (their names being changed), and Sibmah. They gave other names to the cities which they built.
units.rightText: as well as Nebo and Baal-meon (whose names were changed), and Sibmah. And they renamed the cities they rebuilt.

units.leftText: The children of Machir the son of Manasseh went to Gilead, took it, and dispossessed the Amorites who were therein.
units.rightText: The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead, captured it, and drove out the Amorites who were there.

units.leftText: Moses gave Gilead to Machir the son of Manasseh; and he lived therein.
units.rightText: So Moses gave Gilead to the clan of Machir son of Manasseh, and they settled there.

units.leftText: Jair the son of Manasseh went and took its villages, and called them Havvoth Jair.
units.rightText: Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, went and captured their villages and called them Havvoth-jair.
rightNotes: 32:41 Havvoth-jair means the villages of Jair.

units.leftText: Nobah went and took Kenath and its villages, and called it Nobah, after his own name.
units.rightText: And Nobah went and captured Kenath and its villages and called it Nobah, after his own name.

units.leftText: These are the journeys of the children of Israel, when they went out of the land of Egypt by their armies under the hand of Moses and Aaron.
units.rightText: These are the journeys of the Israelites when they came out of the land of Egypt by their divisions under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.

units.leftText: Moses wrote the starting points of their journeys by the commandment of the LORD. These are their journeys according to their starting points.
units.rightText: At the LORD’s command, Moses recorded the stages of their journey. These are the stages listed by their starting points:

units.leftText: They traveled from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the next day after the Passover, the children of Israel went out with a high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians,
units.rightText: On the fifteenth day of the first month, on the day after the Passover, the Israelites set out from Rameses. They marched out defiantly in full view of all the Egyptians,
rightNotes: 33:3 Or marched out boldly; literally marched out with an upraised hand

units.leftText: while the Egyptians were burying all their firstborn, whom the LORD had struck among them. The LORD also executed judgments on their gods.
units.rightText: who were burying all their firstborn, whom the LORD had struck down among them; for the LORD had executed judgment against their gods.

units.leftText: The children of Israel traveled from Rameses, and encamped in Succoth.
units.rightText: The Israelites set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.

units.leftText: They traveled from Succoth, and encamped in Etham, which is in the edge of the wilderness.
units.rightText: They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.

units.leftText: They traveled from Etham, and turned back to Pihahiroth, which is before Baal Zephon, and they encamped before Migdol.
units.rightText: They set out from Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon, and they camped near Migdol.

units.leftText: They traveled from before Hahiroth, and crossed through the middle of the sea into the wilderness. They went three days’ journey in the wilderness of Etham, and encamped in Marah.
units.rightText: They set out from Pi-hahiroth and crossed through the sea, into the wilderness, and they journeyed three days into the Wilderness of Etham and camped at Marah.
